      1 +# ARD-001: Markdown Viewer Pro Integration
      2 +
      3 +**Status**: Approved
      4 +**Date**: 2024-12-22
      5 +**Author**: AntiGravity, Cline (Principal SDE Review)
      6 +**Decision**: Integrate `markdown-viewer-app` as internal library for all rendering
      7 +
      8 +---
      9 +
     10 +## 1. Context
     11 +
     12 +### Problem Statement
     13 +Coach Atlas requires rich markdown rendering across multiple views:
     14 +1. **Chat Interface** - AI responses with code, diagrams, math
     15 +2. **Tutorial View** - Full-screen structured content
     16 +3. **Interview Mode** - Interactive problems with hints
     17 +
     18 +### Detailed Implementation Plan
     19 +
     20 +### 1. Directory Structure Setup
     21 +We will establish a dedicated module for the markdown logic to keep it isolated from the main app logic.
     22 +
     23 +```
     24 +src/
     25 +└── lib/
     26 +    └── markdown-viewer/
     27 +        ├── index.ts              # Main export
     28 +        ├── MarkdownRenderer.tsx  # React Component Wrapper
     29 +        ├── core/
     30 +        │   ├── parser.ts         # Port of script.js (marked config)
     31 +        │   └── renderer.ts       # Port of marked renderer
     32 +        ├── services/
     33 +        │   ├── MermaidService.ts # Port of MermaidService.js
     34 +        │   └── PrismService.ts   # Port of PrismService.js
     35 +        ├── themes/
     36 +        │   ├── index.ts         # Theme loader
     37 +        │   └── files/           # CSS files (copied directly)
     38 +        └── utils/
     39 +            └── colorHelpers.ts   # Port of colorHelpers.js
     40 +```
     41 +
     42 +### 2. Component Logic (`MarkdownRenderer.tsx`)
     43 +This component will serve as the bridge between React and the Vanilla JS logic of the viewer.
     44 +*   **Props**: `content: string`, `theme?: string`
     45 +*   **Effect**:
     46 +    1.  Initialize `MermaidService` (lazy loaded).
     47 +    2.  Parse content using `marked` (configured with `markedFootnote` and custom extensions).
     48 +    3.  Sanitize using `DOMPurify`.
     49 +    4.  Render HTML to a `div`.
     50 +    5.  Post-process: trigger `Mermaid.render` on `.mermaid-diagram` class.
     51 +    6.  Post-process: trigger `Prism.highlightAll` on code blocks.
     52 +
     53 +### 3. Theme System
     54 +*   Themes will be imported as raw CSS strings (via Vite `?inline` or standard import) and injected into a `<style id="theme-style">` tag in the head.
     55 +*   `MermaidService` will continue to use `getCssVariable` to read the active theme colors for dynamic diagram styling.
     56 +
     57 +### 4. Dependencies
     58 +We need to install the exact versions used in the viewer to ensure compatibility:
     59 +*   `marked`
     60 +*   `marked-footnote`
     61 +*   `dompurify`
     62 +*   `mermaid`
     63 +*   `prismjs`
     64 +*   `katex`
     65 +
     66 +### 5. Why Not `react-markdown`?
     67 +The previous plan suggested `react-markdown`, but `markdown-viewer-app` uses `marked` directly with custom extensions (alerts, custom heading IDs for TOC). To achieve **100% parity**, we must use `marked` and port the exact extensions found in `script.js` (lines 562-846).
     68 +
     69 +## Action Items
     70 +1.  **Dependency Install**: `npm install marked marked-footnote dompurify mermaid prismjs katex`
     71 +2.  **Code Porting**:
     72 +    *   Copy `themes/*.css` -> `src/lib/markdown-viewer/themes/files/`
     73 +    *   Port `script.js` (Marked config) -> `src/lib/markdown-viewer/core/parser.ts`
     74 +    *   Port `MermaidService.js` -> `src/lib/markdown-viewer/services/MermaidService.ts`
     75 +3.  **Component Creation**: Build `<MarkdownRenderer />`.
     76 +
     77 +### Existing Asset
     78 +We have a production-ready markdown viewer at:
     79 +```
     80 +src/lib/external/markdown-viewer-app/
     81 +```
     82 +
     83 +**Features Available:**
     84 +- ✅ 15 professional themes (dark/light variants)
     85 +- ✅ PrismJS syntax highlighting (20+ languages)
     86 +- ✅ Mermaid diagrams (flowcharts, sequences, etc.)
     87 +- ✅ HTML export with embedded styles
     88 +- ✅ PDF export capability
     89 +- ✅ Storage management
     90 +- ✅ 85%+ test coverage
     91 +
     92 +### Principle
     93 +> **Don't reinvent the wheel** - Reuse proven, tested code.
     94 +

    127 +## 3. Implementation Specification

    129 +### 3.1 Files to Port

    132 +|------------|--------|---------|

    141 +### 3.2 React Component: MarkdownRenderer
    142 +
    143 +```typescript
    144 +// src/components/markdown/MarkdownRenderer.tsx
    145 +import { useEffect, useRef, memo } from 'react';
    146 +import DOMPurify from 'dompurify';
    147 +import { marked } from 'marked';
    148 +import Prism from 'prismjs';
    149 +
    150 +// Import languages
    151 +import 'prismjs/components/prism-javascript';
    152 +import 'prismjs/components/prism-typescript';
    153 +import 'prismjs/components/prism-python';
    154 +import 'prismjs/components/prism-java';
    155 +import 'prismjs/components/prism-cpp';
    156 +import 'prismjs/components/prism-csharp';
    157 +import 'prismjs/components/prism-go';
    158 +import 'prismjs/components/prism-rust';
    159 +import 'prismjs/components/prism-sql';
    160 +import 'prismjs/components/prism-bash';
    161 +import 'prismjs/components/prism-json';
    162 +import 'prismjs/components/prism-yaml';
    163 +import 'prismjs/components/prism-markdown';
    164 +import 'prismjs/components/prism-jsx';
    165 +import 'prismjs/components/prism-tsx';
    166 +
    167 +interface MarkdownRendererProps {
    168 +  content: string;
    169 +  className?: string;
    170 +  theme?: 'nebula-dark' | 'nebula-light' | 'default-dark' | string;
    171 +  onCopyCode?: (code: string) => void;
    172 +}
    173 +
    174 +export const MarkdownRenderer = memo(function MarkdownRenderer({
    175 +  content,
    176 +  className = '',
    177 +  theme = 'nebula-dark',
    178 +  onCopyCode
    179 +}: MarkdownRendererProps) {
    180 +  const containerRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
    181 +
    182 +  useEffect(() => {
    183 +    if (!containerRef.current) return;
    184 +
    185 +    // Parse markdown to HTML
    186 +    const rawHtml = marked.parse(content, {
    187 +      gfm: true,
    188 +      breaks: true
    189 +    });
    190 +
    191 +    // Sanitize HTML (XSS protection)
    192 +    const cleanHtml = DOMPurify.sanitize(rawHtml as string, {
    193 +      ADD_TAGS: ['iframe'], // For embeds if needed
    194 +      ADD_ATTR: ['target', 'rel']
    195 +    });
    196 +
    197 +    containerRef.current.innerHTML = cleanHtml;
    198 +
    199 +    // Apply syntax highlighting
    200 +    containerRef.current.querySelectorAll('pre code').forEach((block) => {
    201 +      Prism.highlightElement(block as HTMLElement);
    202 +
    203 +      // Add copy button
    204 +      const pre = block.parentElement;
    205 +      if (pre && !pre.querySelector('.copy-btn')) {
    206 +        const copyBtn = document.createElement('button');
    207 +        copyBtn.className = 'copy-btn';
    208 +        copyBtn.textContent = 'Copy';
    209 +        copyBtn.onclick = () => {
    210 +          navigator.clipboard.writeText(block.textContent || '');
    211 +          copyBtn.textContent = 'Copied!';
    212 +          setTimeout(() => { copyBtn.textContent = 'Copy'; }, 2000);
    213 +          onCopyCode?.(block.textContent || '');
    214 +        };
    215 +        pre.appendChild(copyBtn);
    216 +      }
    217 +    });
    218 +
    219 +    // Render Mermaid diagrams (lazy load)
    220 +    const mermaidBlocks = containerRef.current.querySelectorAll('code.language-mermaid');
    221 +    if (mermaidBlocks.length > 0) {
    222 +      import('mermaid').then(({ default: mermaid }) => {
    223 +        mermaid.initialize({
    224 +          startOnLoad: false,
    225 +          theme: theme.includes('dark') ? 'dark' : 'default'
    226 +        });
    227 +
    228 +        mermaidBlocks.forEach((block, i) => {
    229 +          const code = block.textContent || '';
    230 +          const container = document.createElement('div');
    231 +          container.className = 'mermaid-container';
    232 +
    233 +          mermaid.render(`mermaid-${i}`, code).then(({ svg }) => {
    234 +            container.innerHTML = svg;
    235 +            block.parentElement?.replaceWith(container);
    236 +          }).catch((err) => {
    237 +            container.innerHTML = `<div class="mermaid-error">Diagram error: ${err.message}</div>`;
    238 +            block.parentElement?.replaceWith(container);
    239 +          });
    240 +        });
    241 +      });
    242 +    }
    243 +
    244 +    // Render KaTeX math (lazy load)
    245 +    const mathBlocks = containerRef.current.querySelectorAll('code.language-math');
    246 +    if (mathBlocks.length > 0) {
    247 +      import('katex').then(({ default: katex }) => {
    248 +        import('katex/dist/katex.min.css');
    249 +
    250 +        mathBlocks.forEach((block) => {
    251 +          const code = block.textContent || '';
    252 +          const container = document.createElement('div');
    253 +          container.className = 'math-container';
    254 +
    255 +          try {
    256 +            katex.render(code, container, { displayMode: true });
    257 +            block.parentElement?.replaceWith(container);
    258 +          } catch (err) {
    259 +            container.innerHTML = `<div class="math-error">Math error: ${(err as Error).message}</div>`;
    260 +            block.parentElement?.replaceWith(container);
    261 +          }
    262 +        });
    263 +      });
    264 +    }
    265 +  }, [content, theme, onCopyCode]);
    266 +
    267 +  return (
    268 +    <div
    269 +      ref={containerRef}
    270 +      className={`markdown-body markdown-theme-${theme} ${className}`}
    271 +    />
    272 +  );
    273 +});
    274 +```
    275 +
    276 +### 3.3 Theme Integration
    277 +
    278 +```typescript
    279 +// src/hooks/useMarkdownTheme.ts
    280 +import { useState, useEffect, createContext, useContext } from 'react';
    281 +
    282 +type Theme = 'nebula-dark' | 'nebula-light' | 'default-dark' | 'default-light' |
    283 +             'forest-dark' | 'forest-light' | 'neon-dark' | 'neon-light' |
    284 +             'obsidian-dark' | 'obsidian-light' | 'ocean-dark' | 'ocean-light' |
    285 +             'sunset-dark' | 'sunset-light';
    286 +
    287 +interface ThemeContextValue {
    288 +  theme: Theme;
    289 +  setTheme: (theme: Theme) => void;
    290 +  availableThemes: Theme[];
    291 +}
    292 +
    293 +const MarkdownThemeContext = createContext<ThemeContextValue | null>(null);
    294 +
    295 +export function MarkdownThemeProvider({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
    296 +  const [theme, setTheme] = useState<Theme>('nebula-dark');
    297 +
    298 +  useEffect(() => {
    299 +    // Load theme CSS dynamically
    300 +    const link = document.createElement('link');
    301 +    link.rel = 'stylesheet';
    302 +    link.href = `/styles/markdown-themes/${theme}.css`;
    303 +    link.id = 'markdown-theme';
    304 +
    305 +    const existing = document.getElementById('markdown-theme');
    306 +    if (existing) existing.remove();
    307 +
    308 +    document.head.appendChild(link);
    309 +  }, [theme]);
    310 +
    311 +  return (
    312 +    <MarkdownThemeContext.Provider value={{
    313 +      theme,
    314 +      setTheme,
    315 +      availableThemes: [
    316 +        'nebula-dark', 'nebula-light',
    317 +        'default-dark', 'default-light',
    318 +        'forest-dark', 'forest-light',
    319 +        'neon-dark', 'neon-light',
    320 +        'obsidian-dark', 'obsidian-light',
    321 +        'ocean-dark', 'ocean-light',
    322 +        'sunset-dark', 'sunset-light'
    323 +      ]
    324 +    }}>
    325 +      {children}
    326 +    </MarkdownThemeContext.Provider>
    327 +  );
    328 +}
    329 +
    330 +export function useMarkdownTheme() {
    331 +  const context = useContext(MarkdownThemeContext);
    332 +  if (!context) throw new Error('useMarkdownTheme must be used within MarkdownThemeProvider');
    333 +  return context;
    334 +}
    335 +```

    337 +### 3.4 Export Service
    338 +
    339 +```typescript
    340 +// src/lib/export/exportService.ts
    341 +import { MarkdownRenderer } from '@/components/markdown';
    342 +
    343 +export async function exportToHTML(
    344 +  content: string,
    345 +  title: string,
    346 +  theme: string = 'nebula-dark'
    347 +): Promise<string> {
    348 +  // Load theme CSS
    349 +  const themeCSS = await fetch(`/styles/markdown-themes/${theme}.css`).then(r => r.text());
    350 +
    351 +  // Generate HTML
    352 +  const html = `
    353 +<!DOCTYPE html>
    354 +<html lang="en">
    355 +<head>
    356 +  <meta charset="UTF-8">
    357 +  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
    358 +  <title>${title} - Coach Atlas</title>
    359 +  <style>${themeCSS}</style>
    360 +</head>
    361 +<body class="markdown-body markdown-theme-${theme}">
    362 +  ${marked.parse(content)}
    363 +</body>
    364 +</html>`;
    365 +
    366 +  return html;
    367 +}
    368 +
    369 +export function downloadFile(content: string, filename: string, mimeType: string) {
    370 +  const blob = new Blob([content], { type: mimeType });
    371 +  const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
    372 +  const a = document.createElement('a');
    373 +  a.href = url;
    374 +  a.download = filename;
    375 +  a.click();
    376 +  URL.revokeObjectURL(url);
    377 +}
    378 +
    379 +export async function exportToMarkdown(content: string, filename: string) {
    380 +  downloadFile(content, `${filename}.md`, 'text/markdown');
    381 +}
    382 +
    383 +export async function exportToHTMLFile(content: string, title: string, theme?: string) {
    384 +  const html = await exportToHTML(content, title, theme);
    385 +  downloadFile(html, `${title.replace(/\s+/g, '-').toLowerCase()}.html`, 'text/html');
    386 +}
    387 +```
    388 +
    389 +---
    390 +
    391 +## 4. Dependencies Required
    392 +
    393 +```bash
    394 +npm install marked dompurify prismjs mermaid katex
    395 +npm install -D @types/dompurify @types/prismjs
    396 +```
    397 +
    398 +**Bundle Size Impact:**
    399 +| Package | Size (gzip) | Loading |
    400 +|---------|-------------|---------|
    401 +| marked | ~15KB | Immediate |
    402 +| dompurify | ~8KB | Immediate |
    403 +| prismjs | ~20KB | Immediate |
    404 +| mermaid | ~500KB | **Lazy loaded** |
    405 +| katex | ~100KB | **Lazy loaded** |
    406 +
    407 +**Total immediate:** ~43KB
    408 +**Total lazy:** ~600KB (loaded only when diagrams/math used)
    409 +
    410 +---
    411 +
    412 +## 5. Usage Examples
    413 +
    414 +### In Chat Component
    415 +```tsx
    416 +// src/pages/Chat.tsx
    417 +import { MarkdownRenderer } from '@/components/markdown';
    418 +
    419 +function MessageBubble({ message }: { message: Message }) {
    420 +  return (
    421 +    <div className={`message ${message.role}`}>
    422 +      {message.role === 'assistant' ? (
    423 +        <MarkdownRenderer content={message.content} />
    424 +      ) : (
    425 +        <p>{message.content}</p>
    426 +      )}
    427 +    </div>
    428 +  );
    429 +}
    430 +```
    431 +
    432 +### In Tutorial View
    433 +```tsx
    434 +// src/pages/Tutorial.tsx
    435 +import { MarkdownRenderer } from '@/components/markdown';
    436 +import { useMarkdownTheme, MarkdownThemeProvider } from '@/hooks/useMarkdownTheme';
    437 +
    438 +function TutorialPage({ content }: { content: string }) {
    439 +  const { theme, setTheme, availableThemes } = useMarkdownTheme();
    440 +
    441 +  return (
    442 +    <div className="tutorial-view">
    443 +      <select value={theme} onChange={e => setTheme(e.target.value as any)}>
    444 +        {availableThemes.map(t => <option key={t} value={t}>{t}</option>)}
    445 +      </select>
    446 +
    447 +      <MarkdownRenderer content={content} theme={theme} />
    448 +    </div>
    449 +  );
    450 +}
    451 +```
    452 +
    453 +---
    454 +
    455 +## 6. Validation Criteria
    456 +
    457 +| Test | Expected Result |
    458 +|------|-----------------|
    459 +| Code block renders | Syntax highlighted with correct language |
    460 +| Copy button works | Code copied to clipboard, button shows "Copied!" |
    461 +| Mermaid diagram renders | SVG diagram displays correctly |
    462 +| Math formula renders | KaTeX renders LaTeX correctly |
    463 +| Theme switch works | Styles update without page reload |
    464 +| XSS attack blocked | Malicious HTML sanitized |
    465 +| Export to MD works | Valid markdown file downloads |
    466 +| Export to HTML works | Self-contained HTML with embedded CSS |
    467 +
    468 +---
    469 +
    470 +## 7. Migration Path
    471 +
    472 +### Phase 1: Setup (Day 1)
    473 +1. Install dependencies
    474 +2. Copy theme CSS files to `src/styles/markdown-themes/`
    475 +3. Create `MarkdownRenderer` component
    476 +
    477 +### Phase 2: Integration (Day 2)
    478 +1. Replace `<p>{message.content}</p>` in Chat.tsx with `<MarkdownRenderer>`
    479 +2. Add `MarkdownThemeProvider` to App.tsx
    480 +3. Test with various markdown content
    481 +
    482 +### Phase 3: Enhancement (Day 3)
    483 +1. Add export functionality
    484 +2. Add theme selector to Settings
    485 +3. Performance optimization (memo, virtualization)
    486 +
    487 +---
    488 +
    489 +## 8. Consequences
    490 +
    491 +### Positive
    492 +- **Consistency**: Same rendering across all views
    493 +- **Quality**: Battle-tested code with 85%+ coverage
    494 +- **Features**: 15 themes, syntax highlighting, diagrams, math
    495 +- **Performance**: Lazy loading for heavy libraries
    496 +
    497 +### Negative
    498 +- **Divergence**: Updates to `markdown-viewer-app` require manual sync
    499 +- **Bundle**: ~600KB lazy-loaded for diagrams/math
    500 +
    501 +### Mitigations
    502 +- Keep `src/lib/external/markdown-viewer-app` as reference (read-only)
    503 +- Document any adaptations made
    504 +- Consider extracting to shared npm package in future
    505 +
    506 +---
    507 +
    508 +## 9. Approval
    509 +
    510 +| Role | Name | Status | Date |
    511 +|------|------|--------|------|
    512 +| Architect | AntiGravity | ✅ Approved | 2024-12-22 |
    513 +| Principal SDE | Cline | ✅ Approved | 2024-12-22 |
    514 +
    515 +---
    516 +
    517 +## Document History
    518 +
    519 +| Version | Date | Author | Changes |
    520 +|---------|------|--------|---------|
    521 +| 1.0 | 2024-12-22 | AntiGravity | Initial proposal |
    522 +| 1.1 | 2024-12-22 | Cline | Added implementation details, code examples |
    523

### ✨ `docs/ard/002-byok-api-key-strategy.md` **[ADDED]**

**Status:** ✅ **NEW FILE** - This file has been newly created

**Type:** Documentation 📖

```diff
@@ -0,0 +1,378 @@
      1 +# ARD-002: BYOK (Bring Your Own Key) Strategy
      2 +
      3 +**Status**: Approved (Critical)
      4 +**Date**: 2024-12-22
      5 +**Author**: Cline (Principal SDE)
      6 +**Priority**: P0 - Foundational Architecture Decision
      7 +**Decision**: Users MUST provide their own API keys. Developer NEVER provides keys.
      8 +
      9 +---
     10 +
     11 +## ⚠️ CRITICAL PRINCIPLE
     12 +
     13 +> **Coach Atlas is 100% BYOK (Bring Your Own Key).**
     14 +>
     15 +> **The developer provides NO API keys. ZERO cost liability for the developer.**
     16 +>
     17 +> **Users are responsible for their own API usage and costs.**
     18 +
     19 +---
     20 +
     21 +## 1. Context
     22 +
     23 +### Problem Statement
     24 +AI API calls cost money. If the developer provides API keys:
     25 +- **Unlimited liability** - Users could run up massive bills
     26 +- **Abuse risk** - Keys could be leaked or shared
     27 +- **Scaling costs** - Popular app = bankrupt developer
     28 +- **No sustainable business model** - Free API access isn't viable
     29 +
     30 +### Industry Standard
     31 +All major AI-powered apps use one of these models:
     32 +1. **BYOK** - User provides their own keys (Claude, ChatGPT wrappers)
     33 +2. **Subscription** - User pays developer, developer pays API (SaaS)
     34 +3. **Freemium** - Limited free tier, pay for more (rate-limited)
     35 +
     36 +### Our Decision
     37 +**Coach Atlas uses BYOK exclusively** - the simplest, safest model for a developer.
     38 +
     39 +---
     40 +
     41 +## 2. Decision
     42 +
     43 +### Core Rules
     44 +
     45 +| Rule | Requirement | Violation = |
     46 +|------|-------------|-------------|
     47 +| **Rule 1** | NO developer API keys in codebase | Critical bug |
     48 +| **Rule 2** | NO backend that stores/proxies keys | Architecture violation |
     49 +| **Rule 3** | User keys stored ONLY in user's browser | Security requirement |
     50 +| **Rule 4** | Direct client-to-provider API calls | Privacy feature |
     51 +| **Rule 5** | Clear messaging that USER pays API costs | Legal/UX requirement |
     52 +
     53 +### Architecture
     54 +
     55 +```
     56 +┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
     57 +│                      USER'S BROWSER                          │
     58 +│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
     59 +│  │              Coach Atlas (React App)                 │    │
     60 +│  │  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │    │
     61 +│  │  │          User's API Key (localStorage)       │   │    │
     62 +│  │  │     Never sent to our servers. Ever.         │   │    │
     63 +│  │  └─────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │    │
     64 +│  │                        │                            │    │
     65 +│  │                        ▼                            │    │
     66 +│  │  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │    │
     67 +│  │  │        Direct HTTPS to AI Provider          │   │    │
     68 +│  │  │  (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google - User's Bill)  │   │    │
     69 +│  │  └─────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │    │
     70 +│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
     71 +└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
     72 +
     73 +❌ NO BACKEND SERVER (No key proxying, no storage, no costs)
     74 +❌ NO DEVELOPER API KEYS (Zero liability)
     75 +✅ USER PAYS THEIR OWN BILLS (Directly to OpenAI/Anthropic/Google)
     76 +```
     77 +
     78 +---
     79 +
     80 +## 3. Implementation
     81 +
     82 +### 3.1 Settings Page - Key Entry
     83 +
     84 +```tsx
     85 +// src/pages/Settings.tsx
     86 +function SettingsPage() {
     87 +  return (
     88 +    <div>
     89 +      <Alert variant="info" className="mb-4">
     90 +        <AlertTitle>🔑 Your API Keys, Your Costs</AlertTitle>
     91 +        <AlertDescription>
     92 +          Coach Atlas uses YOUR API keys. You pay the AI providers directly.
     93 +          We never see, store, or transmit your keys to any server.
     94 +          <a href="/docs/api-keys" className="underline ml-1">
     95 +            Learn how to get API keys →
     96 +          </a>
     97 +        </AlertDescription>
     98 +      </Alert>
     99 +
    100 +      <ApiKeyInput
    101 +        provider="openai"
    102 +        label="OpenAI API Key"
    103 +        placeholder="sk-..."
    104 +        helpText="Get your key at platform.openai.com"
    105 +      />
    106 +
    107 +      {/* More providers... */}
    108 +    </div>
    109 +  );
    110 +}
    111 +```
    112 +
    113 +### 3.2 Storage - Browser Only
    114 +
    115 +```typescript
    116 +// src/lib/storage/credentials.ts
    117 +
    118 +/**
    119 + * BYOK Storage Manager
    120 + *
    121 + * CRITICAL: Keys are stored ONLY in the user's browser localStorage.
    122 + * They are NEVER sent to any server, including ours.
    123 + * The user is solely responsible for their API usage costs.
    124 + */
    125 +
    126 +const STORAGE_KEY = 'coach-atlas-credentials';
    127 +
    128 +interface Credentials {
    129 +  openai?: { apiKey: string };
    130 +  anthropic?: { apiKey: string };
    131 +  google?: { apiKey: string };
    132 +  bedrock?: { accessKeyId: string; secretAccessKey: string; region: string };
    133 +}
    134 +
    135 +export function saveCredentials(credentials: Credentials): void {
    136 +  // Store in user's browser ONLY
    137 +  localStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, JSON.stringify(credentials));
    138 +}
    139 +
    140 +export function loadCredentials(): Credentials | null {
    141 +  const stored = localStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY);
    142 +  return stored ? JSON.parse(stored) : null;
    143 +}
    144 +
    145 +export function clearCredentials(): void {
    146 +  localStorage.removeItem(STORAGE_KEY);
    147 +}
    148 +
    149 +// IMPORTANT: No function to export or transmit credentials exists
    150 +```
    151 +
    152 +### 3.3 API Calls - Direct to Provider
    153 +
    154 +```typescript
    155 +// src/lib/ai/openai.ts
    156 +
    157 +/**
    158 + * BYOK: All API calls go directly from user's browser to OpenAI.
    159 + * No proxy server. No backend. User pays OpenAI directly.
    160 + */
    161 +
    162 +export async function callOpenAI(
    163 +  messages: Message[],
    164 +  userApiKey: string // User's key, from their localStorage
    165 +): Promise<string> {
    166 +  const response = await fetch('https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions', {
    167 +    method: 'POST',
    168 +    headers: {
    169 +      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    170 +      'Authorization': `Bearer ${userApiKey}` // User's key, user's bill
    171 +    },
    172 +    body: JSON.stringify({
    173 +      model: 'gpt-4o',
    174 +      messages
    175 +    })
    176 +  });
    177 +
    178 +  if (!response.ok) {
    179 +    const error = await response.json();
    180 +    throw new Error(error.error?.message || 'API call failed');
    181 +  }
    182 +
    183 +  const data = await response.json();
    184 +  return data.choices[0].message.content;
    185 +}
    186 +```
    187 +
    188 +### 3.4 No Backend Required
    189 +
    190 +```
    191 +Coach Atlas Architecture:
    192 +─────────────────────────
    193 +
    194 +✅ Static files only (HTML, CSS, JS)
    195 +✅ Hosted on CDN (Vercel, Netlify, GitHub Pages)
    196 +✅ Zero server costs for developer
    197 +✅ Zero API costs for developer
    198 +✅ User's browser talks directly to AI providers
    199 +
    200 +❌ NO Express/Node backend
    201 +❌ NO database for storing keys
    202 +❌ NO proxy server for API calls
    203 +❌ NO developer-provided API keys
    204 +```
    205 +
    206 +---
    207 +
    208 +## 4. User Communication
    209 +
    210 +### 4.1 Landing Page Messaging
    211 +
    212 +```tsx
    213 +// src/components/Hero.tsx
    214 +<div className="feature-callout">
    215 +  <h3>🔑 Bring Your Own Key</h3>
    216 +  <p>
    217 +    Use your own API keys from OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google.
    218 +    <strong>You control your costs.</strong> We never see your keys.
    219 +  </p>
    220 +</div>
    221 +```
    222 +
    223 +### 4.2 First-Time Setup Flow
    224 +
    225 +```
    226 +Step 1: "Welcome to Coach Atlas!"
    227 +        "To get started, you'll need an API key from one of these providers:"
    228 +        [OpenAI] [Anthropic] [Google]
    229 +
    230 +Step 2: "Don't have an API key?"
    231 +        "Click here for a quick guide to getting your free trial credits."
    232 +        - OpenAI: $5 free credits for new accounts
    233 +        - Anthropic: Limited free tier available
    234 +        - Google: $300 free credits for new GCP accounts
    235 +
    236 +Step 3: "Your key stays private"
    237 +        "Your API key is stored only in your browser.
    238 +         It's never sent to our servers. You pay the AI provider directly."
    239 +
    240 +Step 4: [Paste API Key] → [Validate] → [Start Chatting]
    241 +```
    242 +
    243 +### 4.3 Cost Awareness UI
    244 +
    245 +```tsx
    246 +// src/components/chat/CostIndicator.tsx
    247 +function CostIndicator({ tokens, model }: { tokens: number; model: string }) {
    248 +  const estimatedCost = calculateCost(tokens, model);
    249 +
    250 +  return (
    251 +    <div className="text-xs text-muted">
    252 +      ~{tokens.toLocaleString()} tokens • ~${estimatedCost.toFixed(4)}
    253 +      <TooltipTrigger>
    254 +        <span className="underline ml-1">Your API cost</span>
    255 +      </TooltipTrigger>
    256 +      <TooltipContent>
    257 +        This message used approximately {tokens} tokens.
    258 +        You'll be billed directly by {getProvider(model)}.
    259 +      </TooltipContent>
    260 +    </div>
    261 +  );
    262 +}
    263 +```
    264 +
    265 +---
    266 +
    267 +## 5. Security Considerations
    268 +
    269 +### 5.1 Key Protection
    270 +
    271 +| Risk | Mitigation |
    272 +|------|------------|
    273 +| XSS stealing keys | CSP headers, no inline scripts |
    274 +| Key in URL | Never include keys in URLs |
    275 +| Key logging | No console.log of keys in production |
    276 +| Key in errors | Sanitize error messages |
    277 +| Key in analytics | No analytics that capture localStorage |
    278 +
    279 +### 5.2 Code Review Checklist
    280 +
    281 +Before merging any PR, verify:
    282 +- [ ] No hardcoded API keys in code
    283 +- [ ] No keys logged to console
    284 +- [ ] No keys sent to any analytics/error tracking
    285 +- [ ] No keys in URL parameters
    286 +- [ ] Keys stored only in localStorage
    287 +- [ ] API calls go directly to provider, not through backend
    288 +
    289 +---
    290 +
    291 +## 6. Legal & Compliance
    292 +
    293 +### 6.1 Terms of Service Requirements
    294 +
    295 +```
    296 +Coach Atlas Terms of Service must include:
    297 +
    298 +1. BYOK DISCLOSURE
    299 +   "Coach Atlas requires you to provide your own API keys from third-party
    300 +   AI providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, AWS). You are solely responsible
    301 +   for any costs incurred from using these services."
    302 +
    303 +2. NO WARRANTY FOR API COSTS
    304 +   "We do not control, limit, or guarantee the costs associated with your
    305 +   API usage. Please review the pricing of your chosen AI provider."
    306 +
    307 +3. KEY SECURITY RESPONSIBILITY
    308 +   "Your API keys are stored locally on your device. You are responsible
    309 +   for keeping your keys secure. We recommend rotating keys periodically."
    310 +```
    311 +
    312 +### 6.2 Privacy Policy Requirements
    313 +
    314 +```
    315 +Coach Atlas Privacy Policy must state:
    316 +
    317 +1. NO KEY TRANSMISSION
    318 +   "Your API keys are never transmitted to Coach Atlas servers. They remain
    319 +   solely in your browser's local storage."
    320 +
    321 +2. NO KEY STORAGE
    322 +   "We do not have any database or server that stores your API keys."
    323 +
    324 +3. DIRECT API COMMUNICATION
    325 +   "When you use Coach Atlas, your browser communicates directly with the
    326 +   AI provider using your API key. We do not act as an intermediary."
    327 +```
    328 +
    329 +---
    330 +
    331 +## 7. Consequences
    332 +
    333 +### Positive
    334 +- **Zero cost liability** for developer
    335 +- **No scaling costs** as user base grows
    336 +- **Privacy-first** architecture
    337 +- **Simple hosting** (static files only)
    338 +- **User trust** through transparency
    339 +
    340 +### Negative
    341 +- **Setup friction** for new users (need to get API key)
    342 +- **No usage analytics** (can't track API calls)
    343 +- **No rate limiting** (user could exhaust their own credits)
    344 +
    345 +### Mitigations for Negatives
    346 +- Provide clear API key acquisition guides
    347 +- Show estimated token/cost per message
    348 +- Optional rate limiting in UI (user-configurable)
    349 +
    350 +---
    351 +
    352 +## 8. Validation Criteria
    353 +
    354 +| Test | Expected Result |
    355 +|------|-----------------|
    356 +| Search codebase for API keys | Zero matches |
    357 +| Check network requests | Only to AI providers, not to backend |
    358 +| Inspect localStorage | Only place where keys are stored |
    359 +| Clear localStorage | App should prompt for keys again |
    360 +| Invalid key | Clear error message, no charge |
    361 +
    362 +---
    363 +
    364 +## 9. Approval
    365 +
    366 +| Role | Name | Status | Date |
    367 +|------|------|--------|------|

    369 +| Principal SDE | Cline | ✅ Approved | 2024-12-22 |

    371 +

    375 +

### ✨ `docs/brd/BRD-coach-atlas.md` **[ADDED]**

**Status:** ✅ **NEW FILE** - This file has been newly created

**Type:** Documentation 📖

```diff
@@ -0,0 +1,720 @@
      1 +# Coach Atlas - Business Requirements Document (BRD)
      2 +
      3 +**Document Version**: 1.0
      4 +**Date**: 2024-12-22
      5 +**Status**: Draft
      6 +**Owner**: PrakharMNNIT
      7 +
      8 +---
      9 +
     10 +## Table of Contents
     11 +
     12 +1. [Executive Summary](#1-executive-summary)
     13 +2. [Business Objectives](#2-business-objectives)
     14 +3. [Stakeholders](#3-stakeholders)
     15 +4. [Functional Requirements](#4-functional-requirements)
     16 +5. [Non-Functional Requirements](#5-non-functional-requirements)
     17 +6. [User Stories](#6-user-stories)
     18 +7. [Technical Requirements](#7-technical-requirements)
     19 +8. [Integration Requirements](#8-integration-requirements)
     20 +9. [WebView Requirements](#9-webview-requirements)
     21 +10. [Acceptance Criteria](#10-acceptance-criteria)
     22 +11. [Constraints & Assumptions](#11-constraints--assumptions)
     23 +12. [Risk Assessment](#12-risk-assessment)
     24 +13. [Implementation Phases](#13-implementation-phases)
     25 +14. [Appendix](#14-appendix)
     26 +
     27 +---
     28 +
     29 +## 1. Executive Summary
     30 +
     31 +### 1.1 Product Vision
     32 +
     33 +Coach Atlas is an AI-powered technical interview mentor and comprehensive tutorial creator that transforms how engineers prepare for technical interviews. Unlike existing solutions that encourage memorization, Coach Atlas builds genuine problem-solving skills through guided discovery and brutally honest feedback.
     34 +
     35 +### 1.2 Problem Statement
     36 +
     37 +Software engineers face critical challenges in interview preparation:
     38 +- **Memorization culture**: Most resources teach "what" not "how to think"
     39 +- **No real feedback**: Self-study provides no honest skill assessment
     40 +- **Fragmented resources**: Interview prep scattered across multiple platforms
     41 +- **Non-production code**: Examples don't work in real jobs
     42 +- **Expensive coaching**: Human coaches cost $100-500/hour
     43 +
     44 +### 1.3 Solution Overview
     45 +
     46 +Coach Atlas provides:
     47 +- **AI Interview Coach**: Socratic method teaching with escalating hints
     48 +- **Tutorial Generator**: Comprehensive, beginner-to-advanced guides
     49 +- **Multi-Provider Support**: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google AI, AWS Bedrock (BYOK)
     50 +- **Rich Content Rendering**: Markdown, syntax highlighting, Mermaid diagrams, KaTeX math
     51 +- **WebView Compatible**: Embeddable in mobile apps via WebView
     52 +
     53 +### 1.4 Success Metrics
     54 +
     55 +| Metric | Target | Measurement |
     56 +|--------|--------|-------------|
     57 +| User Session Duration | > 15 minutes | Session tracking |
     58 +| Chat Response Time | < 3 seconds (first token) | Performance monitoring |
     59 +| Tutorial Completeness | 95% structured output | Content analysis |
     60 +| Mobile Usage | > 30% of sessions | Viewport detection |
     61 +| Error Rate | < 0.1% | Error logging |
     62 +
     63 +---
     64 +
     65 +## 2. Business Objectives
     66 +
     67 +### 2.1 Primary Objectives
     68 +
     69 +| ID | Objective | Priority | Success Criteria |
     70 +|----|-----------|----------|------------------|
     71 +| BO-01 | Enable effective interview preparation | P0 | Users report improved confidence |
     72 +| BO-02 | Provide multi-provider AI flexibility | P0 | All 4 providers functional |
     73 +| BO-03 | Deliver beautiful content rendering | P0 | Markdown, code, diagrams render correctly |
     74 +| BO-04 | Support mobile via WebView | P1 | 100% functionality in WebView |
     75 +| BO-05 | Zero vendor lock-in | P1 | Users can switch providers seamlessly |
     76 +
     77 +### 2.2 Secondary Objectives
     78 +
     79 +| ID | Objective | Priority | Success Criteria |
     80 +|----|-----------|----------|------------------|

    248 +## 6. User Stories
    249 +
    250 +### Epic 1: Core Chat Experience
    251 +
    252 +```
    253 +US-01: As a user, I want to see AI responses render markdown properly
    254 +       so that code blocks, lists, and formatting display correctly.
    255 +
    256 +       Acceptance Criteria:
    257 +       - Code blocks have syntax highlighting
    258 +       - Headers render with proper sizing
    259 +       - Lists (ordered/unordered) display correctly
    260 +       - Links are clickable
    261 +       - Bold/italic text renders
    262 +
    263 +US-02: As a user, I want to see AI responses stream in real-time
    264 +       so that I don't wait for the entire response before seeing content.
    265 +
    266 +       Acceptance Criteria:
    267 +       - Tokens appear as they're received
    268 +       - Markdown renders progressively
    269 +       - Loading indicator shows during streaming
    270 +       - Can scroll while streaming
    271 +
    272 +US-03: As a user, I want my chat history to persist
    273 +       so that I can continue conversations after closing the browser.
    274 +
    275 +       Acceptance Criteria:
    276 +       - Messages saved to localStorage
    277 +       - Chat restored on page load
    278 +       - Can clear history manually
    279 +       - Multiple conversations supported (stretch)
    280 +```
    281 +
    282 +### Epic 2: Interview Coaching
    283 +
    284 +```
    285 +US-10: As an interview candidate, I want Coach Atlas to guide me
    286 +       through problems using questions rather than giving answers immediately.
    287 +
    288 +       Acceptance Criteria:
    289 +       - Initial response asks clarifying questions
    290 +       - Follow-up prompts for approach explanation
    291 +       - Hints escalate from subtle to direct
    292 +       - Final solution includes explanation
    293 +
    294 +US-11: As an interview candidate, I want to see visual diagrams
    295 +       for system design problems so I can understand architecture.
    296 +
    297 +       Acceptance Criteria:
    298 +       - Mermaid diagrams render in chat
    299 +       - Diagrams are readable on mobile
    300 +       - Can copy diagram source
    301 +```
    302 +
    303 +### Epic 3: Tutorial Creation
    304 +
    305 +```
    306 +US-20: As an educator, I want to generate structured tutorials
    307 +       by typing "TUTORIAL: [topic]" so I get comprehensive content.
    308 +
    309 +       Acceptance Criteria:
    310 +       - Tutorial has clear sections
    311 +       - Includes beginner, intermediate, advanced levels
    312 +       - Code examples are runnable
    313 +       - Interview tips included
    314 +
    315 +US-21: As an educator, I want to export tutorials as Markdown
    316 +       so I can share them with students.
    317 +
    318 +       Acceptance Criteria:
    319 +       - Export button appears for tutorials
    320 +       - Downloaded .md file is valid markdown
    321 +       - Images/diagrams included as text
    322 +```
    323 +
    324 +### Epic 4: WebView Integration
    325 +
    326 +```
    327 +US-30: As a mobile app developer, I want Coach Atlas to work in WebView
    328 +       so I can embed it in my React Native/Flutter app.
    329 +
    330 +       Acceptance Criteria:

    434 +### 7.3 API Integration Patterns
    435 +
    436 +```typescript
    437 +// Provider Strategy Pattern
    438 +interface AIProvider {
    439 +  name: string;
    440 +  call(messages: Message[]): Promise<string>;
    441 +  stream(messages: Message[]): AsyncGenerator<string>;
    442 +  validateKey(key: string): Promise<boolean>;
    443 +}
    444 +
    445 +// Streaming Response Handling
    446 +async function* streamResponse(provider: AIProvider, messages: Message[]) {
    447 +  for await (const token of provider.stream(messages)) {
    448 +    yield token;
    449 +  }
    450 +}
    451 +```

    487 +## 9. WebView Requirements
    488 +
    489 +### 9.1 Compatibility Matrix
    490 +
    491 +| Platform | WebView Engine | Min Version | Notes |
    492 +|----------|---------------|-------------|-------|
    493 +| iOS | WKWebView | iOS 14+ | Preferred |
    494 +| Android | Chrome Custom Tabs | Android 7+ | Or WebView |
    495 +| React Native | react-native-webview | 11.0+ | Most common |
    496 +| Flutter | webview_flutter | 4.0+ | Official plugin |
    497 +| Capacitor | @capacitor/browser | 5.0+ | Native bridge |
    498 +
    499 +### 9.2 WebView Bridge API
    500 +
    501 +```typescript
    502 +// React → Native
    503 +interface WebViewBridge {
    504 +  share(content: string, format: 'text' | 'markdown' | 'html'): void;
    505 +  copyToClipboard(text: string): void;
    506 +  openExternal(url: string): void;
    507 +  hapticFeedback(type: 'light' | 'medium' | 'heavy'): void;
    508 +  getConfig(): Promise<AppConfig>;
    509 +  setConfig(config: AppConfig): Promise<void>;
    510 +}
    511 +
    512 +// Native → React
    513 +interface NativeMessages {
    514 +  CONFIG_UPDATE: { config: AppConfig };
    515 +  THEME_CHANGE: { theme: 'light' | 'dark' };
    516 +  SAFE_AREA: { top: number; bottom: number };
    517 +}
    518 +
    519 +// Implementation
    520 +const bridge: WebViewBridge = {
    521 +  share: (content, format) => {
    522 +    window.ReactNativeWebView?.postMessage(
    523 +      JSON.stringify({ type: 'SHARE', payload: { content, format } })
    524 +    );
    525 +  },
    526 +  // ...
    527 +};
    528 +```
    529 +

    533 +/* Support for notched devices */
    534 +:root {

    536 +  --safe-area-bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px);
    537 +}
    538 +
    539 +.app-container {
    540 +  padding-top: var(--safe-area-top);
    541 +  padding-bottom: var(--safe-area-bottom);
    542 +}

    589 +
    590 +## 11. Constraints & Assumptions
    591 +
    592 +### 11.1 Constraints
    593 +
    594 +1. **No backend**: All processing happens client-side
    595 +2. **BYOK model**: Users must provide their own API keys
    596 +3. **Browser storage limits**: ~5MB localStorage per domain
    597 +4. **CORS restrictions**: Direct API calls only to providers with CORS support
    598 +5. **Bundle size**: Must stay under 500KB for mobile performance
    599 +
    600 +### 11.2 Assumptions
    601 +
    602 +1. Users have valid API keys from at least one provider
    603 +2. Users have modern browsers (Chrome 90+, Safari 14+, Firefox 90+)
    604 +3. Network connectivity available for AI interactions
    605 +4. Users understand basic markdown syntax
    606 +5. Mobile users access via WebView, not mobile browser
    607 +
    608 +---
    609 +
    610 +## 12. Risk Assessment
    611 +
    612 +| Risk | Probability | Impact | Mitigation |
    613 +|------|------------|--------|------------|
    614 +| API provider changes | Medium | High | Abstract provider interface, easy to update |
    615 +| Rate limiting by providers | Medium | Medium | User education, optional rate limiting |
    616 +| Large bundle size | Medium | Medium | Code splitting, lazy loading |
    617 +| WebView compatibility issues | Low | High | Extensive testing, fallback UI |
    618 +| localStorage quota exceeded | Low | Medium | Data rotation, IndexedDB fallback |
    619 +| XSS vulnerabilities | Low | Critical | DOMPurify, CSP headers |

    672 +
    673 +```
    674 +You are Coach Atlas, a world-class technical mentor who combines deep interview
    675 +preparation coaching with comprehensive tutorial creation. You teach through
    676 +guided discovery, provide brutally honest feedback, and create production-ready
    677 +learning resources.
    678 +
    679 +Your core principles:
    680 +1. Build Problem Solvers, Not Solution Memorizers
    681 +2. Guided Discovery First - Ask questions before giving answers
    682 +3. Brutal Honesty Always - Tell it like it is, no sugarcoating
    683 +4. Visual Learning - Use diagrams, tables, and structured examples
    684 +5. Production-Ready - Everything you teach should work in real jobs
    685 +
    686 +For interview coaching: Use the Socratic method with escalating hints.
    687 +For tutorials: Create comprehensive, beginner-to-advanced guides with code examples.
    688 +For system design: Guide through requirements, capacity, API design, database,
    689 +architecture, and trade-offs.
    690 +
    691 +Always be direct, professional, and focused on building real skills.
    692 +```
    693 +
    694 +### 14.2 Glossary
    695 +
    696 +| Term | Definition |
    697 +|------|------------|
    698 +| BYOK | Bring Your Own Key - Users provide their own API keys |
    699 +| SSE | Server-Sent Events - Streaming protocol for real-time data |
    700 +| WebView | Native component that renders web content in mobile apps |
    701 +| Mermaid | Text-based diagramming tool |
    702 +| KaTeX | Fast math typesetting library |
    703 +| DOMPurify | XSS sanitization library |
    704 +
    705 +### 14.3 References
    706 +
    707 +- [Markdown Viewer Pro](https://github.com/PrakharMNNIT/markdown-viewer-app)
    708 +- [shadcn/ui Documentation](https://ui.shadcn.com/)

### ✨ `docs/hld/webview-integration-strategy.md` **[ADDED]**

**Type:** Documentation 📖

```diff
@@ -0,0 +1,893 @@
      1 +# Coach Atlas - WebView Integration Strategy
      2 +
      3 +**Document Version**: 1.0
      4 +**Date**: 2024-12-22
      5 +**Status**: Draft
      6 +**Purpose**: Define how Coach Atlas can be embedded in mobile apps via WebView
      7 +
      8 +---
      9 +
     10 +## Table of Contents
     11 +
     12 +1. [Overview](#1-overview)
     13 +2. [WebView Compatibility](#2-webview-compatibility)
     14 +3. [Integration Patterns](#3-integration-patterns)
     15 +4. [Bridge API Specification](#4-bridge-api-specification)
     16 +5. [Platform-Specific Guides](#5-platform-specific-guides)
     17 +6. [Configuration Options](#6-configuration-options)
     18 +7. [Security Considerations](#7-security-considerations)
     19 +8. [Performance Optimization](#8-performance-optimization)
     20 +9. [Troubleshooting](#9-troubleshooting)
     21 +
     22 +---
     23 +
     24 +## 1. Overview
     25 +
     26 +### 1.1 What is WebView Integration?
     27 +
     28 +Coach Atlas is designed as a standalone web application that can be embedded within native mobile applications using WebView technology. This allows mobile developers to:
     29 +
     30 +- Add AI interview coaching to existing apps
     31 +- Build dedicated Coach Atlas mobile apps without native development
     32 +- Share codebase between web and mobile platforms
     33 +- Leverage web technologies for rapid iteration
     34 +
     35 +### 1.2 Architecture
     36 +
     37 +```
     38 +┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
     39 +│                    Native Mobile App                     │
     40 +│  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
     41 +│  │                    WebView Container               │  │
     42 +│  │  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │  │
     43 +│  │  │              Coach Atlas SPA                 │  │  │
     44 +│  │  │  ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐   │  │  │
     45 +│  │  │  │         React Application            │   │  │  │
     46 +│  │  │  │  - Chat Interface                    │   │  │  │
     47 +│  │  │  │  - Settings Management               │   │  │  │
     48 +│  │  │  │  - Tutorial Display                  │   │  │  │
     49 +│  │  │  └─────────────────────────────────────┘   │  │  │
     50 +│  │  │                     │                        │  │  │
     51 +│  │  │              WebView Bridge                  │  │  │
     52 +│  │  └─────────────────────┼───────────────────────┘  │  │
     53 +│  │                        │                          │  │
     54 +│  │              Native Bridge Handler                │  │
     55 +│  └────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────┘  │
     56 +│                           │                              │
     57 +│              Native Features (Share, Storage, etc.)      │
     58 +└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
     59 +```
     60 +
     61 +### 1.3 Benefits
     62 +
     63 +| Benefit | Description |
     64 +|---------|-------------|
     65 +| **Single Codebase** | One React app for web, iOS, and Android |
     66 +| **Rapid Updates** | Update content without app store review |
     67 +| **Full Features** | All web features work in WebView |
     68 +| **Cost Effective** | No native development required |
     69 +| **Easy Integration** | Drop-in component for existing apps |
     70 +
     71 +### 1.4 Trade-offs
     72 +
     73 +| Trade-off | Mitigation |
     74 +|-----------|------------|
     75 +| Performance | Code splitting, lazy loading, optimized bundle |
     76 +| Native Feel | Haptic feedback, native share, proper animations |
     77 +| Storage | Use native storage via bridge for large data |
     78 +| Offline | Service Worker for basic offline support |
     79 +
     80 +---
     81 +
     82 +## 2. WebView Compatibility
     83 +
     84 +### 2.1 Supported Platforms
     85 +
     86 +| Platform | WebView Engine | Min Version | Status |
     87 +|----------|---------------|-------------|--------|
     88 +| iOS | WKWebView | iOS 14+ | ✅ Supported |
     89 +| Android | Chromium WebView | Android 7+ (API 24) | ✅ Supported |
     90 +| React Native | react-native-webview | 11.0+ | ✅ Supported |
     91 +| Flutter | webview_flutter | 4.0+ | ✅ Supported |
     92 +| Capacitor | Capacitor WebView | 5.0+ | ✅ Supported |
     93 +| Electron | Chromium | Any | ✅ Supported |
     94 +
     95 +### 2.2 Browser Features Required
     96 +
     97 +| Feature | Usage | Fallback |
     98 +|---------|-------|----------|
     99 +| ES2020 | Core JavaScript | Transpile with Vite |
    100 +| CSS Grid | Layout | Flexbox fallback |
    101 +| CSS Variables | Theming | Static values |
    102 +| Fetch API | API calls | Polyfill |
    103 +| LocalStorage | Persistence | Native bridge storage |
    104 +| IntersectionObserver | Lazy loading | Eager load |
    105 +
    106 +### 2.3 API Compatibility
    107 +
    108 +| API | Support | Notes |
    109 +|-----|---------|-------|
    110 +| OpenAI | ✅ Full | CORS enabled |
    111 +| Anthropic | ✅ Full | CORS enabled |
    112 +| Google AI | ✅ Full | CORS enabled |
    113 +| AWS Bedrock | ⚠️ Partial | Requires proxy or native bridge |
    114 +
    115 +---
    116 +
    117 +## 3. Integration Patterns
    118 +
    119 +### 3.1 Pattern A: Full Replacement
    120 +
    121 +Replace entire screen with Coach Atlas WebView.
    122 +
    123 +```
    124 +┌──────────────────────┐
    125 +│     Native App       │
    126 +├──────────────────────┤
    127 +│                      │
    128 +│   ┌──────────────┐   │
    129 +│   │   Coach      │   │
    130 +│   │   Atlas      │   │
    131 +│   │   WebView    │   │
    132 +│   │   (100%)     │   │
    133 +│   └──────────────┘   │
    134 +│                      │
    135 +└──────────────────────┘
    136 +```
    137 +
    138 +**Use Case**: Dedicated Coach Atlas app or section
    139 +
    140 +**Pros**: Full experience, simple implementation
    141 +
    142 +**Cons**: Navigation between native/web
    143 +
    144 +### 3.2 Pattern B: Modal/Sheet
    145 +
    146 +Display Coach Atlas as a modal overlay.
    147 +
    148 +```
    149 +┌──────────────────────┐
    150 +│     Native App       │
    151 +│  ┌────────────────┐  │
    152 +│  │  Modal Header  │  │
    153 +│  ├────────────────┤  │
    154 +│  │                │  │
    155 +│  │  Coach Atlas   │  │
    156 +│  │   WebView      │  │
    157 +│  │                │  │
    158 +│  └────────────────┘  │
    159 +│                      │
    160 +└──────────────────────┘
    161 +```
    162 +
    163 +**Use Case**: Chat assistant within larger app
    164 +
    165 +**Pros**: Context preserved, easy dismiss
    166 +
    167 +**Cons**: Smaller viewport, limited features
    168 +
    169 +### 3.3 Pattern C: Embedded Component
    170 +
    171 +Embed specific features (e.g., tutorial view only).
    172 +
    173 +```
    174 +┌──────────────────────┐
    175 +│     Native App       │
    176 +├──────────────────────┤
    177 +│    Native Content    │
    178 +├──────────────────────┤
    179 +│   Coach Atlas        │
    180 +│   Tutorial View      │
    181 +│   (Embedded)         │
    182 +├──────────────────────┤
    183 +│   Native Content     │
    184 +└──────────────────────┘
    185 +```
    186 +
    187 +**Use Case**: Display tutorials in learning app
    188 +
    189 +**Pros**: Seamless integration
    190 +
    191 +**Cons**: Complex bridge communication
    192 +
    193 +### 3.4 Recommended Pattern
    194 +
    195 +**For Mobile Apps**: Pattern A (Full Replacement) with native navigation header
    196 +
    197 +**For Existing Apps**: Pattern B (Modal/Sheet) for assistant functionality
    198 +
    199 +---
    200 +
    201 +## 4. Bridge API Specification
    202 +
    203 +### 4.1 React → Native Communication
    204 +
    205 +```typescript
    206 +// src/lib/webview.ts
    207 +
    208 +interface WebViewBridge {
    209 +  /**
    210 +   * Check if running inside WebView
    211 +   */
    212 +  isWebView(): boolean;
    213 +
    214 +  /**
    215 +   * Share content using native share sheet
    216 +   */
    217 +  share(options: ShareOptions): Promise<void>;
    218 +
    219 +  /**
    220 +   * Copy text to native clipboard
    221 +   */
    222 +  copyToClipboard(text: string): Promise<void>;
    223 +
    224 +  /**
    225 +   * Open URL in external browser
    226 +   */
    227 +  openExternal(url: string): void;
    228 +
    229 +  /**
    230 +   * Trigger haptic feedback
    231 +   */
    232 +  haptic(type: 'light' | 'medium' | 'heavy' | 'success' | 'error'): void;
    233 +
    234 +  /**
    235 +   * Request native storage
    236 +   */
    237 +  storage: {
    238 +    get(key: string): Promise<string | null>;
    239 +    set(key: string, value: string): Promise<void>;
    240 +    remove(key: string): Promise<void>;
    241 +  };
    242 +
    243 +  /**
    244 +   * Get device info
    245 +   */
    246 +  getDeviceInfo(): Promise<DeviceInfo>;
    247 +
    248 +  /**
    249 +   * Close WebView (if in modal)
    250 +   */
    251 +  close(): void;
    252 +}
    253 +
    254 +interface ShareOptions {
    255 +  title?: string;
    256 +  text: string;
    257 +  url?: string;
    258 +  format: 'text' | 'markdown' | 'html';
    259 +}
    260 +
    261 +interface DeviceInfo {
    262 +  platform: 'ios' | 'android' | 'web';
    263 +  version: string;
    264 +  safeAreaTop: number;
    265 +  safeAreaBottom: number;
    266 +}
    267 +```
    268 +
    269 +### 4.2 Native → React Communication
    270 +
    271 +```typescript
    272 +// Messages sent from native to React
    273 +
    274 +type NativeMessage =
    275 +  | { type: 'CONFIG_UPDATE'; payload: ConfigPayload }
    276 +  | { type: 'THEME_CHANGE'; payload: { theme: 'light' | 'dark' } }
    277 +  | { type: 'SAFE_AREA_UPDATE'; payload: { top: number; bottom: number } }
    278 +  | { type: 'BACK_PRESSED'; payload: null }
    279 +  | { type: 'KEYBOARD_STATE'; payload: { visible: boolean; height: number } }
    280 +  | { type: 'APP_STATE'; payload: { state: 'active' | 'background' | 'inactive' } };
    281 +
    282 +interface ConfigPayload {
    283 +  apiKey?: string;
    284 +  provider?: string;
    285 +  model?: string;
    286 +}
    287 +```
    288 +
    289 +### 4.3 Implementation
    290 +
    291 +```typescript
    292 +// src/lib/webview.ts
    293 +
    294 +const isWebView = (): boolean => {
    295 +  return !!(
    296 +    (window as any).ReactNativeWebView ||
    297 +    (window as any).flutter_inappwebview ||
    298 +    (window as any).webkit?.messageHandlers?.nativeBridge
    299 +  );
    300 +};
    301 +
    302 +const postMessage = (type: string, payload: any) => {
    303 +  const message = JSON.stringify({ type, payload, timestamp: Date.now() });
    304 +
    305 +  // React Native
    306 +  if ((window as any).ReactNativeWebView) {
    307 +    (window as any).ReactNativeWebView.postMessage(message);
    308 +    return;
    309 +  }
    310 +
    311 +  // Flutter
    312 +  if ((window as any).flutter_inappwebview) {
    313 +    (window as any).flutter_inappwebview.callHandler('nativeBridge', message);
    314 +    return;
    315 +  }
    316 +
    317 +  // iOS WKWebView (native app)
    318 +  if ((window as any).webkit?.messageHandlers?.nativeBridge) {
    319 +    (window as any).webkit.messageHandlers.nativeBridge.postMessage(message);
    320 +    return;
    321 +  }
    322 +
    323 +  // Fallback: web
    324 +  console.log('[WebView Bridge] No native handler:', type, payload);
    325 +};
    326 +
    327 +export const bridge: WebViewBridge = {
    328 +  isWebView,
    329 +
    330 +  share: async (options) => {
    331 +    if (isWebView()) {
    332 +      postMessage('SHARE', options);
    333 +    } else if (navigator.share) {
    334 +      await navigator.share({ title: options.title, text: options.text, url: options.url });
    335 +    } else {
    336 +      await navigator.clipboard.writeText(options.text);
    337 +    }
    338 +  },
    339 +
    340 +  copyToClipboard: async (text) => {
    341 +    if (isWebView()) {
    342 +      postMessage('COPY_CLIPBOARD', { text });
    343 +    } else {
    344 +      await navigator.clipboard.writeText(text);
    345 +    }
    346 +  },
    347 +
    348 +  openExternal: (url) => {
    349 +    if (isWebView()) {
    350 +      postMessage('OPEN_EXTERNAL', { url });
    351 +    } else {
    352 +      window.open(url, '_blank');
    353 +    }
    354 +  },
    355 +
    356 +  haptic: (type) => {
    357 +    if (isWebView()) {
    358 +      postMessage('HAPTIC', { type });
    359 +    }
    360 +  },
    361 +
    362 +  storage: {
    363 +    get: async (key) => {
    364 +      if (isWebView()) {
    365 +        return new Promise((resolve) => {
    366 +          const handler = (event: MessageEvent) => {
    367 +            const data = JSON.parse(event.data);
    368 +            if (data.type === 'STORAGE_GET_RESPONSE' && data.key === key) {
    369 +              window.removeEventListener('message', handler);
    370 +              resolve(data.value);
    371 +            }
    372 +          };
    373 +          window.addEventListener('message', handler);
    374 +          postMessage('STORAGE_GET', { key });
    375 +        });
    376 +      }
    377 +      return localStorage.getItem(key);
    378 +    },
    379 +    set: async (key, value) => {
    380 +      if (isWebView()) {
    381 +        postMessage('STORAGE_SET', { key, value });
    382 +      } else {
    383 +        localStorage.setItem(key, value);
    384 +      }
    385 +    },
    386 +    remove: async (key) => {
    387 +      if (isWebView()) {
    388 +        postMessage('STORAGE_REMOVE', { key });
    389 +      } else {
    390 +        localStorage.removeItem(key);
    391 +      }
    392 +    }
    393 +  },
    394 +
    395 +  getDeviceInfo: async () => {
    396 +    if (isWebView()) {
    397 +      return new Promise((resolve) => {
    398 +        const handler = (event: MessageEvent) => {
    399 +          const data = JSON.parse(event.data);
    400 +          if (data.type === 'DEVICE_INFO_RESPONSE') {
    401 +            window.removeEventListener('message', handler);
    402 +            resolve(data.payload);
    403 +          }
    404 +        };
    405 +        window.addEventListener('message', handler);
    406 +        postMessage('GET_DEVICE_INFO', {});
    407 +      });
    408 +    }
    409 +    return {
    410 +      platform: 'web',
    411 +      version: navigator.userAgent,
    412 +      safeAreaTop: 0,
    413 +      safeAreaBottom: 0
    414 +    };
    415 +  },
    416 +
    417 +  close: () => {
    418 +    if (isWebView()) {
    419 +      postMessage('CLOSE', {});
    420 +    }
    421 +  }
    422 +};
    423 +```
    424 +
    425 +---
    426 +
    427 +## 5. Platform-Specific Guides
    428 +
    429 +### 5.1 React Native Integration
    430 +
    431 +```typescript
    432 +// App.tsx (React Native)
    433 +import { WebView } from 'react-native-webview';
    434 +import { SafeAreaView, StyleSheet } from 'react-native';
    435 +
    436 +const CoachAtlasScreen = () => {
    437 +  const webViewRef = useRef<WebView>(null);
    438 +
    439 +  const handleMessage = (event: WebViewMessageEvent) => {
    440 +    const message = JSON.parse(event.nativeEvent.data);
    441 +
    442 +    switch (message.type) {
    443 +      case 'SHARE':
    444 +        Share.share({
    445 +          message: message.payload.text,
    446 +          title: message.payload.title,
    447 +        });
    448 +        break;
    449 +      case 'COPY_CLIPBOARD':
    450 +        Clipboard.setString(message.payload.text);
    451 +        break;
    452 +      case 'HAPTIC':
    453 +        Haptics.impactAsync(
    454 +          message.payload.type === 'light'
    455 +            ? Haptics.ImpactFeedbackStyle.Light
    456 +            : Haptics.ImpactFeedbackStyle.Medium
    457 +        );
    458 +        break;
    459 +      case 'CLOSE':
    460 +        navigation.goBack();
    461 +        break;
    462 +    }
    463 +  };
    464 +
    465 +  const injectSafeArea = () => {
    466 +    const safeArea = useSafeAreaInsets();
    467 +    webViewRef.current?.injectJavaScript(`
    468 +      window.postMessage(JSON.stringify({
    469 +        type: 'SAFE_AREA_UPDATE',
    470 +        payload: { top: ${safeArea.top}, bottom: ${safeArea.bottom} }
    471 +      }), '*');
    472 +    `);
    473 +  };
    474 +
    475 +  return (
    476 +    <SafeAreaView style={styles.container}>
    477 +      <WebView
    478 +        ref={webViewRef}
    479 +        source={{ uri: 'https://coach-atlas.vercel.app' }}
    480 +        onMessage={handleMessage}
    481 +        onLoadEnd={injectSafeArea}
    482 +        javaScriptEnabled={true}
    483 +        domStorageEnabled={true}
    484 +        allowsInlineMediaPlayback={true}
    485 +        mediaPlaybackRequiresUserAction={false}
    486 +        sharedCookiesEnabled={true}
    487 +      />
    488 +    </SafeAreaView>
    489 +  );
    490 +};
    491 +
    492 +const styles = StyleSheet.create({
    493 +  container: {
    494 +    flex: 1,
    495 +    backgroundColor: '#0a0f1a', // Match Coach Atlas background
    496 +  },
    497 +});
    498 +```

    558 +### 5.3 iOS Native Integration
    559 +
    560 +```swift
    561 +// CoachAtlasViewController.swift
    562 +import UIKit
    563 +import WebKit
    564 +
    565 +class CoachAtlasViewController: UIViewController {
    566 +    private var webView: WKWebView!
    567 +
    568 +    override func viewDidLoad() {
    569 +        super.viewDidLoad()
    570 +
    571 +        let config = WKWebViewConfiguration()
    572 +        let contentController = WKUserContentController()
    573 +        contentController.add(self, name: "nativeBridge")
    574 +        config.userContentController = contentController
    575 +
    576 +        webView = WKWebView(frame: view.bounds, configuration: config)
    577 +        webView.autoresizingMask = [.flexibleWidth, .flexibleHeight]
    578 +        view.addSubview(webView)
    579 +
    580 +        if let url = URL(string: "https://coach-atlas.vercel.app") {
    581 +            webView.load(URLRequest(url: url))
    582 +        }
    583 +    }
    584 +}
    585 +
    586 +extension CoachAtlasViewController: WKScriptMessageHandler {
    587 +    func userContentController(_ userContentController: WKUserContentController,
    588 +                               didReceive message: WKScriptMessage) {
    589 +        guard let body = message.body as? String,
    590 +              let data = body.data(using: .utf8),
    591 +              let json = try? JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: data) as? [String: Any],
    592 +              let type = json["type"] as? String else { return }
    593 +
    594 +        switch type {
    595 +        case "SHARE":
    596 +            if let payload = json["payload"] as? [String: String],
    597 +               let text = payload["text"] {
    598 +                let activityVC = UIActivityViewController(
    599 +                    activityItems: [text],
    600 +                    applicationActivities: nil
    601 +                )
    602 +                present(activityVC, animated: true)
    603 +            }
    604 +        case "COPY_CLIPBOARD":
    605 +            if let payload = json["payload"] as? [String: String],
    606 +               let text = payload["text"] {
    607 +                UIPasteboard.general.string = text
    608 +            }
    609 +        case "HAPTIC":
    610 +            UIImpactFeedbackGenerator(style: .light).impactOccurred()
    611 +        case "CLOSE":
    612 +            dismiss(animated: true)
    613 +        default:
    614 +            break
    615 +        }
    616 +    }
    617 +}
    618 +```
    619 +
    620 +### 5.4 Android Native Integration
    621 +
    622 +```kotlin
    623 +// CoachAtlasActivity.kt
    624 +import android.os.Bundle
    625 +import android.webkit.*
    626 +import androidx.appcompat.app.AppCompatActivity
    627 +import org.json.JSONObject
    628 +
    629 +class CoachAtlasActivity : AppCompatActivity() {
    630 +    private lateinit var webView: WebView
    631 +
    632 +    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
    633 +        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
    634 +
    635 +        webView = WebView(this).apply {
    636 +            settings.javaScriptEnabled = true
    637 +            settings.domStorageEnabled = true
    638 +            settings.allowContentAccess = true
    639 +
    640 +            addJavascriptInterface(WebViewBridge(), "AndroidBridge")
    641 +
    642 +            webViewClient = WebViewClient()
    643 +            loadUrl("https://coach-atlas.vercel.app")
    644 +        }
    645 +
    646 +        setContentView(webView)
    647 +    }
    648 +
    649 +    inner class WebViewBridge {
    650 +        @JavascriptInterface
    651 +        fun postMessage(message: String) {
    652 +            val json = JSONObject(message)
    653 +            when (json.getString("type")) {
    654 +                "SHARE" -> {
    655 +                    val payload = json.getJSONObject("payload")
    656 +                    val intent = Intent(Intent.ACTION_SEND).apply {
    657 +                        type = "text/plain"
    658 +                        putExtra(Intent.EXTRA_TEXT, payload.getString("text"))
    659 +                    }
    660 +                    startActivity(Intent.createChooser(intent, "Share"))
    661 +                }
    662 +                "COPY_CLIPBOARD" -> {
    663 +                    val payload = json.getJSONObject("payload")
    664 +                    val clipboard = getSystemService(CLIPBOARD_SERVICE) as ClipboardManager
    665 +                    clipboard.setPrimaryClip(
    666 +                        ClipData.newPlainText("Coach Atlas", payload.getString("text"))
    667 +                    )
    668 +                }
    669 +                "HAPTIC" -> {
    670 +                    val vibrator = getSystemService(VIBRATOR_SERVICE) as Vibrator
    671 +                    vibrator.vibrate(VibrationEffect.createOneShot(10, VibrationEffect.DEFAULT_AMPLITUDE))
    672 +                }
    673 +                "CLOSE" -> finish()
    674 +            }
    675 +        }
    676 +    }
    677 +}
    678 +```

    681 +
    682 +## 6. Configuration Options
    683 +
    684 +### 6.1 URL Parameters
    685 +
    686 +Coach Atlas accepts configuration via URL parameters:
    687 +
    688 +| Parameter | Type | Description | Default |
    689 +|-----------|------|-------------|---------|
    690 +| `mode` | `chat` \| `tutorial` | Initial mode | `chat` |
    691 +| `theme` | `dark` \| `light` | Color theme | `dark` |
    692 +| `embedded` | `true` \| `false` | Hide navigation | `false` |
    693 +| `provider` | `openai` \| `anthropic` \| `google` | Pre-select provider | None |
    694 +
    695 +**Example:**
    696 +```
    697 +https://coach-atlas.vercel.app/chat?mode=chat&theme=dark&embedded=true
    698 +```
    699 +
    700 +### 6.2 Programmatic Configuration
    701 +
    702 +```typescript
    703 +// Send config from native to web
    704 +webView.injectJavaScript(`
    705 +  window.postMessage(JSON.stringify({
    706 +    type: 'CONFIG_UPDATE',
    707 +    payload: {
    708 +      provider: 'anthropic',
    709 +      model: 'claude-sonnet-4-5',
    710 +      apiKey: '${apiKey}',
    711 +      theme: 'dark'
    712 +    }
    713 +  }), '*');
    714 +`);
    715 +```
    716 +
    717 +---
    718 +
    719 +## 7. Security Considerations
    720 +
    721 +### 7.1 API Key Handling
    722 +
    723 +| Approach | Security | Recommendation |
    724 +|----------|----------|----------------|
    725 +| Store in WebView localStorage | Medium | OK for BYOK model |
    726 +| Pass via URL parameter | ❌ Low | Never do this |
    727 +| Pass via native bridge | ✅ High | Best for managed keys |
    728 +| Store in native Keychain/Keystore | ✅ Highest | Best security |
    729 +
    730 +### 7.2 Secure Bridge Implementation
    731 +
    732 +```typescript
    733 +// Only accept messages from trusted origins
    734 +window.addEventListener('message', (event) => {
    735 +  // Verify origin
    736 +  if (event.origin !== 'https://coach-atlas.vercel.app') {
    737 +    console.warn('Rejected message from untrusted origin:', event.origin);
    738 +    return;
    739 +  }
    740 +
    741 +  // Process message
    742 +  handleNativeMessage(event.data);
    743 +});
    744 +```
    745 +
    746 +### 7.3 Content Security Policy
    747 +
    748 +```html
    749 +<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="
    750 +  default-src 'self';
    751 +  script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval';
    752 +  style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline';
    753 +  connect-src 'self'
    754 +    https://api.openai.com
    755 +    https://api.anthropic.com
    756 +    https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com;
    757 +  img-src 'self' data: blob:;
    758 +">
    759 +```
    760 +
    761 +---
    762 +
    763 +## 8. Performance Optimization
    764 +
    765 +### 8.1 Preloading
    766 +
    767 +```typescript
    768 +// React Native: Preload WebView
    769 +const PreloadedWebView = () => {
    770 +  const [loaded, setLoaded] = useState(false);
    771 +
    772 +  useEffect(() => {
    773 +    // Preload in background
    774 +    Image.prefetch('https://coach-atlas.vercel.app');
    775 +  }, []);
    776 +
    777 +  return (
    778 +    <WebView
    779 +      source={{ uri: 'https://coach-atlas.vercel.app' }}
    780 +      onLoadEnd={() => setLoaded(true)}
    781 +      style={{ opacity: loaded ? 1 : 0 }}
    782 +    />
    783 +  );
    784 +};
    785 +```
    786 +
    787 +### 8.2 Caching
    788 +
    789 +```typescript
    790 +// Enable aggressive caching
    791 +webView.settings.cacheMode = WebSettings.LOAD_CACHE_ELSE_NETWORK;
    792 +```
    793 +
    794 +### 8.3 Bundle Optimization
    795 +
    796 +Coach Atlas optimizes for WebView with:
    797 +- Code splitting (route-level)
    798 +- Lazy loading (Mermaid, KaTeX)
    799 +- Compressed assets (gzip)
    800 +- Service Worker caching
    801 +
    802 +**Target Metrics:**
    803 +- Initial load: < 2s
    804 +- Bundle size: < 500KB gzipped
    805 +- Time to interactive: < 3s
    806 +
    807 +---
    808 +
    809 +## 9. Troubleshooting
    810 +
    811 +### 9.1 Common Issues
    812 +
    813 +| Issue | Cause | Solution |
    814 +|-------|-------|----------|
    815 +| Blank screen | JavaScript disabled | Enable `javaScriptEnabled` |
    816 +| API calls fail | CORS | Check provider CORS headers |
    817 +| Storage not working | DOM storage disabled | Enable `domStorageEnabled` |
    818 +| Keyboard covers input | No safe area | Implement keyboard avoidance |
    819 +| Slow performance | No caching | Enable WebView cache |
    820 +| Dark theme flash | Light default | Set WebView background color |
    821 +
    822 +### 9.2 Debug Mode
    823 +
    824 +```typescript
    825 +// Enable debug logging
    826 +if (__DEV__) {
    827 +  const originalPostMessage = webView.postMessage;
    828 +  webView.postMessage = (message) => {
    829 +    console.log('[WebView OUT]', message);
    830 +    originalPostMessage(message);
    831 +  };
    832 +}
    833 +```
    834 +
    835 +### 9.3 Testing Checklist
    836 +
    837 +- [ ] App loads in WebView
    838 +- [ ] Chat functionality works
    839 +- [ ] Markdown renders correctly
    840 +- [ ] Code blocks syntax highlighted
    841 +- [ ] Share button works
    842 +- [ ] Copy button works
    843 +- [ ] Settings persist
    844 +- [ ] Safe area respected
    845 +- [ ] Keyboard handling works
    846 +- [ ] Back button handled
    847 +
    848 +---
    849 +
    850 +## Appendix: Sample Apps
    851 +
    852 +### A. Minimal React Native App
    853 +
    854 +```bash
    855 +# Create new React Native project
    856 +npx react-native init CoachAtlasApp
    857 +cd CoachAtlasApp
    858 +
    859 +# Install WebView
    860 +npm install react-native-webview
    861 +
    862 +# iOS setup
    863 +cd ios && pod install && cd ..
    864 +
    865 +# Run
    866 +npx react-native run-ios
    867 +npx react-native run-android
    868 +```
    869 +
    870 +### B. Deploy Your Own Instance
    871 +
    872 +```bash
    873 +# Fork and clone
    874 +git clone https://github.com/PrakharMNNIT/coach-atlas.git
    875 +cd coach-atlas
    876 +
    877 +# Install dependencies
    878 +npm install
    879 +
    880 +# Build for production
    881 +npm run build
    882 +
    883 +# Deploy to Vercel
    884 +npx vercel
    885 +```
    886 +
    887 +---
    888 +
    889 +**Document History**
    890 +

    892 +|---------|------|--------|---------|

    894

@@ -0,0 +1,53 @@
      1 +# LLD-001: Screaming Architecture & Module Structure
      2 +
      3 +**Status**: Approved
      4 +**Date**: 2024-12-22
      5 +**Author**: AntiGravity (Principal SDE)
      6 +**Context**: The current structure is "Lovable" boilerplate (flat components). For a production-ready application, we need a scalable "Screaming Architecture" that clearly separates features, services, and shared UI.
      7 +
      8 +## 1. Directory Structure
      9 +
     10 +We will move from `src/components/*` to a Feature-based architecture.
     11 +
     12 +```text
     13 +src/
     14 +├── app/                    # App-wide setup
     15 +│   ├── App.tsx             # Root component
     16 +│   ├── main.tsx            # Entry point
     17 +│   ├── providers.tsx       # Global providers (Query, Theme, AI)
     18 +│   └── router.tsx          # Route definitions
     19 +├── features/               # Feature Modules (SCREAMING ARCHITECTURE)
     20 +│   ├── chat/               # The Core Chat Feature
     21 +│   │   ├── components/     # Chat-specific UI (MessageBubble, Input)
     22 +│   │   ├── hooks/          # Chat logic (useChatStream)
     23 +│   │   └── ChatPage.tsx    # Page Entry
     24 +│   ├── tutorials/          # Tutorial Mode
     25 +│   ├── interview/          # Interview Mode
     26 +│   └── settings/           # Settings Feature
     27 +├── shared/                 # Shared across features
     28 +│   ├── ui/                 # Atomic UI (shadcn/ui buttons, cards)
     29 +│   ├── layouts/            # Layout components (MainLayout, Sidebar)
     30 +│   └── utils/              # Pure utility functions
     31 +├── services/               # Core Business Logic (Singleton/Class-based)
     32 +│   ├── ai/                 # AI Service (OpenAI, Anthropic wrappers)
     33 +│   ├── storage/            # IndexedDB / LocalStorage wrappers
     34 +│   └── bridge/             # WebView Bridge Service
     35 +├── lib/                    # Heavy external integrations
     36 +│   └── markdown-viewer/    # The ported Markdown Engine (ARD-001)
     37 +├── assets/                 # Static assets
     38 +└── types/                  # Global TS types
     39 +```
     40 +
     41 +## 2. Rules
     42 +
     43 +1.  **Strict Boundaries**: `server` code (if any) never touches `ui`. `shared` never imports from `features`.
     44 +2.  **Feature Isolation**: A feature should contain everything it needs. `features/chat` has its own components.
     45 +3.  **UI Library**: `shared/ui` is strictly for dumb, presentational components (shadcn/ui).
     46 +4.  **Service Layer**: All side-effects (API calls, DB writes) happen in `services/`, not inside React components.
     47 +
     48 +## 3. Migration Plan (Phase 1)
     49 +1.  Create the new directory structure.
     50 +2.  Move `src/components/ui` -> `src/shared/ui`.
     51 +3.  Move `src/pages/Chat.tsx` -> `src/features/chat/ChatPage.tsx`.
     52 +4.  Move `src/pages/Settings.tsx` -> `src/features/settings/SettingsPage.tsx`.
     53 +5.  Refactor imports.
     54  

```
