**Type:** Documentation 📖

```diff
@@ -0,0 +1,61 @@
      1 +# LLD-002: Service Layer Abstraction
      2 +
      3 +**Status**: Approved
      4 +**Date**: 2024-12-22
      5 +**Author**: AntiGravity (Principal SDE)
      6 +**Context**: API calls and DB logic are currently mixed into React components (`Chat.tsx` calling `fetch`). This violates clean architecture, makes testing impossible, and breaks with WebView limitations.
      7 +
      8 +## 1. Architecture
      9 +
     10 +We will implement a **Service-Repository Pattern** adapted for the Client-Side.
     11 +
     12 +```mermaid
     13 +graph TD
     14 +    UI[React Components] --> Hooks[Custom Hooks]
     15 +    Hooks --> Context[React Context Providers]
     16 +    Context --> Services[Service Classes (Singleton)]
     17 +    Services --> APIs[External APIs / DB]
     18 +```
     19 +
     20 +## 2. The Services
     21 +
     22 +We will define these core services in `src/services/`:
     23 +
     24 +### 2.1 `AIService` (Polymorphic)
     25 +*   **Interface**: `sendMessage(messages: Message[], config: Config): Promise<Stream<string>>`
     26 +*   **Adapters**: `OpenAIAdapter`, `AnthropicAdapter`, `GoogleAdapter`.
     27 +*   **Responsibility**: Handles raw HTTP requests, error parsing, and stream transformation. **BYOK logic lives here.**
     28 +
     29 +### 2.2 `StorageService` (Repository)
     30 +*   **Technology**: `Dexie.js` (IndexedDB).
     31 +*   **Repositories**:
     32 +    *   `ConversationRepository`: Save/Load chats.
     33 +    *   `SettingsRepository`: Save/Load API keys (encrypted/safe storage).
     34 +*   **Responsibility**: Abstract the specific DB technology. Allow swapping `localStorage` for `IndexedDB` seamlessly.
     35 +
     36 +### 2.3 `BridgeService` (WebView)
     37 +*   **Responsibility**: Handle `window.postMessage` communication with native apps.
     38 +*   **Signals**: `onTokenUpdate`, `onNavigation`, `onShare`.
     39 +
     40 +## 3. React Integration
     41 +
     42 +Services are **Pure TypeScript Classes** (no React). They are injected via **React Context**.
     43 +
     44 +```tsx
     45 +// src/app/providers.tsx
     46 +const aiService = new AIService();
     47 +const storageService = new StorageService();
     48 +
     49 +export function AppProviders({ children }) {
     50 +  return (
     51 +    <ServicesContext.Provider value={{ aiService, storageService }}>
     52 +      {children}
     53 +    </ServicesContext.Provider>
     54 +  )
     55 +}
     56 +```
     57 +
     58 +## 4. Why?
     59 +*   **Testability**: We can unit test `AIService` without rendering React components.
     60 +*   **Portability**: The same services can be used in a React Native implementation later.
     61 +*   **Separation**: `ChatPage.tsx` focuses on UI state, not `fetch` error handling.
     62  

```


### ✨ `docs/lld/persistence-strategy.md` **[ADDED]**

**Status:** ✅ **NEW FILE** - This file has been newly created

**Type:** Documentation 📖

```diff
@@ -0,0 +1,740 @@
      1 +# Coach Atlas - Chat Persistence Strategy
      2 +
      3 +**Document Version**: 1.0
      4 +**Date**: 2024-12-22
      5 +**Status**: Approved
      6 +**Pattern**: Offline-First with IndexedDB
      7 +
      8 +---
      9 +
     10 +## Executive Summary
     11 +
     12 +This document defines how Coach Atlas stores chat history and context persistently, even when the web app is closed. The strategy uses **IndexedDB** (via Dexie.js) for unlimited, structured, offline-first storage that is completely free and privacy-respecting.
     13 +
     14 +---
     15 +
     16 +## Why IndexedDB over localStorage?
     17 +
     18 +| Feature | localStorage | IndexedDB |
     19 +|---------|-------------|-----------|
     20 +| Storage Limit | ~5MB | ~50% of disk (100s of MB) |
     21 +| Data Structure | Key-value strings only | Complex objects, arrays |
     22 +| Querying | Manual parsing | Indexed queries |
     23 +| Performance | Synchronous (blocks UI) | Asynchronous (non-blocking) |
     24 +| Offline Support | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes |
     25 +| Free | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes |
     26 +| Privacy | ✅ Device-only | ✅ Device-only |
     27 +
     28 +**Verdict**: IndexedDB is the professional choice for any app with significant data.
     29 +
     30 +---
     31 +
     32 +## Library Choice: Dexie.js
     33 +
     34 +[Dexie.js](https://dexie.org/) wraps IndexedDB with a clean, Promise-based API.
     35 +
     36 +```bash
     37 +npm install dexie
     38 +```
     39 +
     40 +**Why Dexie?**
     41 +- Zero configuration
     42 +- TypeScript-first
     43 +- Reactive queries (live updates)
     44 +- 15KB gzipped (tiny footprint)
     45 +- Battle-tested (millions of users)
     46 +
     47 +---
     48 +
     49 +## Database Schema
     50 +
     51 +### Schema Design
     52 +
     53 +```typescript
     54 +// src/lib/db/schema.ts
     55 +import Dexie, { type Table } from 'dexie';
     56 +
     57 +export interface Conversation {
     58 +  id?: number;            // Auto-increment primary key
     59 +  title: string;          // "Two Sum Problem" or auto-generated
     60 +  mode: 'chat' | 'interview' | 'tutorial';
     61 +  provider: string;       // 'openai', 'anthropic', etc.
     62 +  model: string;          // 'gpt-4o', 'claude-sonnet-4-5'
     63 +  createdAt: Date;
     64 +  updatedAt: Date;
     65 +  messageCount: number;
     66 +  summary?: string;       // AI-generated summary of conversation
     67 +  tags?: string[];        // ['arrays', 'two-pointer']
     68 +  starred?: boolean;      // User bookmark
     69 +}
     70 +
     71 +export interface Message {
     72 +  id?: number;            // Auto-increment primary key
     73 +  conversationId: number; // Foreign key to Conversation
     74 +  role: 'user' | 'assistant' | 'system';
     75 +  content: string;        // Full message content (markdown)
     76 +  timestamp: Date;
     77 +  tokens?: number;        // Token count (for analytics)
     78 +  metadata?: {
     79 +    model?: string;
     80 +    finishReason?: string;
     81 +    latency?: number;     // Response time in ms
     82 +  };
     83 +}
     84 +
     85 +export interface Settings {
     86 +  id: string;             // 'config' (singleton)
     87 +  provider: string;
     88 +  model: string;
     89 +  credentials: Record<string, string>;
     90 +  theme: 'dark' | 'light';
     91 +  preferences: {
     92 +    autoSave: boolean;
     93 +    streamingEnabled: boolean;
     94 +    markdownEnabled: boolean;
     95 +  };
     96 +}
     97 +
     98 +export class CoachAtlasDB extends Dexie {
     99 +  conversations!: Table<Conversation>;
    100 +  messages!: Table<Message>;
    101 +  settings!: Table<Settings>;
    102 +
    103 +  constructor() {
    104 +    super('coach-atlas');
    105 +
    106 +    this.version(1).stores({
    107 +      conversations: '++id, mode, provider, createdAt, updatedAt, *tags',
    108 +      messages: '++id, conversationId, role, timestamp',
    109 +      settings: 'id'
    110 +    });
    111 +  }
    112 +}
    113 +
    114 +export const db = new CoachAtlasDB();
    115 +```
    116 +
    117 +### Index Explanation
    118 +
    119 +| Table | Index | Purpose |
    120 +|-------|-------|---------|
    121 +| conversations | `++id` | Auto-increment primary key |
    122 +| conversations | `mode` | Filter by chat/interview/tutorial |
    123 +| conversations | `provider` | Filter by AI provider |
    124 +| conversations | `createdAt` | Sort by date |
    125 +| conversations | `*tags` | Multi-entry index for tag search |
    126 +| messages | `conversationId` | Fetch all messages for a chat |
    127 +| messages | `timestamp` | Sort messages chronologically |
    128 +
    129 +---
    130 +
    131 +## Data Access Layer
    132 +
    133 +### Conversation Operations
    134 +
    135 +```typescript
    136 +// src/lib/db/conversations.ts
    137 +import { db, type Conversation } from './schema';
    138 +
    139 +export const conversations = {
    140 +  // Create new conversation
    141 +  async create(data: Omit<Conversation, 'id' | 'createdAt' | 'updatedAt' | 'messageCount'>): Promise<number> {
    142 +    return db.conversations.add({
    143 +      ...data,
    144 +      createdAt: new Date(),
    145 +      updatedAt: new Date(),
    146 +      messageCount: 0
    147 +    });
    148 +  },
    149 +
    150 +  // Get all conversations (sorted by recent)
    151 +  async getAll(): Promise<Conversation[]> {
    152 +    return db.conversations
    153 +      .orderBy('updatedAt')
    154 +      .reverse()
    155 +      .toArray();
    156 +  },
    157 +
    158 +  // Get conversation by ID
    159 +  async getById(id: number): Promise<Conversation | undefined> {
    160 +    return db.conversations.get(id);
    161 +  },
    162 +
    163 +  // Update conversation
    164 +  async update(id: number, changes: Partial<Conversation>): Promise<void> {
    165 +    await db.conversations.update(id, {
    166 +      ...changes,
    167 +      updatedAt: new Date()
    168 +    });
    169 +  },
    170 +
    171 +  // Delete conversation and its messages
    172 +  async delete(id: number): Promise<void> {
    173 +    await db.transaction('rw', db.conversations, db.messages, async () => {
    174 +      await db.messages.where('conversationId').equals(id).delete();
    175 +      await db.conversations.delete(id);
    176 +    });
    177 +  },
    178 +
    179 +  // Search conversations
    180 +  async search(query: string): Promise<Conversation[]> {
    181 +    const lowerQuery = query.toLowerCase();
    182 +    return db.conversations
    183 +      .filter(conv =>
    184 +        conv.title.toLowerCase().includes(lowerQuery) ||
    185 +        conv.summary?.toLowerCase().includes(lowerQuery) ||
    186 +        conv.tags?.some(tag => tag.toLowerCase().includes(lowerQuery))
    187 +      )
    188 +      .toArray();
    189 +  },
    190 +
    191 +  // Get by tag
    192 +  async getByTag(tag: string): Promise<Conversation[]> {
    193 +    return db.conversations.where('tags').equals(tag).toArray();
    194 +  },
    195 +
    196 +  // Get starred
    197 +  async getStarred(): Promise<Conversation[]> {
    198 +    return db.conversations.filter(conv => conv.starred === true).toArray();
    199 +  }
    200 +};
    201 +```
    202 +
    203 +### Message Operations
    204 +
    205 +```typescript
    206 +// src/lib/db/messages.ts
    207 +import { db, type Message, conversations } from './schema';
    208 +
    209 +export const messages = {
    210 +  // Add message to conversation
    211 +  async add(conversationId: number, data: Omit<Message, 'id' | 'conversationId' | 'timestamp'>): Promise<number> {
    212 +    const id = await db.messages.add({
    213 +      ...data,
    214 +      conversationId,
    215 +      timestamp: new Date()
    216 +    });
    217 +
    218 +    // Update conversation metadata
    219 +    const conv = await db.conversations.get(conversationId);
    220 +    if (conv) {
    221 +      await db.conversations.update(conversationId, {
    222 +        messageCount: conv.messageCount + 1,
    223 +        updatedAt: new Date()
    224 +      });
    225 +    }
    226 +
    227 +    return id;
    228 +  },
    229 +
    230 +  // Get all messages for conversation
    231 +  async getByConversation(conversationId: number): Promise<Message[]> {
    232 +    return db.messages
    233 +      .where('conversationId')
    234 +      .equals(conversationId)
    235 +      .sortBy('timestamp');
    236 +  },
    237 +
    238 +  // Get last N messages (for context window)
    239 +  async getLastN(conversationId: number, n: number): Promise<Message[]> {
    240 +    const allMessages = await this.getByConversation(conversationId);
    241 +    return allMessages.slice(-n);
    242 +  },
    243 +
    244 +  // Delete message
    245 +  async delete(id: number): Promise<void> {
    246 +    const message = await db.messages.get(id);
    247 +    if (message) {
    248 +      await db.messages.delete(id);
    249 +      const conv = await db.conversations.get(message.conversationId);
    250 +      if (conv) {
    251 +        await db.conversations.update(message.conversationId, {
    252 +          messageCount: Math.max(0, conv.messageCount - 1)
    253 +        });
    254 +      }
    255 +    }
    256 +  },
    257 +
    258 +  // Clear all messages in conversation
    259 +  async clearConversation(conversationId: number): Promise<void> {
    260 +    await db.messages.where('conversationId').equals(conversationId).delete();
    261 +    await db.conversations.update(conversationId, {
    262 +      messageCount: 0,
    263 +      updatedAt: new Date()
    264 +    });
    265 +  }
    266 +};
    267 +```
    268 +
    269 +### Settings Operations
    270 +
    271 +```typescript
    272 +// src/lib/db/settings.ts
    273 +import { db, type Settings } from './schema';
    274 +
    275 +const DEFAULT_SETTINGS: Settings = {
    276 +  id: 'config',
    277 +  provider: '',
    278 +  model: '',
    279 +  credentials: {},
    280 +  theme: 'dark',
    281 +  preferences: {
    282 +    autoSave: true,
    283 +    streamingEnabled: true,
    284 +    markdownEnabled: true
    285 +  }
    286 +};
    287 +
    288 +export const settings = {
    289 +  // Get settings (create default if not exists)
    290 +  async get(): Promise<Settings> {
    291 +    const existing = await db.settings.get('config');
    292 +    if (!existing) {
    293 +      await db.settings.add(DEFAULT_SETTINGS);
    294 +      return DEFAULT_SETTINGS;
    295 +    }
    296 +    return existing;
    297 +  },
    298 +
    299 +  // Update settings
    300 +  async update(changes: Partial<Omit<Settings, 'id'>>): Promise<void> {
    301 +    const existing = await this.get();
    302 +    await db.settings.put({
    303 +      ...existing,
    304 +      ...changes,
    305 +      id: 'config'
    306 +    });
    307 +  },
    308 +
    309 +  // Clear all settings
    310 +  async clear(): Promise<void> {
    311 +    await db.settings.delete('config');
    312 +  }
    313 +};
    314 +```
    315 +
    316 +---
    317 +
    318 +## React Hooks
    319 +
    320 +### useConversations Hook
    321 +
    322 +```typescript
    323 +// src/hooks/useConversations.ts
    324 +import { useLiveQuery } from 'dexie-react-hooks';
    325 +import { db } from '@/lib/db/schema';
    326 +import { conversations } from '@/lib/db/conversations';
    327 +
    328 +export function useConversations() {
    329 +  // Live query - automatically updates when data changes
    330 +  const allConversations = useLiveQuery(
    331 +    () => db.conversations.orderBy('updatedAt').reverse().toArray()
    332 +  );
    333 +
    334 +  return {
    335 +    conversations: allConversations ?? [],
    336 +    isLoading: allConversations === undefined,
    337 +    create: conversations.create,
    338 +    update: conversations.update,
    339 +    delete: conversations.delete,
    340 +    search: conversations.search
    341 +  };
    342 +}
    343 +```
    344 +
    345 +### useChat Hook
    346 +
    347 +```typescript
    348 +// src/hooks/useChat.ts
    349 +import { useState, useCallback } from 'react';
    350 +import { useLiveQuery } from 'dexie-react-hooks';
    351 +import { db } from '@/lib/db/schema';
    352 +import { messages } from '@/lib/db/messages';
    353 +import { conversations } from '@/lib/db/conversations';
    354 +
    355 +export function useChat(conversationId: number | null) {
    356 +  const [isLoading, setIsLoading] = useState(false);
    357 +  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
    358 +
    359 +  // Live query for messages
    360 +  const chatMessages = useLiveQuery(
    361 +    () => conversationId
    362 +      ? db.messages.where('conversationId').equals(conversationId).sortBy('timestamp')
    363 +      : [],
    364 +    [conversationId]
    365 +  );
    366 +
    367 +  // Live query for conversation metadata
    368 +  const conversation = useLiveQuery(
    369 +    () => conversationId ? db.conversations.get(conversationId) : undefined,
    370 +    [conversationId]
    371 +  );
    372 +
    373 +  const sendMessage = useCallback(async (content: string) => {
    374 +    if (!conversationId) return;
    375 +
    376 +    setIsLoading(true);
    377 +    setError(null);
    378 +
    379 +    try {
    380 +      // Save user message
    381 +      await messages.add(conversationId, {
    382 +        role: 'user',
    383 +        content
    384 +      });
    385 +
    386 +      // Get AI response (implementation in useAI hook)
    387 +      // ...
    388 +
    389 +      // Save assistant message
    390 +      await messages.add(conversationId, {
    391 +        role: 'assistant',
    392 +        content: response,
    393 +        metadata: { model, latency }
    394 +      });
    395 +    } catch (err) {
    396 +      setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Failed to send message');
    397 +    } finally {
    398 +      setIsLoading(false);
    399 +    }
    400 +  }, [conversationId]);
    401 +
    402 +  return {
    403 +    messages: chatMessages ?? [],
    404 +    conversation,
    405 +    isLoading,
    406 +    error,
    407 +    sendMessage,
    408 +    clearMessages: () => conversationId && messages.clearConversation(conversationId)
    409 +  };
    410 +}
    411 +```
    412 +
    413 +---
    414 +
    415 +## Export/Import Functionality
    416 +
    417 +### Export to JSON
    418 +
    419 +```typescript
    420 +// src/lib/db/export.ts
    421 +import { db } from './schema';
    422 +
    423 +export async function exportAllData(): Promise<string> {
    424 +  const [convs, msgs, config] = await Promise.all([
    425 +    db.conversations.toArray(),
    426 +    db.messages.toArray(),
    427 +    db.settings.get('config')
    428 +  ]);
    429 +
    430 +  const exportData = {
    431 +    version: 1,
    432 +    exportedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
    433 +    conversations: convs,
    434 +    messages: msgs,
    435 +    settings: config
    436 +  };
    437 +
    438 +  return JSON.stringify(exportData, null, 2);
    439 +}
    440 +
    441 +export async function exportConversation(conversationId: number): Promise<string> {
    442 +  const [conv, msgs] = await Promise.all([
    443 +    db.conversations.get(conversationId),
    444 +    db.messages.where('conversationId').equals(conversationId).toArray()
    445 +  ]);
    446 +
    447 +  const exportData = {
    448 +    version: 1,
    449 +    exportedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
    450 +    conversation: conv,
    451 +    messages: msgs
    452 +  };
    453 +
    454 +  return JSON.stringify(exportData, null, 2);
    455 +}
    456 +
    457 +export function downloadJSON(data: string, filename: string) {
    458 +  const blob = new Blob([data], { type: 'application/json' });
    459 +  const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
    460 +  const a = document.createElement('a');
    461 +  a.href = url;
    462 +  a.download = filename;
    463 +  a.click();
    464 +  URL.revokeObjectURL(url);
    465 +}
    466 +```
    467 +
    468 +### Import from JSON
    469 +
    470 +```typescript
    471 +// src/lib/db/import.ts
    472 +import { db, type Conversation, type Message } from './schema';
    473 +
    474 +interface ImportData {
    475 +  version: number;
    476 +  conversations?: Conversation[];
    477 +  messages?: Message[];
    478 +  conversation?: Conversation;
    479 +}
    480 +
    481 +export async function importData(jsonString: string): Promise<{
    482 +  conversations: number;
    483 +  messages: number;
    484 +}> {
    485 +  const data: ImportData = JSON.parse(jsonString);
    486 +
    487 +  let conversationCount = 0;
    488 +  let messageCount = 0;
    489 +
    490 +  await db.transaction('rw', db.conversations, db.messages, async () => {
    491 +    // Handle full export format
    492 +    if (data.conversations) {
    493 +      for (const conv of data.conversations) {
    494 +        const { id, ...convData } = conv;
    495 +        await db.conversations.add(convData as Conversation);
    496 +        conversationCount++;
    497 +      }
    498 +    }
    499 +
    500 +    if (data.messages) {
    501 +      for (const msg of data.messages) {
    502 +        const { id, ...msgData } = msg;
    503 +        await db.messages.add(msgData as Message);
    504 +        messageCount++;
    505 +      }
    506 +    }
    507 +
    508 +    // Handle single conversation format
    509 +    if (data.conversation) {
    510 +      const { id, ...convData } = data.conversation;
    511 +      const newId = await db.conversations.add(convData as Conversation);
    512 +      conversationCount++;
    513 +
    514 +      if (data.messages) {
    515 +        for (const msg of data.messages) {
    516 +          await db.messages.add({
    517 +            ...msg,
    518 +            conversationId: newId
    519 +          } as Message);
    520 +          messageCount++;
    521 +        }
    522 +      }
    523 +    }
    524 +  });
    525 +
    526 +  return { conversations: conversationCount, messages: messageCount };
    527 +}
    528 +```
    529 +
    530 +---
    531 +
    532 +## Context Restoration Flow
    533 +
    534 +### How Context is Restored When Opening a Past Chat
    535 +
    536 +```
    537 +┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    538 +│                   User Opens App                         │
    539 +└─────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘
    540 +                      ▼
    541 +┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    542 +│  1. Load conversation list from IndexedDB               │
    543 +│     (useLiveQuery: db.conversations.orderBy...)         │
    544 +└─────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘
    545 +                      ▼
    546 +┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    547 +│  2. User clicks on past conversation                    │
    548 +│     (conversationId selected)                           │
    549 +└─────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘
    550 +                      ▼
    551 +┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    552 +│  3. Fetch all messages for conversation                 │
    553 +│     (db.messages.where('conversationId').equals(id))    │
    554 +└─────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘
    555 +                      ▼
    556 +┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    557 +│  4. Display messages in chat UI                         │
    558 +│     (Messages render with markdown)                     │
    559 +└─────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘
    560 +                      ▼
    561 +┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    562 +│  5. When user sends new message:                        │
    563 +│     - Get last N messages for context                   │
    564 +│     - Send to AI with conversation history              │
    565 +│     - AI has full context to continue                   │
    566 +└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    567 +```
    568 +
    569 +### Context Window Management
    570 +
    571 +```typescript
    572 +// src/lib/ai/context.ts
    573 +import { messages } from '@/lib/db/messages';
    574 +import type { Message } from '@/lib/db/schema';
    575 +
    576 +const MAX_CONTEXT_MESSAGES = 20;
    577 +const MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS = 8000; // Leave room for response
    578 +
    579 +export async function buildContextMessages(
    580 +  conversationId: number,
    581 +  systemPrompt: string
    582 +): Promise<Array<{ role: string; content: string }>> {
    583 +  // Get recent messages
    584 +  const recentMessages = await messages.getLastN(conversationId, MAX_CONTEXT_MESSAGES);
    585 +
    586 +  // Build context array
    587 +  const context = [
    588 +    { role: 'system', content: systemPrompt }
    589 +  ];
    590 +
    591 +  // Add messages, respecting token limit
    592 +  let totalTokens = estimateTokens(systemPrompt);
    593 +
    594 +  for (const msg of recentMessages) {
    595 +    const msgTokens = estimateTokens(msg.content);
    596 +    if (totalTokens + msgTokens > MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS) break;
    597 +
    598 +    context.push({
    599 +      role: msg.role,
    600 +      content: msg.content
    601 +    });
    602 +    totalTokens += msgTokens;
    603 +  }
    604 +
    605 +  return context;
    606 +}
    607 +
    608 +function estimateTokens(text: string): number {
    609 +  // Rough estimate: 1 token ≈ 4 characters
    610 +  return Math.ceil(text.length / 4);
    611 +}
    612 +```
    613 +
    614 +---
    615 +
    616 +## Storage Quota Management
    617 +
    618 +```typescript
    619 +// src/lib/db/quota.ts
    620 +export async function checkStorageQuota(): Promise<{
    621 +  used: number;
    622 +  available: number;
    623 +  percentUsed: number;
    624 +}> {
    625 +  if (navigator.storage && navigator.storage.estimate) {
    626 +    const estimate = await navigator.storage.estimate();
    627 +    const used = estimate.usage ?? 0;
    628 +    const available = estimate.quota ?? 0;
    629 +
    630 +    return {
    631 +      used,
    632 +      available,
    633 +      percentUsed: available > 0 ? (used / available) * 100 : 0
    634 +    };
    635 +  }
    636 +
    637 +  return { used: 0, available: 0, percentUsed: 0 };
    638 +}
    639 +
    640 +export async function cleanOldConversations(keepDays: number = 30): Promise<number> {
    641 +  const cutoffDate = new Date();
    642 +  cutoffDate.setDate(cutoffDate.getDate() - keepDays);
    643 +
    644 +  const oldConversations = await db.conversations
    645 +    .where('updatedAt')
    646 +    .below(cutoffDate)
    647 +    .filter(conv => !conv.starred) // Don't delete starred
    648 +    .toArray();
    649 +
    650 +  let deletedCount = 0;
    651 +
    652 +  for (const conv of oldConversations) {
    653 +    if (conv.id) {
    654 +      await db.messages.where('conversationId').equals(conv.id).delete();
    655 +      await db.conversations.delete(conv.id);
    656 +      deletedCount++;
    657 +    }
    658 +  }
    659 +
    660 +  return deletedCount;
    661 +}
    662 +```
    663 +
    664 +---
    665 +
    666 +## Migration from localStorage
    667 +
    668 +For users who have existing data in localStorage:
    669 +
    670 +```typescript
    671 +// src/lib/db/migrate.ts
    672 +import { db } from './schema';
    673 +import { loadConfig, clearConfig } from '@/lib/providers';
    674 +
    675 +export async function migrateFromLocalStorage(): Promise<boolean> {
    676 +  const oldConfig = loadConfig();
    677 +
    678 +  if (oldConfig) {
    679 +    await db.settings.put({
    680 +      id: 'config',
    681 +      provider: oldConfig.provider,
    682 +      model: oldConfig.model,
    683 +      credentials: oldConfig.credentials,
    684 +      theme: 'dark',
    685 +      preferences: {
    686 +        autoSave: true,
    687 +        streamingEnabled: true,
    688 +        markdownEnabled: true
    689 +      }
    690 +    });
    691 +
    692 +    // Clear old localStorage after migration
    693 +    clearConfig();
    694 +
    695 +    return true;
    696 +  }
    697 +
    698 +  return false;
    699 +}
    700 +```
    701 +
    702 +---
    703 +

    710 +├── messages.ts        # Message CRUD operations

    721 +
    722 +## Benefits Summary
    723 +
    724 +| Benefit | Description |
    725 +|---------|-------------|
    726 +| **Offline-First** | View all past chats without internet |
    727 +| **Private** | Data never leaves the device |
    728 +| **Fast** | Async operations, no UI blocking |
    729 +| **Unlimited** | 100s of MB vs 5MB localStorage |
    730 +| **Structured** | Query by date, tags, starred status |
    731 +| **Exportable** | Backup to JSON anytime |
    732 +| **Reactive** | UI auto-updates with Dexie live queries |

      4 +**Approver**: AntiGravity (Principal SDE)

      6 +
      7 +## Context
      8 +We are upgrading a "Lovable" boilerplate prototype into a production-ready "Screaming Architecture" (LLD-001).

     10 +## Objectives
     11 +1.  Structure the codebase according to `docs/lld/001-module-architecture.md`.
     12 +2.  Enable **Strict Type Safety**.

     14 +
     15 +## Detailed Steps

     18 +- [ ] Create `src/app`, `src/features`, `src/shared`, `src/services`, `src/lib`.

@@ -0,0 +1,297 @@
      1 +# Coach Atlas - Active Context
      2 +
      3 +## Current Session Focus
      4 +
      5 +**Date**: 2024-12-22
      6 +**Objective**: Complete Sr Principal SDE code review, identify gaps, create implementation plan
      7 +
      8 +## Recent Analysis Summary
      9 +
     10 +### Code Review Findings (Critical Issues)
     11 +
     12 +#### 1. **Chat.tsx - Production Gaps**
     13 +
     14 +| Issue | Severity | Location | Impact |
     15 +|-------|----------|----------|--------|
     16 +| No streaming support | High | `callOpenAI`, `callAnthropic`, `callGoogle` | Poor UX, long wait times |
     17 +| No markdown rendering | Critical | Message display | Raw markdown shown to users |
     18 +| No error retry logic | Medium | API calls | Failed requests not retried |
     19 +| No conversation persistence | High | State management | Chat lost on refresh |
     20 +| AWS Bedrock not functional | Medium | `handleSend` switch | Provider unusable |
     21 +| No rate limiting | Medium | API calls | Risk of API abuse/costs |
     22 +| No input sanitization | High | User input | XSS vulnerability potential |
     23 +
     24 +#### 2. **Settings.tsx - Validation Gaps**
     25 +
     26 +| Issue | Severity | Impact |
     27 +|-------|----------|--------|
     28 +| No API key validation | High | Users don't know if key is valid until chat |
     29 +| No model availability check | Medium | Selected model may not be accessible |
     30 +| No credential encryption | Medium | Keys stored in plain text |
     31 +
     32 +#### 3. **Index.tsx (Landing Page) - Completeness**
     33 +
     34 +| Issue | Severity | Impact |
     35 +|-------|----------|--------|
     36 +| ChatInterface is demo only | Medium | Misleading users |
     37 +| Sign In/Get Started non-functional | Low | UI elements do nothing |
     38 +| No actual navigation from feature cards | Low | Dead-end interactions |
     39 +
     40 +#### 4. **System Prompt - Underutilized**
     41 +
     42 +The excellent system prompt in Chat.tsx is underutilized:
     43 +- No mode switching (Interview vs Tutorial)
     44 +- No structured output parsing
     45 +- No context awareness for follow-ups
     46 +- No escalating hint system implementation
     47 +
     48 +### Architectural Gaps
     49 +
     50 +1. **No Error Boundaries** - App can crash on render errors
     51 +2. **No Loading Skeletons** - Jarring content pops
     52 +3. **No Virtualization** - Long conversations will lag
     53 +4. **No Code Splitting** - Single bundle loaded
     54 +5. **No Service Worker** - No offline capability
     55 +6. **No Analytics** - No usage insights
     56 +7. **No A11y Implementation** - WCAG not addressed
     57 +
     58 +### Missing Features (Per BRD Requirements)
     59 +
     60 +| Feature | Status | Priority |
     61 +|---------|--------|----------|
     62 +| Markdown rendering in chat | ❌ Missing | P0 |
     63 +| Syntax highlighting | ❌ Missing | P0 |
     64 +| Mermaid diagrams | ❌ Missing | P1 |
     65 +| KaTeX math rendering | ❌ Missing | P2 |
     66 +| Streaming responses | ❌ Missing | P0 |
     67 +| Chat history persistence | ❌ Missing | P0 |
     68 +| Tutorial mode | ❌ Missing | P1 |
     69 +| Interview mode toggle | ❌ Missing | P1 |
     70 +| Export functionality | ❌ Missing | P2 |
     71 +| WebView compatibility | ❌ Missing | P1 |
     72 +
     73 +## Markdown Viewer Pro Integration Plan
     74 +
     75 +### Repository Analysis
     76 +From https://github.com/PrakharMNNIT/markdown-viewer-app:
     77 +
     78 +**Key Features to Port:**
     79 +1. Real-time markdown preview
     80 +2. 12 themes (6 base × 2 variants)
     81 +3. PrismJS syntax highlighting (20+ languages)
     82 +4. Mermaid diagram support
     83 +5. KaTeX math rendering
     84 +6. Export to HTML/PDF
     85 +7. Custom theme builder
     86 +
     87 +**Integration Strategy:**
     88 +```
     89 +Option A: Extract Core Modules
     90 +- Copy markdown rendering logic
     91 +- Copy Prism + Mermaid initialization
     92 +- Adapt themes to Tailwind
     93 +- Bundle size impact: ~150KB
     94 +
     95 +Option B: Create Shared Package
     96 +- Publish @coach-atlas/markdown-renderer
     97 +- Import in both projects
     98 +- Maintain separately
     99 +- Bundle size impact: ~100KB (tree-shaken)
    100 +
    101 +Option C: WebView Hybrid (RECOMMENDED)
    102 +- Use Markdown Viewer Pro as iframe/WebView for tutorials
    103 +- Use simplified markdown for chat bubbles
    104 +- Best of both worlds
    105 +- Bundle size impact: ~50KB in main app
    106 +```
    107 +
    108 +### Files to Port from Markdown Viewer Pro
    109 +
    110 +```
    111 +From: markdown-viewer-app/src/js/
    112 +├── markdown/
    113 +│   ├── parser.js      → src/lib/markdown/parser.ts
    114 +│   ├── renderer.js    → src/lib/markdown/renderer.ts
    115 +│   └── sanitizer.js   → src/lib/markdown/sanitizer.ts
    116 +├── syntax/
    117 +│   └── prism-init.js  → src/lib/syntax/prism.ts
    118 +├── diagrams/
    119 +│   └── mermaid-init.js→ src/lib/diagrams/mermaid.ts
    120 +└── math/
    121 +    └── katex-init.js  → src/lib/math/katex.ts
    122 +
    123 +From: markdown-viewer-app/themes/
    124 +└── *.css              → src/styles/markdown-themes/
    125 +```
    126 +
    127 +## Open Questions
    128 +
    129 +1. **Should tutorials open in full-screen mode?** - Like Markdown Viewer Pro's Zen mode
    130 +2. **Should we implement conversation branching?** - Fork from any message
    131 +3. **Should code execution be supported?** - Run code snippets (security implications)
    132 +4. **How to handle very long tutorials?** - Virtual scrolling vs pagination
    133 +
    134 +## Immediate Next Steps
    135 +
    136 +1. Create comprehensive BRD document
    137 +2. Create implementation plan with phases
    138 +3. Set up proper project structure
    139 +4. Install missing dependencies
    140 +5. Implement markdown rendering component
    141 +6. Add streaming support to Chat
    142 +
    143 +## Technical Decisions Made
    144 +
    145 +| Decision | Rationale | Date |
    146 +|----------|-----------|------|
    147 +| Use Option C for Markdown integration | Minimal main bundle, full features for tutorials | 2024-12-22 |
    148 +| Add Vitest over Jest | Faster, native ESM, Vite integration | 2024-12-22 |
    149 +| Use marked + DOMPurify over react-markdown | Better performance, more control | 2024-12-22 |
    150 +| Add Error Boundaries at route level | Graceful degradation | 2024-12-22 |
    151 +
    152 +## Blockers
    153 +
    154 +1. **npm install failing** - Need to run `npm install` to fix missing node_modules
    155 +2. **No memory-bank existed** - Created fresh (this session)
    156 +3. **TypeScript strict mode off** - Will cause refactoring when enabled
    157 +
    158 +## Team Roles & Workflow
    159 +
    160 +### AntiGravity (Principal SDE)
    161 +- **Role**: Architect, Reviewer, Approver.
    162 +- **Responsibilities**:
    163 +    - Define Architecture & Schemas.
    164 +    - Review PRs/Codebase against Standards.
    165 +    - Identify Security & Performance Risks.
    166 +    - **No Code Implementation**.
    167 +
    168 +### Cline (Senior Developer)
    169 +- **Role**: Implementer.
    170 +- **Responsibilities**:
    171 +    - Write Code & Tests.
    172 +    - Execute Implementation Plans.
    173 +    - manage Dependencies.
    174 +
    175 +## Current Focus
    176 +We are currently in the **Planning & Architecture Refinement** phase.
    177 +## Current Working Branch
    178 +
    179 +- Main branch: `main`
    180 +- Latest commit: `a2452178b19233efa03063d5ce1bcd37ff122f13`
    181 +- Status: Needs significant development work
    182 +
    183 +## Session Notes
    184 +
    185 +- Project scaffolded via Lovable.dev
    186 +- 40+ shadcn/ui components pre-installed (many unused)
    187 +- System prompt is excellent, needs implementation support
    188 +- Landing page is polished, functionality is incomplete
    189 +- WebView compatibility will be straightforward (static SPA)
    190 +
    191 +---
    192 +
    193 +## Sr Principal SDE Evaluation: Gemini/Antigravity Plan
    194 +
    195 +### Document Reviewed
    196 +`/Users/praxlannister/.gemini/antigravity/brain/c287e139-10e4-4803-87d6-10279b216575/implementation_plan.md.resolved`
    197 +
    198 +### Overall Assessment: ✅ APPROVED with Minor Enhancements
    199 +
    200 +The Gemini plan is **solid, well-structured, and production-ready**. It correctly identifies the critical gaps and proposes sensible solutions.
    201 +
    202 +### Strengths
    203 +| Aspect | Assessment |
    204 +|--------|------------|
    205 +| Phase ordering | ✅ Correct - Visual first, then persistence |
    206 +| Markdown stack | ✅ `react-markdown` + `remark-gfm` + `rehype-highlight` is industry standard |
    207 +| Persistence | ✅ IndexedDB via Dexie.js is the right choice |
    208 +| WebView bridge | ✅ `postMessage` protocol is correct |
    209 +| Security | ✅ TypeScript strict mode is essential |
    210 +
    211 +### Recommendations (Enhancements)
    212 +
    213 +| Item | Gemini Plan | My Addition | Priority |
    214 +|------|-------------|-------------|----------|
    215 +| Markdown lib | `react-markdown` | Consider `marked` for smaller bundle | P2 |
    216 +| Math support | `rehype-katex` | ✅ Agreed | P2 |
    217 +| Diagrams | `mermaid` | Add lazy loading (heavy lib) | P1 |
    218 +| History UI | Sidebar | Add search + tags + starred | P2 |
    219 +| Export | JSON only | Add Markdown export too | P2 |
    220 +| Streaming | Not mentioned | Add streaming for all providers | P0 |
    221 +
    222 +### Key Agreements
    223 +1. **IndexedDB + Dexie.js** - Correct choice for offline-first persistence
    224 +2. **AIProvider abstraction** - Essential for clean architecture
    225 +3. **WebView bridge** - `postMessage` protocol is standard
    226 +4. **TypeScript strict** - Non-negotiable for production
    227 +
    228 +### Reconciled Implementation Order
    229 +
    230 +```
    231 +Phase 1: Visual Learning (Gemini) → Core Chat (Cline)
    232 +├── MarkdownRenderer component
    233 +├── Code syntax highlighting (Prism/rehype-highlight)
    234 +├── Mermaid diagrams (lazy loaded)
    235 +├── Typography styling
    236 +
    237 +Phase 2: WebView (Gemini) + Streaming (Cline)
    238 +├── vite.config.ts base path
    239 +├── useWebViewBridge hook
    240 +├── Streaming for OpenAI, Anthropic, Google
    241 +├── Progressive markdown rendering
    242 +
    243 +Phase 3: Architecture (Gemini) + Error Handling (Cline)
    244 +├── AIProvider abstraction
    245 +├── TypeScript strict mode
    246 +├── Error boundaries
    247 +├── Loading skeletons
    248 +
    249 +Phase 4: Guided Discovery UI (Gemini)
    250 +├── Hint vs Solution styling
    251 +├── Interview mode toggle
    252 +├── Tutorial mode detection
    253 +
    254 +Phase 5: Persistence (Gemini) + Export (Cline)
    255 +├── Dexie.js schema
    256 +├── Conversation/Message storage
    257 +├── History sidebar with search
    258 +├── Export to JSON + Markdown
    259 +├── localStorage migration
    260 +
    261 +Phase 6: Testing & Polish (Cline)
    262 +├── Vitest setup (85% coverage)
    263 +├── E2E tests (Cypress)
    264 +├── Accessibility audit
    265 +├── Performance optimization
    266 +```
    267 +
    268 +### Final Verdict
    269 +
    270 +**The Gemini plan and my analysis are ~90% aligned.** The main additions I recommend:
    271 +
    272 +1. **Streaming responses** - Critical P0 missing from Gemini plan
    273 +2. **Markdown export** - Users want `.md` files, not just JSON
    274 +3. **Lazy loading Mermaid** - 500KB+ library needs code splitting
    275 +4. **Search/filter for history** - Essential UX for many conversations
    276 +
    277 +Both plans can be executed together. I recommend starting with **Phase 1: Visual Learning** as Gemini suggests, since the chat needs to look good before we worry about persistence.
    278 +
    279 +---
    280 +
    281 +## Persistence Strategy Summary
    282 +
    283 +**Technology**: IndexedDB via Dexie.js (free, unlimited, offline-first)
    284 +
    285 +**Schema**:
    286 +- `conversations`: id, title, mode, provider, createdAt, tags, starred
    287 +- `messages`: id, conversationId, role, content, timestamp, metadata
    288 +- `settings`: id, provider, model, credentials, preferences
    289 +
    290 +**Key Features**:
    291 +- Live queries (UI auto-updates)
    292 +- Context restoration (load last N messages for AI)
    293 +- Export/Import JSON
    294 +- Storage quota management
    295 +- localStorage migration
    296 +
    297 +**Documentation**: `docs/03-database/persistence-strategy.md`
    298

@@ -0,0 +1,157 @@
      1 +# Coach Atlas - Product Context
      2 +
      3 +## Problem Statement
      4 +
      5 +### The Pain
      6 +Software engineers preparing for technical interviews face several critical challenges:
      7 +
      8 +1. **Memorization Over Understanding** - Most resources focus on memorizing solutions rather than building problem-solving skills
      9 +2. **No Real Feedback** - Self-study provides no honest assessment of skill gaps
     10 +3. **Fragmented Resources** - Interview prep is scattered across LeetCode, YouTube, blogs, and books
     11 +4. **Non-Production Code** - Examples are often pseudo-code that doesn't run in real jobs
     12 +5. **No Guided Learning Path** - Random problem solving without structured progression
     13 +6. **Expensive Coaching** - Human interview coaches cost $100-500/hour
     14 +
     15 +### The Opportunity
     16 +AI models have become capable enough to:
     17 +- Conduct Socratic questioning that builds understanding
     18 +- Provide honest, detailed feedback on approaches
     19 +- Generate comprehensive tutorials with working code
     20 +- Simulate interview scenarios with realistic follow-ups
     21 +- Adapt difficulty based on demonstrated skill level
     22 +
     23 +## Value Proposition
     24 +
     25 +> **"Your AI technical mentor that builds problem solvers through guided discovery and brutally honest feedback."**
     26 +
     27 +### For Interview Candidates
     28 +- Get personalized coaching at any time, any topic
     29 +- Build real problem-solving skills, not memorization
     30 +- Receive honest assessment with specific improvement paths
     31 +- Practice system design with visual diagrams
     32 +- Generate study materials tailored to your gaps
     33 +
     34 +### For Educators
     35 +- Create comprehensive tutorials with minimal effort
     36 +- Get production-ready code examples instantly
     37 +- Generate visual aids (diagrams, flowcharts)
     38 +- Export content for student distribution
     39 +
     40 +## Target Users
     41 +
     42 +### Primary Persona: "Anxious Alex"
     43 +- **Role**: Software Engineer (2-5 years experience)
     44 +- **Goal**: Land a job at FAANG/top-tier company
     45 +- **Pain**: Failed interviews due to poor problem-solving approach, not lack of knowledge
     46 +- **Behavior**: Studies 2-3 hours daily, feels stuck on hard problems
     47 +- **Needs**: Guided approach that builds confidence and skill simultaneously
     48 +
     49 +### Secondary Persona: "Teaching Taylor"
     50 +- **Role**: Bootcamp Instructor / University TA
     51 +- **Goal**: Create high-quality learning materials efficiently
     52 +- **Pain**: Spends hours creating tutorials that become outdated quickly
     53 +- **Behavior**: Constantly updating curriculum, needs fresh examples
     54 +- **Needs**: Fast tutorial generation with modern, correct code
     55 +
     56 +### Tertiary Persona: "Self-Learner Sam"
     57 +- **Role**: Career Changer / Student
     58 +- **Goal**: Learn technical concepts deeply without expensive courses
     59 +- **Pain**: YouTube tutorials are shallow, books are overwhelming
     60 +- **Behavior**: Learns best through interactive Q&A
     61 +- **Needs**: Patient mentor who adapts to their level
     62 +
     63 +## User Experience Goals
     64 +
     65 +### Chat Experience
     66 +1. **Immediate Value** - First response provides actionable insight
     67 +2. **Beautiful Rendering** - Code, diagrams, and math look professional
     68 +3. **Guided Flow** - Questions lead user to discovery, not answers
     69 +4. **Responsive** - Works perfectly on mobile/tablet/desktop
     70 +5. **Persistent** - Conversations saved locally, resumable
     71 +
     72 +### Tutorial Experience
     73 +1. **Structured Output** - Clear sections: concept, examples, practice, interview tips
     74 +2. **Progressive Complexity** - Beginner → Intermediate → Advanced in one tutorial
     75 +3. **Visual Learning** - Diagrams, flowcharts, state machines where applicable
     76 +4. **Exportable** - Download as markdown, PDF, or share link
     77 +
     78 +### Interview Practice Experience
     79 +1. **Realistic Pressure** - Timed sessions with interviewer-style follow-ups
     80 +2. **Hint Escalation** - Hints progress from subtle to direct
     81 +3. **Post-Mortem** - Detailed breakdown of what went well/poorly
     82 +4. **Pattern Recognition** - Links problems to broader patterns
     83 +
     84 +## User Flows
     85 +
     86 +### Flow 1: First-Time Setup
     87 +```
     88 +Landing Page → Configure API Key → Select Provider/Model → Save → Start Chat
     89 +```
     90 +
     91 +### Flow 2: Interview Practice
     92 +```
     93 +Chat → "Help me with Two Sum" → Guided Questions → User Attempts →
     94 +Feedback → Hints if Stuck → Solution Discussion → Pattern Identification →
     95 +Related Problems Suggestion
     96 +```
     97 +
     98 +### Flow 3: Tutorial Creation
     99 +```
    100 +Chat → "TUTORIAL: Binary Search" → Structured Tutorial Generated →
    101 +View in Formatted Markdown → Export/Copy → Save to Collection
    102 +```
    103 +
    104 +### Flow 4: System Design
    105 +```
    106 +Chat → "Design a URL Shortener" → Requirements Gathering →
    107 +Capacity Estimation → API Design → Data Model → Architecture →
    108 +Trade-offs Discussion → Scaling Considerations → Visual Diagrams
    109 +```
    110 +
    111 +## Success Criteria & KPIs
    112 +
    113 +| KPI | Target | Measurement Method |
    114 +|-----|--------|-------------------|
    115 +| User Engagement | 15+ min avg session | Session duration tracking |
    116 +| Tutorial Completeness | 95% structured sections | Content analysis |
    117 +| Return Rate | 60% return within 7 days | User tracking (local) |
    118 +| Error-Free Sessions | 99.9% | Error logging |
    119 +| Mobile Usage | 30%+ sessions | Viewport analytics |
    120 +
    121 +## Competitive Landscape
    122 +
    123 +### Direct Competitors
    124 +| Product | Strength | Weakness | Our Differentiation |
    125 +|---------|----------|----------|---------------------|
    126 +| ChatGPT | General purpose | No interview focus | Specialized prompts, guided discovery |
    127 +| LeetCode Premium | Problem library | No coaching | Personalized guidance |
    128 +| Pramp | Peer practice | Human availability | Available 24/7, consistent quality |
    129 +| InterviewCake | Structured content | Static, not adaptive | Dynamic, conversational |
    130 +
    131 +### Our Moat
    132 +1. **Ultimate Prompt** - Highly refined system prompt for interview coaching
    133 +2. **Markdown Viewer Pro Integration** - Superior content rendering
    134 +3. **Multi-Provider** - Not locked to one AI vendor
    135 +4. **WebView Ready** - Easy mobile integration without app stores
    136 +
    137 +## Ethical Considerations
    138 +
    139 +### Honesty
    140 +- AI clearly identifies as AI, not human coach
    141 +- Limitations acknowledged (can make mistakes, no guarantees)
    142 +- Feedback is constructive but honest, not falsely encouraging
    143 +
    144 +### Privacy
    145 +- No data collection beyond local storage
    146 +- API keys never leave the browser
    147 +- No analytics that identify individuals
    148 +
    149 +### Accessibility
    150 +- Screen reader support for all features
    151 +- Color blindness considerations in themes
    152 +- Keyboard navigation throughout
    153 +
    154 +### Fairness
    155 +- Free to use (BYOK model)
    156 +- No paywalled features
    157 +- Open source (if decided)
    158  

```

@@ -0,0 +1,129 @@
      1 +# Coach Atlas - Project Brief
      2 +
      3 +## Executive Summary
      4 +
      5 +Coach Atlas is an AI-powered technical interview mentor and comprehensive tutorial creator. The platform combines guided discovery teaching with brutally honest feedback to build problem solvers, not solution memorizers.
      6 +
      7 +## Core Mission
      8 +
      9 +**"Build real problem solvers through guided discovery and honest feedback."**
     10 +
     11 +Transform how engineers prepare for technical interviews by providing:
     12 +1. Socratic method-based interview coaching
     13 +2. Production-ready tutorial generation
     14 +3. Real-time AI conversation with formatted markdown display
     15 +4. Multi-provider AI support (BYOK model)
     16 +
     17 +## Strategic Objectives
     18 +
     19 +### Primary Goals
     20 +1. **Interview Excellence** - Help engineers ace coding, system design, and behavioral interviews
     21 +2. **Deep Understanding** - Teach concepts through guided discovery, not rote memorization
     22 +3. **Production Readiness** - All code and examples are job-ready, not academic abstractions
     23 +4. **Honest Assessment** - Provide brutally honest skill gap analysis with realistic timelines
     24 +
     25 +### Secondary Goals
     26 +1. **Multi-Platform Access** - Web, WebView (mobile integration), standalone desktop
     27 +2. **Provider Flexibility** - Support multiple AI providers without vendor lock-in
     28 +3. **Beautiful Content Display** - Rich markdown rendering with syntax highlighting, diagrams, and math
     29 +4. **Tutorial Export** - Generate shareable, professional tutorials
     30 +
     31 +## Acceptance Criteria for "Done"
     32 +
     33 +### MVP Completion Criteria
     34 +- [ ] Fully functional chat with all 4 AI providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Bedrock)
     35 +- [ ] Markdown rendering with syntax highlighting in chat
     36 +- [ ] Mermaid diagram support for system design
     37 +- [ ] Tutorial mode with structured output
     38 +- [ ] Interview mode with guided discovery flow
     39 +- [ ] Settings persistence and validation
     40 +- [ ] Responsive design for all screen sizes
     41 +- [ ] WebView-compatible for mobile app integration
     42 +- [ ] Error handling with graceful degradation
     43 +- [ ] Loading states and optimistic UI
     44 +
     45 +### Production Criteria
     46 +- [ ] Test coverage ≥ 85%
     47 +- [ ] Lighthouse performance score ≥ 90
     48 +- [ ] Accessibility audit passed (WCAG 2.1 AA)
     49 +- [ ] Security audit passed (no exposed secrets, XSS protection)
     50 +- [ ] Zero known bugs in critical paths
     51 +- [ ] Documentation complete (user guide, API docs, architecture)
     52 +
     53 +## Project Scope
     54 +
     55 +### In Scope
     56 +1. Chat interface with AI providers
     57 +2. Markdown content rendering (via Markdown Viewer Pro integration)
     58 +3. Interview coaching mode
     59 +4. Tutorial creation mode
     60 +5. Settings/configuration management
     61 +6. Local storage persistence
     62 +7. WebView compatibility layer
     63 +8. Export functionality (tutorials)
     64 +
     65 +### Out of Scope (Future Phases)
     66 +1. User authentication/accounts
     67 +2. Cloud sync of conversations
     68 +3. Team/enterprise features
     69 +4. Custom AI model fine-tuning
     70 +5. Voice/audio interactions
     71 +6. Native mobile apps (using WebView instead)
     72 +
     73 +## Success Metrics
     74 +
     75 +| Metric | Target | Measurement |
     76 +|--------|--------|-------------|
     77 +| Chat Response Time | < 3s perceived | First token to render |
     78 +| Tutorial Generation | < 30s | Complete structured output |
     79 +| User Session Duration | > 15 min | Analytics |
     80 +| Error Rate | < 0.1% | Error logging |
     81 +| Mobile WebView Compat | 100% | Cross-device testing |
     82 +
     83 +## Non-Functional Requirements
     84 +
     85 +### Performance
     86 +- Initial load: < 2s on 3G
     87 +- Chat response streaming: immediate (first token)
     88 +- Markdown render: < 100ms
     89 +- Bundle size: < 500KB gzipped
     90 +
     91 +### Security
     92 +- API keys stored locally only (never transmitted to backend)
     93 +- Direct client-to-provider communication
     94 +- CSP headers configured
     95 +- No sensitive data in URL parameters
     96 +
     97 +### Accessibility
     98 +- WCAG 2.1 AA compliance
     99 +- Keyboard navigation support
    100 +- Screen reader compatible
    101 +- High contrast mode support
    102 +
    103 +### Scalability
    104 +- Stateless architecture (client-side only)
    105 +- CDN-deployable static assets
    106 +- No backend scaling concerns (BYOK model)
    107 +
    108 +## Key Stakeholders
    109 +
    110 +- **Primary Users**: Software engineers preparing for technical interviews
    111 +- **Secondary Users**: Educators, bootcamp instructors, self-learners
    112 +- **Technical Owner**: Development team
    113 +- **Product Owner**: PrakharMNNIT

@@ -0,0 +1,269 @@
      1 +# Coach Atlas - System Patterns & Architecture
      2 +
      3 +## System Architecture Overview
      4 +
      5 +```
      6 +┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
      7 +│                           Client Browser                                 │
      8 +├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
      9 +│  ┌─────────────┐  ┌─────────────┐  ┌─────────────┐  ┌─────────────┐    │
     10 +│  │   Pages     │  │ Components  │  │   Hooks     │  │    Lib      │    │
     11 +│  │  - Index    │  │  - Hero     │  │  - useMobile│  │  - providers│    │
     12 +│  │  - Chat     │  │  - Chat     │  │  - useToast │  │  - utils    │    │
     13 +│  │  - Settings │  │  - Features │  │  - useChat* │  │  - markdown*│    │
     14 +│  │  - NotFound │  │  - UI (40+) │  │  - useStream│  │  - storage  │    │
     15 +│  └─────────────┘  └─────────────┘  └─────────────┘  └─────────────┘    │
     16 +├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
     17 +│                         State Management                                 │
     18 +│  ┌─────────────────┐  ┌─────────────────┐  ┌─────────────────┐         │
     19 +│  │  React Query    │  │  Local State    │  │  LocalStorage   │         │
     20 +│  │  (API caching)  │  │  (UI state)     │  │  (persistence)  │         │
     21 +│  └─────────────────┘  └─────────────────┘  └─────────────────┘         │
     22 +└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
     23 +                                    │
     24 +                                    │ Direct API Calls (HTTPS)
     25 +                                    ▼
     26 +┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
     27 +│                        External AI Providers                             │
     28 +│  ┌───────────┐  ┌───────────┐  ┌───────────┐  ┌───────────┐            │
     29 +│  │  OpenAI   │  │ Anthropic │  │  Google   │  │  Bedrock  │            │
     30 +│  │  GPT-4/5  │  │  Claude   │  │  Gemini   │  │  (Future) │            │
     31 +│  └───────────┘  └───────────┘  └───────────┘  └───────────┘            │
     32 +└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
     33 +```
     34 +
     35 +## Design Patterns
     36 +
     37 +### 1. Provider Pattern (AI Providers)
     38 +```typescript
     39 +// Current Implementation in src/lib/providers.ts
     40 +interface ProviderConfig {
     41 +  id: Provider;
     42 +  name: string;
     43 +  description: string;
     44 +  models: Model[];
     45 +  fields: Field[];
     46 +}
     47 +
     48 +// Pattern: Strategy Pattern for API calls
     49 +interface AIProvider {
     50 +  call(messages: Message[], config: Config): Promise<Response>;
     51 +  stream(messages: Message[], config: Config): AsyncGenerator<string>;
     52 +  validateCredentials(credentials: Record<string, string>): boolean;
     53 +}
     54 +```
     55 +
     56 +### 2. Component Architecture
     57 +```
     58 +┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
     59 +│                   Page Layer                     │
     60 +│  (Route-level components with data fetching)    │
     61 +├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
     62 +│                 Feature Layer                    │
     63 +│  (Domain-specific composed components)          │
     64 +├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
     65 +│                    UI Layer                      │
     66 +│  (shadcn/ui primitives, design system)          │
     67 +└─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
     68 +```
     69 +
     70 +### 3. State Management Pattern
     71 +```
     72 +┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
     73 +│              React Query (Server State)          │
     74 +│  - API responses                                 │
     75 +│  - Caching & invalidation                        │
     76 +│  - Background refetch                            │
     77 +├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
     78 +│              React State (UI State)              │
     79 +│  - Form inputs                                   │
     80 +│  - Modal open/close                              │
     81 +│  - Local UI interactions                         │
     82 +├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
     83 +│              LocalStorage (Persistence)          │
     84 +│  - API credentials                               │
     85 +│  - Chat history                                  │
     86 +│  - User preferences                              │
     87 +└─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
     88 +```
     89 +
     90 +## Data Flow
     91 +
     92 +### Chat Message Flow
     93 +```
     94 +User Input → Message Object → Provider Selection → API Call →
     95 +Stream/Response → Markdown Parse → Render → Persist to LocalStorage
     96 +```
     97 +
     98 +### Settings Flow
     99 +```
    100 +User Selection → Form State → Validation → LocalStorage →
    101 +Config Context → Available to Chat
    102 +```
    103 +
    104 +## Domain Boundaries
    105 +
    106 +### 1. Chat Domain
    107 +- **Responsibility**: Message handling, conversation management
    108 +- **Components**: ChatInterface, MessageBubble, InputArea
    109 +- **State**: Messages array, loading, error, streaming status
    110 +- **Persistence**: LocalStorage (chat history)
    111 +
    112 +### 2. Provider Domain
    113 +- **Responsibility**: AI provider abstraction, API calls
    114 +- **Components**: None (pure logic)
    115 +- **State**: Provider config, credentials
    116 +- **Persistence**: LocalStorage (credentials)
    117 +
    118 +### 3. Markdown Domain (NEW - Markdown Viewer Pro Integration)
    119 +- **Responsibility**: Content rendering, syntax highlighting, diagrams
    120 +- **Components**: MarkdownRenderer, CodeBlock, MermaidDiagram
    121 +- **State**: Render mode, theme
    122 +- **Dependencies**: PrismJS, Mermaid, KaTeX
    123 +
    124 +### 4. Tutorial Domain (NEW)
    125 +- **Responsibility**: Structured content generation, export
    126 +- **Components**: TutorialView, TutorialExport, TableOfContents
    127 +- **State**: Tutorial structure, export format
    128 +- **Persistence**: LocalStorage (saved tutorials)
    129 +
    130 +## Error Handling Strategy
    131 +
    132 +### Error Types
    133 +```typescript
    134 +enum ErrorType {
    135 +  NETWORK = 'network',
    136 +  API_AUTH = 'api_auth',
    137 +  API_RATE_LIMIT = 'api_rate_limit',
    138 +  API_CONTENT = 'api_content',
    139 +  VALIDATION = 'validation',
    140 +  STORAGE = 'storage',
    141 +  RENDER = 'render'
    142 +}
    143 +
    144 +interface AppError {
    145 +  type: ErrorType;
    146 +  message: string;
    147 +  recoverable: boolean;
    148 +  action?: () => void;
    149 +}
    150 +```
    151 +
    152 +### Error Boundaries
    153 +```
    154 +App Error Boundary (crash recovery)
    155 +  └─ Route Error Boundary (page-level)
    156 +      └─ Feature Error Boundary (chat, tutorial)
    157 +          └─ Component Error Boundary (markdown render)
    158 +```
    159 +
    160 +## Inter-Component Communication
    161 +
    162 +### Event Patterns
    163 +1. **Props Down, Events Up** - Standard React pattern
    164 +2. **Context for Cross-Cutting** - Theme, config, providers
    165 +3. **Custom Events for WebView** - Bridge to native app
    166 +
    167 +### WebView Communication Protocol
    168 +```typescript
    169 +interface WebViewBridge {
    170 +  // From React to Native
    171 +  postMessage(type: string, payload: any): void;
    172 +
    173 +  // From Native to React
    174 +  onMessage(handler: (event: MessageEvent) => void): void;
    175 +}
    176 +
    177 +// Message Types
    178 +type WebViewMessage =
    179 +  | { type: 'SHARE_CONTENT', payload: { content: string, format: 'md' | 'pdf' } }
    180 +  | { type: 'COPY_CODE', payload: { code: string } }
    181 +  | { type: 'OPEN_EXTERNAL', payload: { url: string } }
    182 +  | { type: 'CONFIG_UPDATE', payload: StoredConfig };
    183 +```
    184 +
    185 +## Scalability Considerations
    186 +
    187 +### Bundle Optimization
    188 +- **Code Splitting**: Route-level lazy loading
    189 +- **Tree Shaking**: Only import used UI components
    190 +- **Dynamic Imports**: Heavy libraries (Mermaid, KaTeX) loaded on demand
    191 +
    192 +### Performance Patterns
    193 +- **Virtualization**: Long message lists
    194 +- **Debouncing**: Input handling, resize events
    195 +- **Memoization**: Markdown render cache
    196 +- **Streaming**: SSE for real-time responses
    197 +
    198 +## Security Architecture
    199 +
    200 +### API Key Protection
    201 +```
    202 +┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
    203 +│           Browser Environment            │
    204 +│  ┌───────────────────────────────────┐  │
    205 +│  │        LocalStorage               │  │
    206 +│  │  - Encrypted at rest (AES-256)    │  │
    207 +│  │  - Never included in URLs         │  │
    208 +│  │  - Never sent to our servers      │  │
    209 +│  └───────────────────────────────────┘  │
    210 +│                    │                     │
    211 +│                    ▼                     │
    212 +│  ┌───────────────────────────────────┐  │
    213 +│  │    Direct HTTPS to Providers      │  │
    214 +│  │  - TLS 1.3                        │  │
    215 +│  │  - Certificate pinning (WebView)  │  │
    216 +│  └───────────────────────────────────┘  │
    217 +└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
    218 +```
    219 +
    220 +### Content Security
    221 +- **XSS Prevention**: DOMPurify for markdown HTML
    222 +- **CSP Headers**: Restrict script sources
    223 +- **Input Validation**: Sanitize all user inputs
    224 +
    225 +## Testing Strategy
    226 +
    227 +### Test Pyramid
    228 +```
    229 +        ┌─────────┐
    230 +        │   E2E   │  (10%)
    231 +        │ Cypress │
    232 +        ├─────────┤
    233 +       │Integration│ (30%)
    234 +       │ Component │
    235 +       ├───────────┤
    236 +      │    Unit    │ (60%)
    237 +      │   Vitest   │
    238 +      └────────────┘
    239 +```
    240 +
    241 +### Critical Path Tests
    242 +1. API configuration flow
    243 +2. Chat send/receive
    244 +3. Markdown rendering
    245 +4. Error handling
    246 +5. LocalStorage persistence
    247 +6. WebView bridge communication
    248 +
    249 +## Module Dependencies
    250 +
    251 +```
    252 +src/
    253 +├── pages/          # Entry points
    254 +│   └── depends on: components, hooks, lib
    255 +├── components/
    256 +│   ├── ui/         # No external deps (shadcn primitives)
    257 +│   └── feature/    # Depends on: ui, hooks, lib
    258 +├── hooks/          # Depends on: lib
    259 +├── lib/            # Zero deps (utilities only)
    260 +└── types/          # Zero deps (type definitions)
    261 +```
    262 +
    263 +## Future Architecture (Phase 2)
    264 +
    265 +### Planned Additions
    266 +1. **Worker Thread** - Markdown parsing off main thread
    267 +2. **IndexedDB** - Large conversation storage
    268 +3. **Service Worker** - Offline capability
    269 +4. **WebRTC** - Voice interaction (future)
    270  

```

    256 +## Deployment Architecture

    232 +## **🎯 High-Tech Engineering Standards**
    233 +
    234 +### **1. Code Excellence**
    235 +
    236 +**Principles:**
    237 +
    238 +- Code is **clean**, **self-documenting**, **modular**, and **idiomatic**
    239 +- Apply **SOLID**, **DRY**, **KISS**, and **YAGNI** consistently
    240 +- Favor **composition over inheritance**, **immutability over mutation**
    241 +- Every abstraction must have clear purpose and pay for its complexity
    242 +- No dead code, commented-out logic, or TODOs in production branches
    243 +
    244 +**Standards:**
    245 +
    246 +- Functions have single responsibility and minimal side effects
    247 +- Naming reveals intent without ambiguity
    248 +- Cyclomatic complexity kept minimal (<10 per function)
    249 +- Comments explain **why**, not **what**
    250 +- Code passes all static analysis with zero warnings
    251 +
    252 +---
    253 +
    254 +### **2. Architecture & Design**
    255 +
    256 +**Principles:**
    257 +
    258 +- **Separation of concerns** across all layers
    259 +- **Explicit dependencies** with inversion of control
    260 +- **Domain-driven design** where appropriate
    261 +- **API-first thinking** for all interfaces
    262 +- **Data immutability** and pure transformation functions
    263 +
    264 +**Standards:**
    265 +
    266 +- Clear boundaries between presentation, business logic, and data layers
    267 +- No circular dependencies
    268 +- Interfaces define contracts, not implementations
    269 +- Scalable by default — design for 10x growth
    270 +- Every component can be tested in isolation
    271 +- Configuration separated from code
    272 +
    273 +---
    274 +
    275 +### **3. Testing & Validation**
    276 +
    277 +**Principles:**
    278 +
    279 +- **Test-first mindset** — tests define behavior
    280 +- **Deterministic tests** — no flakiness tolerated
    281 +- **Fast feedback loops** — tests run in seconds, not minutes
    282 +
    283 +**Coverage Requirements:**
    284 +
    285 +- **Unit tests:** ≥90% meaningful coverage of business logic
    286 +- **Integration tests:** All critical data flows and external boundaries
    287 +- **End-to-end tests:** Core user journeys and failure scenarios
    288 +- **Property-based tests:** For complex algorithms and invariants
    289 +- **Performance tests:** For SLO-critical paths
    290 +- **Security tests:** Input validation, authorization, injection attacks
    291 +
    292 +**Test Standards:**
    293 +
    294 +- Follow **Arrange-Act-Assert** pattern
    295 +- One assertion concept per test
    296 +- Tests are readable specifications
    297 +- Edge cases and error conditions explicitly covered
    298 +- No test interdependencies
    299 +- Tests serve as living documentation
    300 +
    301 +---
    302 +
    303 +### **4. Error Handling & Resilience**
    304 +
    305 +**Principles:**
    306 +
    307 +- **Fail fast, fail explicit** — no silent failures
    308 +- **Defensive programming** without paranoia
    309 +- **Graceful degradation** under adverse conditions
    310 +
    311 +**Standards:**
    312 +
    313 +- All error paths explicitly handled
    314 +- Use type-safe error handling (Result types, Either, exceptions with clear semantics)
    315 +- Errors contain actionable context
    316 +- Retry logic with exponential backoff for transient failures
    317 +- Circuit breakers for external dependencies
    318 +- Timeouts on all I/O operations
    319 +- Structured error logging with correlation IDs
    320 +

    322 +

    324 +
    325 +**Principles:**

    327 +- **Optimize for readability first, performance second** (except hot paths)
    328 +- **Measure before optimizing** — no premature optimization
    329 +- **Algorithmic efficiency** matters more than micro-optimizations
    330 +
    331 +**Standards:**
    332 +
    333 +- Analyze time and space complexity for all algorithms
    334 +- Profile critical paths under realistic load
    335 +- Establish performance baselines and SLOs
    336 +- Monitor resource utilization (CPU, memory, I/O, network)
    337 +- Avoid N+1 queries and redundant computations
    338 +- Design for horizontal scalability
    339 +- Cache intelligently with clear invalidation strategies
    340 +- Optimize for energy efficiency on client devices
    341 +
    342 +---
    343 +
    344 +### **6. Security & Privacy**
    345 +
    346 +**Principles:**
    347 +
    348 +- **Security by design**, not as afterthought
    349 +- **Principle of least privilege**
    350 +- **Defense in depth**
    351 +- **Privacy by default**
    352 +

    414 +**Principles:**

    418 +- **Boy scout rule** — leave code better than you found it

    428 +- Technical debt tracked and prioritized

    430 +- Target: **zero technical debt**

    432 +---

    475 +
    476 +---
    477 +
    478 +## **🎯 Operational Philosophy**
    479 +
    480 +> "No shortcuts. No regressions. No lost context."
    481 +
    482 +Cline's Memory Bank exists to ensure **continuity, quality, and craftsmanship**.
    483 +
    484 +After every session reset, I must reconstruct the complete mental model of the system and continue engineering **as if I never left** — without compromising on:
    485 +

    491 +- ✅ **Architectural integrity**
    492 +- ✅ **Operational excellence**
    493 +
    494 +### **Core Beliefs:**
    495 +
    496 +1. **Excellence is non-negotiable** — mediocre code costs more long-term than doing it right the first time
    497 +2. **Context is power** — well-maintained memory enables senior-level engineering at machine speed
    498 +3. **Standards prevent decay** — explicit guidelines prevent gradual quality erosion
    499 +4. **Documentation is investment** — future you (and your team) will thank present you
    500 +5. **Technical debt is optional** — with discipline and systems, zero debt is achievable
    501 +
    502 +---
    503 +
    504 +## **🚀 Success Metrics**
    505 +
    506 +A well-maintained Memory Bank enables:
    507 +
    508 +- ✅ **Zero onboarding time** for resumed work
