    5956 +### 📄 `script.js`
    5957 +
    5958 +**Type:** JavaScript Source File 🟨
    5959 +
    5960 +```diff
    5961 +@@ -354,6 +354,81 @@ function initializeApp() {
    5962 +354 354  
    5963 +355 355    // Initialize support widget (donation button in footer)
    5964 +356 356    initSupportWidget();
    5965 +    357 +
    5966 +    358 +  // Initialize support modal (one-time popup)
    5967 +    359 +  initSupportModal();
    5968 +    360 +}
    5969 +    361 +
    5970 +    362 +// ==================== SUPPORT MODAL (ONE-TIME POPUP) ====================
    5971 +    363 +const SUPPORT_MODAL_SHOWN_KEY = 'support_modal_shown';
    5972 +    364 +const SUPPORT_MODAL_DELAY_MS = 5000; // 5 seconds
    5973 +    365 +
    5974 +    366 +/**
    5975 +    367 + * Initialize support modal - shows once after 5 seconds
    5976 +    368 + */
    5977 +    369 +function initSupportModal() {
    5978 +    370 +  const modal = document.getElementById('support-modal');
    5979 +    371 +  const closeBtn = document.getElementById('close-support-modal');
    5980 +    372 +  const dontShowAgainCheckbox = document.getElementById('support-dont-show-again');
    5981 +    373 +
    5982 +    374 +  if (!modal || !closeBtn) {
    5983 +    375 +    console.warn('[SupportModal] Modal elements not found');
    5984 +    376 +    return;
    5985 +    377 +  }
    5986 +    378 +
    5987 +    379 +  // Check if already shown before
    5988 +    380 +  const alreadyShown = localStorage.getItem(SUPPORT_MODAL_SHOWN_KEY);
    5989 +    381 +  if (alreadyShown === 'true') {
    5990 +    382 +    console.log('[SupportModal] Already shown before, skipping');
    5991 +    383 +    return;
    5992 +    384 +  }
    5993 +    385 +
    5994 +    386 +  // Show modal after delay
    5995 +    387 +  setTimeout(() => {
    5996 +    388 +    modal.classList.add('active');
    5997 +    389 +    console.log('[SupportModal] Showing support modal');
    5998 +    390 +  }, SUPPORT_MODAL_DELAY_MS);
    5999 +    391 +
    6000 +    392 +  // Close button handler
    6001 +    393 +  closeBtn.addEventListener('click', () => {
    6002 +    394 +    closeSupportModal(modal, dontShowAgainCheckbox);
    6003 +    395 +  });
    6004 +    396 +
    6005 +    397 +  // Click outside to close
    6006 +    398 +  modal.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
    6007 +    399 +    if (e.target === modal) {
    6008 +    400 +      closeSupportModal(modal, dontShowAgainCheckbox);
    6009 +    401 +    }
    6010 +    402 +  });
    6011 +    403 +
    6012 +    404 +  // Escape key to close
    6013 +    405 +  document.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
    6014 +    406 +    if (e.key === 'Escape' && modal.classList.contains('active')) {
    6015 +    407 +      closeSupportModal(modal, dontShowAgainCheckbox);
    6016 +    408 +    }
    6017 +    409 +  });
    6018 +    410 +
    6019 +    411 +  // Track clicks on support options
    6020 +    412 +  modal.querySelectorAll('.support-option').forEach(option => {
    6021 +    413 +    option.addEventListener('click', () => {
    6022 +    414 +      // Mark as shown when user clicks a support option
    6023 +    415 +      localStorage.setItem(SUPPORT_MODAL_SHOWN_KEY, 'true');
    6024 +    416 +      console.log('[SupportModal] User clicked support option, marking as shown');
    6025 +    417 +    });
    6026 +    418 +  });
    6027 +    419 +}
    6028 +    420 +
    6029 +    421 +/**
    6030 +    422 + * Close the support modal
    6031 +    423 + */
    6032 +    424 +function closeSupportModal(modal, checkbox) {
    6033 +    425 +  modal.classList.remove('active');
    6034 +    426 +
    6035 +    427 +  // If "Don't show again" is checked, remember it
    6036 +    428 +  if (checkbox && checkbox.checked) {
    6037 +    429 +    localStorage.setItem(SUPPORT_MODAL_SHOWN_KEY, 'true');
    6038 +    430 +    console.log('[SupportModal] User opted out of future modals');
    6039 +    431 +  }
    6040 +357 432  }
    6041 +358 433  
    6042 +359 434  // ==================== SUPPORT WIDGET (DONATION ROUTER) ====================
    6043 +360 435  
    6044 +
    6045 +```

### ✨ `src/lib/external/markdown-viewer-app/CODE_REVIEW_AND_FINDINGS.md` **[ADDED]**

**Status:** ✅ **NEW FILE** - This file has been newly created

**Type:** Documentation 📖

```diff
@@ -0,0 +1,52 @@
      1 +# Code & Architecture Review: Export Services
      2 +
      3 +## 1. Code Review
      4 +
      5 +### PDFService (PDF Export)
      6 +- **Status:** ⚠️ Resolved Rendering Issue
      7 +- **Issue:** The `html2pdf` library (specifically `html2canvas`) crashed when parsing modern CSS `color-mix()` functions used in the UI (Glassmorphism).
      8 +- **Fix:** Refactored `style.css` to use solid color variables (`var(--bg-secondary)`) instead of `color-mix()` for elements involved in the export context (Buttons).
      9 +- **Quality:**
     10 +  - ✅ Clean separation of config (`buildHtml2PdfConfig`) and execution.
     11 +  - ✅ Robust validation of user inputs (margins, page size).
     12 +  - ⚠️ Dependency on global `html2pdf` (should be modular, but acceptable for this architecture).
     13 +
     14 +### HTMLService (HTML Export)
     15 +- **Status:** ✅ NEW Implementation
     16 +- **Issue:** Previous implementation was monolithic (inside `script.js`) and produced broken HTML (missing math styles, missing syntax highlighting dependencies).
     17 +- **Fix:** Created dedicated `HTMLService.js`.
     18 +  - Injects `katex.min.css` (CDN) for Math support.
     19 +  - Injects `prism-tomorrow.min.css` (CDN) for Code highlighting.
     20 +  - Injects Theme CSS properly.
     21 +- **Quality:**
     22 +  - ✅ Service-based architecture.
     23 +  - ✅ Generates standalone HTML blobs.
     24 +
     25 +## 2. Architectural Review
     26 +
     27 +### Service Layer
     28 +- **Pattern:** The application uses a "Service Class" pattern (`PDFService`, `MermaidService`, `HTMLService`) instantiated in the main controller (`script.js`).
     29 +- **Verdict:** Good. This keeps logic out of the global scope and allows for easier testing/mocking.
     30 +- **Recommendation:** `script.js` acts as a text-heavy "God Controller". Future refactoring should split `script.js` into `EditorController`, `PreviewController`, and `ToolbarController`.
     31 +
     32 +### CSS / Styling
     33 +- **Architecture:** CSS Variables (`:root`) used for Theming.
     34 +- **Issue:** Modern CSS (`color-mix`) caused compatibility issues with legacy tools (`html2canvas`).
     35 +- **Lesson:** When building "Export to PDF" features that rely on DOM parsing, avoid bleeding-edge CSS in exportable elements.
     36 +
     37 +## 3. UI/UX Review
     38 +
     39 +### PDF Export
     40 +- **Experience:** ⭐️ Premium.
     41 +- **Features:** Live Preview, Custom Margins, Page Size, Font Scale.
     42 +- **Feedback:** The glassmorphism and animations in the modal are visually pleasing.
     43 +
     44 +### HTML Export
     45 +- **Experience:** 😐 Functional.
     46 +- **Features:** "Click to Download".
     47 +- **Feedback:** Lacks a "Preview" or configuration (e.g., "Exclude CSS?").
     48 +- **Improvement:** Could add a simple modal to choose "Self-contained (Base64 images)" vs "Linked".
     49 +
     50 +## Summary of Findings
     51 +- **Critical Fix:** `color-mix` CSS removed to unblock PDF generation.
     52 +- **New Feature:** `HTMLService` ensures exported files render Math and Code correctly.
     53  

```

    846 +### Plain text / No highlighting
    847 +
    848 +```
    849 +This is plain text without syntax highlighting.
    850 +It preserves spacing and formatting.
    851 +    Indented text here.
    852 +```
    853 +
    854 +---
    855 +
    856 +## Math Syntax
    857 +
    858 +### 1️⃣ Inline Math – Basic & Edge Cases
    859 +
    860 +**Simple letters & numbers:** $a, b, c, 1, 2, 3$
    861 +
    862 +**Subscripts & superscripts (including nesting):** $x_i$, $y^{2}$, $z_{i}^{\,j}$, $a_{b_{c}}^{d^{e}}$
    863 +
    864 +**Euler's identity:** $e^{i\pi}+1=0$
    865 +
    866 +**Fractions inline:** $\frac{p}{q}$ and display-style inline: $\dfrac{a+b}{c+d}$, text-style: $\tfrac{x}{y}$
    867 +
    868 +**Binomial/choose notation:** $\binom{n}{k}$ and ${n \choose k}$
    869 +
    870 +**Roots with optional index:** $\sqrt{x}$, $\sqrt[3]{8}$, $\sqrt[n]{a}$
    871 +
    872 +**Greek letters:** $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta, \epsilon, \zeta, \eta, \theta, \iota, \kappa, \lambda, \mu$
    873 +
    874 +**Greek uppercase:** $\Gamma, \Delta, \Theta, \Lambda, \Xi, \Pi, \Sigma, \Phi, \Psi, \Omega$
    875 +
    876 +**Blackboard-bold sets:** $\mathbb{R}, \mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{N}, \mathbb{Q}, \mathbb{C}, \mathbb{H}$
    877 +
    878 +**Calligraphic, fraktur, script fonts:** $\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{L}, \mathfrak{g}, \mathfrak{S}, \mathscr{L}, \mathscr{H}$
    879 +
    880 +**Bold/italic/sans-serif in math:** $\mathbf{ABC}, \mathsf{ABC}, \mathit{ABC}, \mathrm{ABC}$
    881 +
    882 +**Accents:** $\hat{x}, \tilde{y}, \bar{z}, \dot{u}, \ddot{v}, \acute{a}, \grave{e}, \breve{o}, \check{c}$
    883 +
    884 +**Vectors & arrow notation:** $\vec{a}, \overrightarrow{AB}, \overleftarrow{CD}, \widehat{ABC}$
    885 +
    886 +**Over/under braces with annotations:**
    887 +
    888 +- $\overbrace{1+2+ \dots +n}^{\text{n terms}}$
    889 +- $\underbrace{a_1 + a_2 + \dots + a_n}_{\text{sum}}$
    890 +
    891 +**Strikethrough/cancel:** $\cancel{(x+y)}$, $\bcancel{abc}$, $\xcancel{xyz}$
    892 +
    893 +**Color in math:** $\color{red}{x^2} + \color{blue}{y^2} = \color{green}{z^2}$
    894 +
    895 +**Boxed expression:** $\boxed{E = mc^2}$
    896 +
    897 +**Multiple inline formulas on a single line (spacing test):**
    898 +The quadratic formula is $x = \frac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^{2}-4ac}}{2a}$ while the discriminant is $D = b^{2}-4ac$ and the roots satisfy $ax^{2}+bx+c=0$.
    899 +
    900 +---
    901 +
    902 +### 2️⃣ Display (Block) Math – Standard & Edge Cases
    903 +
    904 +#### 2.1 Simple displayed equations
    905 +
    906 +$$
    907 +\int_{0}^{\infty} e^{-x^{2}}\,dx = \frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2}
    908 +$$
    909 +
    910 +\[
    911 +\lim*{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{n}\sum*{k=1}^{n}k = \frac{1}{2}
    912 +\]
    913 +
    914 +#### 2.2 Large operators with limits
    915 +
    916 +$$
    917 +\sum_{i=1}^{n}\sum_{j=1}^{m} a_{ij}
    918 +\qquad
    919 +\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}\left(1+\frac{1}{k^{2}}\right)
    920 +\qquad
    921 +\bigcup_{i\in I} A_i
    922 +\qquad
    923 +\bigcap_{i=1}^{n} B_i
    924 +$$
    925 +
    926 +$$
    927 +\limsup_{x\to 0}\frac{\sin x}{x}=1,
    928 +\qquad
    929 +\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{a_n}{b_n}=0
    930 +$$
    931 +
    932 +#### 2.3 Multi-line environments (numbered) – align
    933 +
    934 +\begin{align}
    935 +f(x) &= ax^{2}+bx+c \label{eq:quad}\\
    936 +f'(x) &= 2ax+b \\
    937 +\int\_{0}^{1}x^{n}\,dx &= \frac{1}{n+1}\tag{\*}
    938 +\end{align}
    939 +
    940 +#### 2.4 Multi-line environments (unnumbered) – align\*
    941 +
    942 +\begin{align*}
    943 +\cos^{2}\theta + \sin^{2}\theta &= 1 \\
    944 +e^{i\pi}+1 &= 0
    945 +\end{align*}
    946 +
    947 +#### 2.5 gather (centered, numbered)
    948 +
    949 +\begin{gather}
    950 +\frac{d}{dx}\bigl(e^{x}\bigr)=e^{x} \\
    951 +\Gamma\!\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)=\sqrt{\pi}
    952 +\end{gather}
    953 +
    954 +#### 2.6 gather\* (centered, no numbers)
    955 +
    956 +\begin{gather*}
    957 +\sin\bigl(\tfrac{\pi}{2}\bigr)=1\\
    958 +\log\_{10} 1000 = 3
    959 +\end{gather*}
    960 +
    961 +#### 2.7 multline (long equation broken across lines)
    962 +
    963 +\begin{multline}
    964 +\sum\_{k=1}^{n}\frac{1}{k}
    965 += 1+\frac12+\frac13+\dots+\frac1n \\
    966 +\approx \ln n + \gamma + \frac{1}{2n} - \frac{1}{12n^{2}}+\cdots
    967 +\end{multline}
    968 +
    969 +#### 2.8 split inside equation
    970 +
    971 +\begin{equation}
    972 +\begin{split}
    973 +a+b &= c+d \\
    974 +e+f &= g+h
    975 +\end{split}
    976 +\end{equation}
    977 +
    978 +#### 2.9 cases (piece-wise definitions)
    979 +
    980 +$$
    981 +f(x)=
    982 +\begin{cases}
    983 +x^{2}          & \text{if } x\ge 0,\\[4pt]
    984 +-x             & \text{if } x<0.
    985 +\end{cases}
    986 +$$
    987 +
    988 +$$
    989 +|x| =
    990 +\begin{cases}
    991 +x & x \geq 0 \\
    992 +-x & x < 0
    993 +\end{cases}
    994 +$$
    995 +
    996 +#### 2.10 array (matrix-like alignment without delimiters)
    997 +
    998 +$$
    999 +\begin{array}{rcl}
    1000 +x^{2}+y^{2} &=& z^{2}\\
    1001 +a+b+c       &=& d
    1002 +\end{array}
    1003 +$$
    1004 +
    1005 +$$
    1006 +\begin{array}{c|c|c}
    1007 +\text{Column 1} & \text{Column 2} & \text{Column 3} \\
    1008 +\hline
    1009 +a & b & c \\
    1010 +d & e & f
    1011 +\end{array}
    1012 +$$
    1013 +
    1014 +#### 2.11 All Matrix Types: pmatrix, bmatrix, vmatrix, Vmatrix, Bmatrix
    1015 +
    1016 +$$
    1017 +A=\begin{pmatrix}
    1018 +1 & 0 & 0\\
    1019 +0 & \cos\theta & -\sin\theta\\
    1020 +0 & \sin\theta & \phantom{-}\cos\theta
    1021 +\end{pmatrix},
    1022 +\qquad
    1023 +B=\begin{bmatrix}
    1024 +a & b\\
    1025 +c & d
    1026 +\end{bmatrix}
    1027 +$$
    1028 +
    1029 +$$
    1030 +\det C=\begin{vmatrix}
    1031 +x & y\\
    1032 +z & w
    1033 +\end{vmatrix},
    1034 +\qquad
    1035 +D=\begin{Vmatrix}
    1036 +p & q\\
    1037 +r & s
    1038 +\end{Vmatrix},
    1039 +\qquad
    1040 +E=\begin{Bmatrix}
    1041 +1 & 2\\
    1042 +3 & 4
    1043 +\end{Bmatrix}
    1044 +$$
    1045 +
    1046 +#### 2.12 smallmatrix inside inline math
    1047 +
    1048 +The 2×2 identity: $\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ and rotation: $\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}\cos\theta&-\sin\theta\\\sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$.
    1049 +
    1050 +---
    1051 +
    1052 +### 3️⃣ Delimiters – Size, Scaling, and Nesting
    1053 +
    1054 +**Auto-sizing with \left \right:**
    1055 +
    1056 +$$
    1057 +\left(
    1058 +  \frac{a}{b}
    1059 +\right),
    1060 +\quad
    1061 +\left[
    1062 +  \frac{1}{1+\displaystyle\frac{x}{y}}
    1063 +\right],
    1064 +\quad
    1065 +\left\langle
    1066 +  \sum_{i=1}^{n} i
    1067 +\right\rangle,
    1068 +\quad
    1069 +\left\{
    1070 +  \begin{aligned}
    1071 +    x &> 0\\
    1072 +    y &< 0
    1073 +  \end{aligned}
    1074 +\right\}
    1075 +$$
    1076 +
    1077 +**Manual sizing (\big, \Big, \bigg, \Bigg):**
    1078 +
    1079 +$$
    1080 +\big( a \big),\;
    1081 +\Big[ b \Big],\;
    1082 +\bigg\{ c \bigg\},\;
    1083 +\Bigg| d \Bigg|
    1084 +$$
    1085 +
    1086 +$$
    1087 +\Bigl( \bigl( ( x ) \bigr) \Bigr)
    1088 +\quad
    1089 +\biggl\langle \Bigl\langle \bigl\langle \langle x \rangle \bigr\rangle \Bigr\rangle \biggr\rangle
    1090 +$$
    1091 +
    1092 +**Floor, ceiling, and absolute value:**
    1093 +
    1094 +$$
    1095 +\lfloor x \rfloor, \quad \lceil y \rceil, \quad |z|, \quad \|v\|
    1096 +$$
    1097 +
    1098 +$$
    1099 +\left\lfloor \frac{n}{2} \right\rfloor, \quad \left\lceil \log_2 n \right\rceil
    1100 +$$
    1101 +
    1102 +---
    1103 +
    1104 +### 4️⃣ Advanced Symbolic Constructs
    1105 +
    1106 +| Symbol                 | LaTeX Code                                        | Rendered                                      |
    1107 +| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
    1108 +| **Implication**        | `$A \implies B$`                                  | $A \implies B$                                |
    1109 +| **Equivalence**        | `$A \iff B$`                                      | $A \iff B$                                    |
    1110 +| **Logical operators**  | `$p \land q,\; p \lor q,\; \neg p$`               | $p \land q,\; p \lor q,\; \neg p$             |
    1111 +| **Set builder**        | `$\{x\in\mathbb{R}\mid x>0\}$`                    | $\{x\in\mathbb{R}\mid x>0\}$                  |
    1112 +| **Function arrow**     | `$f\colon X\to Y$`                                | $f\colon X\to Y$                              |
    1113 +| **Partial derivative** | `$\frac{\partial f}{\partial x}$`                 | $\frac{\partial f}{\partial x}$               |
    1114 +| **Nabla / gradient**   | `$\nabla f$`                                      | $\nabla f$                                    |
    1115 +| **Laplacian**          | `$\Delta u$,`$\nabla^2 u$`                        | $\Delta u$, $\nabla^2 u$                      |
    1116 +| **Infinity**           | `$\infty$`                                        | $\infty$                                      |
    1117 +| **Ellipsis**           | `$\dots,\; \cdots,\; \vdots,\; \ddots$`           | $\dots,\; \cdots,\; \vdots,\; \ddots$         |
    1118 +| **Relations**          | `$x\sim y,\; x\approx y,\; x\equiv y$`            | $x\sim y,\; x\approx y,\; x\equiv y$          |
    1119 +| **Arrows with text**   | `$\xrightarrow{\text{limit}}$`                    | $\xrightarrow{\text{limit}}$                  |
    1120 +| **Double-arrow**       | `$\xleftrightarrow{AB}$`                          | $\xleftrightarrow{AB}$                        |
    1121 +| **Hook arrows**        | `$\xhookrightarrow{f}$`                           | $\xhookrightarrow{f}$                         |
    1122 +| **Overset / Underset** | `$\overset{!}{=}$`, `$\underset{a}{\rightarrow}$` | $\overset{!}{=}$, $\underset{a}{\rightarrow}$ |
    1123 +| **Stackrel**           | `$\stackrel{\text{def}}{=}$`                      | $\stackrel{\text{def}}{=}$                    |
    1124 +| **Tensor indices**     | `$T^{\mu\nu}_{\rho\sigma}$`                       | $T^{\mu\nu}_{\rho\sigma}$                     |
    1125 +| **Commutator**         | `$[A, B]$`                                        | $[A, B]$                                      |
    1126 +| **Anticommutator**     | `$\{A, B\}$`                                      | $\{A, B\}$                                    |
    1127 +
    1128 +---
    1129 +
    1130 +### 5️⃣ Spacing Commands (fine-tuning)
    1131 +
    1132 +$$
    1133 +a\!b\;c\,d\;e\quad f\qquad g
    1134 +$$
    1135 +
    1136 +- `\!` negative thin space
    1137 +- `\,` thin space
    1138 +- `\:`, `\;` medium/thick space
    1139 +- `\quad`, `\qquad` larger spaces
    1140 +
    1141 +**Proper integral spacing:** $\int f(x)\,dx$ vs $\int f(x)dx$

    1144 +
    1145 +### 6️⃣ "Hacky" Math – Edge Cases That Often Break Renderers
    1146 +
    1147 +| Description                   | LaTeX                                                                                 | Notes                       |
    1148 +| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
    1149 +| **Empty fraction**            | $\frac{}{x}$                                                                          | Missing numerator           |
    1150 +| **Phantom spacing**           | $a\phantom{bcd}e$                                                                     | Invisible spacing           |
    1151 +| **Smash (suppress height)**   | $\smash{\frac{a}{b}}c$                                                                | Suppresses vertical extent  |
    1152 +| **Boxed with displaystyle**   | $\boxed{\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{n}i}$                                                | Large operator inside box   |
    1153 +| **operatorname with limits**  | $\operatorname*{argmax}_{x}$                                                          | Custom operator with limits |
    1154 +| **Complex nested delimiters** | $\left\langle\frac{\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{n}i}{\sqrt[3]{x^{2}+y^{2}}}\right\rangle$ | Deeply nested sizing        |
    1155 +| **Text with math and spaces** | $\text{if }x>0\text{ then }y=1$                                                       | Mixed text/math             |
    1156 +| **Whole-block color**         | See below                                                                             | Color entire equation       |
    1157 +| **Custom tag**                | See below                                                                             | `\tag{}` with label         |
    1158 +
    1159 +**Whole-block color test:**

    1256 +### 1️⃣2️⃣ Complex Physics Equations
    1257 +
    1258 +**Maxwell's Equations:**
    1259 +
    1260 +$$
    1261 +\begin{aligned}
    1262 +\nabla \cdot \vec{E} &= \frac{\rho}{\epsilon_0} \\
    1263 +\nabla \cdot \vec{B} &= 0 \\
    1264 +\nabla \times \vec{E} &= -\frac{\partial \vec{B}}{\partial t} \\
    1265 +\nabla \times \vec{B} &= \mu_0\vec{J} + \mu_0\epsilon_0\frac{\partial \vec{E}}{\partial t}
    1266 +\end{aligned}
    1267 +$$
    1268 +
    1269 +**Schrödinger Equation:**
    1270 +
    1271 +$$
    1272 +i\hbar\frac{\partial}{\partial t}\Psi(\vec{r},t) = \left[-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\nabla^2 + V(\vec{r},t)\right]\Psi(\vec{r},t)
    1273 +$$
    1274 +
    1275 +**Einstein Field Equations:**
    1276 +
    1277 +$$
    1278 +R_{\mu\nu} - \frac{1}{2}Rg_{\mu\nu} + \Lambda g_{\mu\nu} = \frac{8\pi G}{c^4}T_{\mu\nu}
    1279 +$$

    1283 +### 1️⃣3️⃣ "All-in-One" Showcase
    1284 +
    1285 +$$
    1286 +\boxed{
    1287 +\begin{aligned}
    1288 +\text{Solve }\;&\color{blue}{\underbrace{ax^{2}+bx+c}_{\text{quadratic}}=0} \\[4pt]
    1289 +x &= \frac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^{2}-4ac}}{2a} \tag{Quadratic Formula}\\[6pt]
    1290 +\text{Discriminant }&\Delta = b^{2}-4ac\\[6pt]
    1291 +\text{Vertex }(h,k)&\text{ where }h=-\frac{b}{2a},\;k=-\frac{\Delta}{4a}\\[6pt]
    1292 +\text{Nature of roots: }&\Delta\begin{cases}
    1293 +>0 &\text{two distinct real roots}\\
    1294 +=0 &\text{one real double root}\\
    1295 +<0 &\text{two complex conjugates}
    1296 +\end{cases}
    1297 +\end{aligned}
    1298 +}
    1299 +$$

    1302 +
    1303 +### 1️⃣4️⃣ Complex Math on Same Line
    1304 +
    1305 +The equation $\int_a^b f(x)dx = F(b) - F(a)$ shows that $\frac{d}{dx}F(x) = f(x)$ where $F$ is antiderivative of $f$.
    1306 +
    1307 +Physics: $\vec{F} = m\vec{a}$, $p = mv$, $KE = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$, $PE = mgh$, $\vec{L} = \vec{r} \times \vec{p}$
    1308 +
    1309 +Statistics: $\bar{x} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n x_i$, $\sigma = \sqrt{\frac{1}{n}\sum(x_i - \bar{x})^2}$, $r = \frac{\sum(x_i-\bar{x})(y_i-\bar{y})}{\sqrt{\sum(x_i-\bar{x})^2\sum(y_i-\bar{y})^2}}$
    1310 +
    1311 +Probability: $P(A|B) = \frac{P(B|A)P(A)}{P(B)}$, $\mathbb{E}[X] = \sum_x x \cdot P(X=x)$, $\text{Var}(X) = \mathbb{E}[X^2] - (\mathbb{E}[X])^2$

    160 +## 🚀 Quick Start
    161 +
    162 +### Prerequisites
    163 +
    164 +- Node.js 18+ and npm
    165 +- Modern browser (Chrome 86+, Firefox 90+, Safari 14+, Edge 86+)
    166 +
    167 +### Installation
    168 +
    169 +```bash
    170 +# Clone the repository
    171 +git clone https://github.com/PrakharMNNIT/markdown-viewer-app.git
    172 +cd markdown-viewer-app
    173 +
    174 +# Install dependencies
    175 +npm install
    176 +
    177 +# Start development server
    178 +npm run dev
    179 +```
    180 +
    181 +### Usage
    182 +
    183 +1. Open your browser to `http://localhost:5173`
    184 +2. Start typing markdown in the left panel
    185 +3. See live preview on the right
    186 +4. **Open Folder** - Click to browse local markdown files
    187 +5. **Zen Mode** - Click for distraction-free reading
    188 +6. Switch themes from the dropdown
    189 +7. Customize colors with the theme builder
    190 +8. Export to HTML or PDF
    191 +
    192 +### Keyboard Shortcuts
    193 +
    194 +| Shortcut | Action |
    195 +|----------|--------|
    196 +| `Ctrl/Cmd + +` | Zoom in |
    197 +| `Ctrl/Cmd + -` | Zoom out |
    198 +| `Ctrl/Cmd + 0` | Reset zoom |
    199 +| `Escape` | Exit Zen Mode |

    233 +
    234 +## 🏗️ Architecture
    235 +
    236 +### Design Patterns
    237 +
    238 +- **Service Layer Pattern** - Isolated business logic (MermaidService, PrismService, FolderBrowserService)
    239 +- **Observer Pattern** - Theme change notifications to dependent services
    240 +- **Dependency Injection** - ThemeManager receives StorageManager instance
    241 +- **Facade Pattern** - Clean API abstractions for complex operations
    242 +- **Strategy Pattern** - Pluggable theme loading strategies
    243 +- **Singleton Pattern** - Anchor navigation heading slug map
    244 +
    245 +### Module Organization
    246 +
    247 +#### **config/** - Configuration and Constants
    248 +
    249 +- `constants.js`: 12 constant groups (ZOOM, STORAGE_KEYS, THEMES, etc.)
    250 +- `errorMessages.js`: Centralized error message definitions
    251 +- `featureFlags.js`: Feature toggle system for safe rollouts
    252 +
    253 +#### **utils/** - Reusable Utilities
    254 +
    255 +- `htmlHelpers.js`: DOM manipulation, blob URLs, file downloads
    256 +- `colorHelpers.js`: CSS variable getters/setters
    257 +- `validators.js`: Input validation and constraints
    258 +
    259 +#### **services/** - Business Logic
    260 +
    261 +- `FolderBrowserService.js`: File System Access API integration
    262 +- `HTMLService.js`: HTML export with theme embedding
    263 +- `MermaidService.js`: Theme-aware diagram rendering (5 methods)
    264 +- `PDFService.js`: PDF generation with html2pdf.js
    265 +- `PrismService.js`: Syntax highlighting with error recovery (5 methods)
    266 +
    267 +#### **core/** - Core Modules
    268 +
    269 +- `StorageManager.js`: LocalStorage abstraction with error handling (11 methods)
    270 +- `ThemeManager.js`: Theme loading, switching, and persistence (11 methods)
    271 +
    272 +### Integration Points
    273 +
    274 +```javascript
    275 +// Main application entry (script.js)
    276 +import { StorageManager } from './src/js/core/StorageManager.js';
    277 +import { ThemeManager } from './src/js/core/ThemeManager.js';
    278 +import { MermaidService } from './src/js/services/MermaidService.js';
    279 +import { PrismService } from './src/js/services/PrismService.js';
    280 +import { FolderBrowserService } from './src/js/services/FolderBrowserService.js';
    281 +import { PDFService } from './src/js/services/PDFService.js';
    282 +import { HTMLService } from './src/js/services/HTMLService.js';
    283 +
    284 +// Initialize with dependency injection
    285 +const storageManager = new StorageManager();
    286 +const themeManager = new ThemeManager(storageManager);
    287 +const mermaidService = new MermaidService();
    288 +const prismService = new PrismService();
    289 +const folderBrowserService = new FolderBrowserService(storageManager);
    290 +const pdfService = new PDFService();
    291 +const htmlService = new HTMLService();
    292 +
    293 +// Configure observer pattern
    294 +themeManager.setThemeChangeListener(() => {
    295 +  mermaidService.reinitialize();
    296 +});
    297 +```

    417 +## 📚 API Reference
    418 +
    419 +### FolderBrowserService (NEW)
    420 +
    421 +```javascript
    422 +const folderService = new FolderBrowserService(storageManager);
    423 +
    424 +// Check support
    425 +if (folderService.isSupported()) {
    426 +  // Open folder dialog
    427 +  const result = await folderService.openFolder();
    428 +  // result: { success, files, folderName, totalFiles }
    429 +
    430 +  // Read file
    431 +  const fileResult = await folderService.readFile(fileHandle);
    432 +  // fileResult: { success, content, name, size }
    433 +
    434 +  // Create new file
    435 +  const createResult = await folderService.createFile(dirHandle, filename, content);
    436 +  // createResult: { success, filename, fileHandle }
    437 +
    438 +  // Refresh folder
    439 +  const refreshResult = await folderService.refreshFolder();
    440 +}
    441 +```
    442 +
    443 +### StorageManager
    444 +
    445 +```javascript
    446 +const storage = new StorageManager();
    447 +
    448 +// Basic operations
    449 +storage.set('key', 'value'); // Store string
    450 +const value = storage.get('key'); // Retrieve string
    451 +storage.remove('key'); // Remove item
    452 +storage.has('key'); // Check existence
    453 +
    454 +// JSON operations
    455 +storage.setJSON('data', { a: 1 }); // Store object
    456 +const obj = storage.getJSON('data'); // Retrieve object
    457 +
    458 +// Utility methods
    459 +storage.getAllKeys(); // Get all keys
    460 +storage.getSize(); // Storage size in bytes
    461 +storage.clear(); // Clear all (USE WITH CAUTION)
    462 +storage.isAvailable(); // Check localStorage availability
    463 +```
    464 +
    465 +### ThemeManager
    466 +
    467 +```javascript
    468 +const themeManager = new ThemeManager(storageManager);
    469 +
    470 +// Theme operations
    471 +await themeManager.loadTheme('ocean-dark'); // Load theme
    472 +themeManager.saveCustomTheme({ '--h1': '#f00' }); // Save custom
    473 +const current = themeManager.getCurrentTheme(); // Get current name
    474 +const colors = themeManager.getCurrentColors(); // Get all colors
    475 +
    476 +// Observer pattern
    477 +themeManager.setThemeChangeListener(themeName => {
    478 +  console.log('Theme changed to:', themeName);
    479 +});
    480 +
    481 +// Utility methods
    482 +const themes = themeManager.getAvailableThemes(); // List all themes
    483 +const exists = themeManager.themeExists('neon-dark'); // Check existence
    484 +```
    485 +
    486 +### MermaidService
    487 +
    488 +```javascript
    489 +const mermaidService = new MermaidService();
    490 +
    491 +// Initialize with current theme
    492 +mermaidService.initialize();
    493 +
    494 +// Render diagram
    495 +const svg = await mermaidService.render(
    496 +  'diagram-1',
    497 +  `
    498 +  graph TD
    499 +    A[Start] --> B[Process]
    500 +    B --> C[End]
    501 +`
    502 +);
    503 +
    504 +// Check readiness and reinitialize
    505 +if (mermaidService.isReady()) {
    506 +  mermaidService.reinitialize(); // Call after theme change
    507 +}
    508 +```
    509 +
    510 +### PDFService (NEW)
    511 +
    512 +```javascript
    513 +const pdfService = new PDFService();
    514 +
    515 +// Generate PDF with options
    516 +const blob = await pdfService.generatePDF(previewElement, {
    517 +  pageSize: 'A4',
    518 +  orientation: 'portrait',
    519 +  margins: [10, 10, 10, 10],
    520 +  fontSize: 12
    521 +});
    522 +
    523 +// Preview PDF in iframe
    524 +const url = await pdfService.previewPDF(previewElement, config);
    525 +
    526 +// Download PDF
    527 +pdfService.downloadPDF();
    528 +```

    605 +
    606 +**Build errors?**
    607 +
    608 +```bash
    609 +rm -rf node_modules package-lock.json
    610 +npm install
    611 +npm run build
    612 +```
    613 +
    614 +**Theme not loading?**
    615 +
    616 +- Check browser console for errors
    617 +- Verify theme file exists in `themes/`
    618 +- Clear browser cache
    619 +
    620 +**Mermaid diagrams not rendering?**
    621 +
    622 +- Check internet connection (CDN required)
    623 +- Verify diagram syntax
    624 +- Check browser console for errors
    625 +
    626 +**Folder Browser not working?**
    627 +
    628 +- Requires Chrome 86+ or Edge 86+
    629 +- Firefox/Safari don't support File System Access API
    630 +- Check for permission prompts
    631 +

    634 +- This is fixed in the latest version

      1 +# 📋 Release Notes - Markdown Viewer Pro

      8 +
      9 +## 🎉 What's New
     10 +
     11 +### Major Features
     12 +
     13 +#### 📁 Folder Browser
     14 +A powerful local file system integration for browsing and managing markdown files.
     15 +
     16 +- **Open Folder** - Browse local folders using File System Access API
     17 +- **File Tree Navigation** - Click to navigate through nested directories
     18 +- **Create Files** - Create new markdown files with 5 templates (empty, basic, readme, notes, blog)
     19 +- **Folder Refresh** - Refresh contents without reopening the folder
     20 +- **Resizable Sidebar** - Drag to resize, auto-collapse when dragged to edge
     21 +- **Expand Button** - Premium animated button to quickly expand collapsed sidebar
     22 +- **State Persistence** - Sidebar width and collapsed state saved to localStorage
     23 +
     24 +#### 🧘 Zen Mode
     25 +Distraction-free reading mode for focused content consumption.
     26 +
     27 +- **Full Screen Preview** - 100% width and height coverage
     28 +- **Hidden UI** - Toolbar, sidebar, and footer automatically hidden
     29 +- **ESC to Exit** - Press Escape or click exit button to return
     30 +- **Centered Content** - Max-width 900px for optimal readability
     31 +
     32 +#### ↔️ Split View Resizer
     33 +Flexible panel sizing for comfortable editing.
     34 +
     35 +- **Draggable Divider** - Resize editor and preview panels
     36 +- **Custom Ratio** - Set anywhere from 20% to 80%
     37 +- **Ratio Persistence** - Split position saved across sessions
     38 +- **Visual Feedback** - Animated handles on hover and drag
     39 +
     40 +#### 🔗 TOC Anchor Navigation
     41 +Smart in-document navigation for table of contents links.
     42 +
     43 +- **Smooth Scrolling** - Click TOC links to scroll to headings
     44 +- **4-Priority Resolution** - Exact → normalized → GitHub-style → fuzzy matching
     45 +- **Browser History** - Back/forward navigation support
     46 +- **Accessibility** - Focus management and keyboard navigation
     47 +- **Special Characters** - C++ → cpp, C# → csharp handling
     48 +- **Deep Linking** - Direct URL hash support (#section-name)
     49 +
     50 +#### ➗ LaTeX Math Support (Enhanced)
     51 +Full mathematical formula rendering with multiple delimiter formats.
     52 +
     53 +- **Inline Math** - `$...$` and `\(...\)` delimiters
     54 +- **Display Math** - `$$...$$` and `\[...\]` delimiters
     55 +- **LaTeX Environments** - Support for align, gather, and more
     56 +- **KaTeX Rendering** - Fast, high-quality math typesetting

     60 +## 🐛 Bug Fixes

     68 +### UI/UX Fixes

     70 +- **Sidebar Resize in Split View** - Resize handle now works correctly in split view mode
     71 +- **Resize Handle UX** - Improved drag handle visibility and interaction
     72 +- **Zen Mode Full Screen** - Fixed 100% width/height coverage

     16 +- **Security:** ⭐ (1/5) - **CRITICAL** Stored XSS vulnerability detected.
     17 +- **Code Quality:** ⭐⭐⭐ (3/5) - Human-readable, but prone to race conditions.

### ✨ `src/lib/external/markdown-viewer-app/codebase_audit/deep_dive_reviews/mermaid_service_review.md` **[ADDED]**

**Status:** ✅ **NEW FILE** - This file has been newly created

**Type:** Documentation 📖

```diff
@@ -0,0 +1,47 @@
      1 +# 🕵️‍♂️ Deep Dive Code Review: `MermaidService.js`
      2 +
      3 +**Reviewer:** CodeBaseGPT (Senior SDE Persona)
      4 +**Date:** 2025-12-09
      5 +**File:** `src/js/services/MermaidService.js` (302 Lines)
      6 +
      7 +---
      8 +
      9 +## ⚠️ Issues & Observations
     10 +
     11 +### 1. ⚙️ Massive Configuration Object (Line 96)
     12 +```javascript
     13 +themeVariables: { ... 100+ lines ... }
     14 +```
     15 +**Critique:** You are explicitly mapping every single Mermaid variable (60+) to your own CSS variables.
     16 +- **Pros:** Total control over the look.
     17 +- **Cons:** **High Coupling**. If Mermaid v12 changes its variable names (e.g., `primaryColor` -> `mainColor`), your integration breaks or looks wrong.
     18 +- **Suggestion:** Consider whether mapped sets (Primary, Secondary, Tertiary) are sufficient, or if this granular control is truly business-critical.
     19 +
     20 +### 2. 🔢 Hardcoded Font configurations (Lines 99, 100)
     21 +```javascript
     22 +fontFamily: '-apple-system, ...',
     23 +fontSize: '16px',
     24 +```
     25 +**Critique:** You are hardcoding fonts in JS.
     26 +- **Issue:** If the user changes the font in `style.css`, the diagrams won't match the rest of the app.
     27 +- **Fix:** Use `getCssVariable('--font-family')` and `getCssVariable('--font-size-base')`.
     28 +
     29 +### 3. 📉 Missing Debounce/Cancellation
     30 +**Critique:** `MermaidService.render` is async.
     31 +- **Scenario:** User types fast. `render('id', 'graph TD...')` is called 5 times in 200ms.
     32 +- **Result:** You might have 5 parallel rendering processes competing.
     33 +- **Fix:** Implement a `Cancellation` mechanism or rely on the Controller to debounce calls (which `script.js` currently fails to do properly).
     34 +
     35 +### 4. 🎭 Theme Detection Logic (Line 45)
     36 +```javascript
     37 +function isLightTheme(bgColor) { ... }
     38 +```
     39 +**Critique:** Clever use of luminance calculation!
     40 +- **Positive:** This is a nice "Senior Dev" touch. It ensures that even if I pick a weird Custom Theme color (e.g., bright yellow background), Mermaid will likely pick the correct "Dark/Light" base mode.
     41 +- **Refactor:** Move `getRelativeLuminance` to `src/js/utils/colorHelpers.js`. It is a pure utility function and might be useful elsewhere (e.g., checking text contrast accessibility).
     42 +
     43 +---
     44 +
     45 +## 🏁 Verdict
     46 +**Grade: B+**
     47 +The logic is solid, but the coupling to Mermaid's specific variable names is a risk. It's "Enterprise Grade" in the sense that it handles everything, but "Enterprise Grade" also means "Heavy maintenance".
     48  

```


### ✨ `src/lib/external/markdown-viewer-app/codebase_audit/deep_dive_reviews/script_js_review.md` **[ADDED]**

**Status:** ✅ **NEW FILE** - This file has been newly created

**Type:** Documentation 📖

```diff
@@ -0,0 +1,121 @@
      1 +# 🕵️‍♂️ Deep Dive Code Review: `script.js`
      2 +
      3 +**Reviewer:** CodeBaseGPT (Senior SDE Persona)
      4 +**Date:** 2025-12-09
      5 +**File:** `script.js` (1372 Lines)
      6 +
      7 +---
      8 +
      9 +## 🛑 Critical Issues (Must Fix)
     10 +
     11 +### 1. 💀 Stored XSS Vulnerability (Line 512)
     12 +```javascript
     13 +preview.innerHTML = html;
     14 +```
     15 +**Critique:** You are taking the output of `marked.parse()` and dumping it directly into the DOM. `marked` does **not** sanitize HTML execution by default.
     16 +- **Scenario:** A user opens a markdown file containing `<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>`.
     17 +- ** Impact:** Arbitrary code execution.
     18 +- **Fix:** You **MUST** use `DOMPurify.sanitize(html)` before assignment.
     19 +
     20 +### 2. 🐢 recursive Polling for Dependencies (Lines 46-75)
     21 +```javascript
     22 +if (typeof marked === 'undefined' ...) {
     23 +    setTimeout(initializeApp, 100);
     24 +    return;
     25 +}
     26 +```
     27 +**Critique:** This "check and retry" pattern is an anti-pattern.
     28 +- **Why:** It burns CPU in a tight loop. It complicates the startup race conditions.
     29 +- **Fix:** Use standard `<script defer>` or ES Module `import` statements to guarantee execution order. If you strictly need globals, use `window.onload`.
     30 +
     31 +### 3. 💥 Race Condition "Magic Numbers" (Lines 490, 535)
     32 +```javascript
     33 +// Line 490
     34 +setTimeout(() => { ... mermaid.render(...) }, 100);
     35 +
     36 +// Line 535
     37 +setTimeout(() => { ... renderMarkdown() }, 100);
     38 +```
     39 +**Critique:** You are using `setTimeout` with a magic number (`100ms`) to "wait" for the DOM or other processes.
     40 +- **Why:** This is unreliable. On a slow machine, 100ms isn't enough, and the render fails. On a fast machine, it causes a perceptible UI stutter.
     41 +- **Fix:** Use **Promises** and `requestAnimationFrame`. `mermaid.render` returns a promise; await it.
     42 +
     43 +### 4. 🔥 Un-Debounced Rendering (Line 666)
     44 +```javascript
     45 +editor.addEventListener('input', renderMarkdown);
     46 +```
     47 +**Critique:** `renderMarkdown` is heavy (Regex + Parsing + DOM clear + Prism + Mermaid).
     48 +- **Why:** Triggers on *every keystroke*. Typing fast will freeze the UI.
     49 +- **Fix:** Wrap the handler in a `debounce` function (e.g., wait 300ms after last keystroke).
     50 +
     51 +---
     52 +
     53 +## ⚠️ Major Logic Flaws & Architecture
     54 +
     55 +### 5. 🏗️ The "God Function": `setupEditor` (Lines 295-1372)
     56 +**Critique:** This function is **1077 lines long**.
     57 +- **Issue:** It contains state (`folderFiles`), event listeners, UI logic (`updatePDFPreview`), and utility helpers (`renderFileTree`).
     58 +- **Impact:** It is effectively impossible to unit test. Scope pollution is rampant.
     59 +- **Fix:** Break this file apart immediately.
     60 +    - `setupEditor()` should only orchestrate.
     61 +    - `setupPDFHandling()` should be its own module.
     62 +    - `setupFolderBrowser()` should be its own module.
     63 +
     64 +### 6. 🍝 Spaghetti Events (Global Scope Pollution)
     65 +```javascript
     66 +let globalRenderMarkdown = null; // Line 24
     67 +...
     68 +globalRenderMarkdown = renderMarkdown; // Line 1367
     69 +```
     70 +**Critique:** You are leaking a local function to the global scope to hack around scope limitations for the theme manager callback.
     71 +- **Fix:** Pass `renderMarkdown` as a dependency or use a proper `EventManager` (Pub/Sub pattern).
     72 +
     73 +### 7. 📁 Hardcoded DOM Generation (Lines 1241-1334)
     74 +**Critique:** The `renderFileTree` function essentially constructs a Virtual DOM manually using `document.createElement`.
     75 +- **Issue:** This logic is mixed with the controller.
     76 +- **Fix:** Move this to a `FileTreeView.js` class. The controller should just say `treeView.render(files)`.
     77 +
     78 +---
     79 +
     80 +## 🔍 Nitpicks & Code Style (Senior SDE Standards)
     81 +
     82 +### 8. 📝 Hardcoded Content (Lines 297-381)
     83 +**Critique:** The default "Welcome" markdown is 84 lines of hardcoded string inside a logic file.
     84 +- **Fix:** Move to `src/js/config/defaultContent.js` or load from a file.
     85 +
     86 +### 9. 🎨 CSS Variable Extraction (Line 553)
     87 +```javascript
     88 +const currentValue = getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue(varName).trim();
     89 +```
     90 +**Critique:** You are calling `getComputedStyle` inside a loop (`forEach` on Line 550).
     91 +- **Impact:** This forces a **Style Recalculation** (Reflow) on every iteration. Expensive.
     92 +- **Fix:** Cache `getComputedStyle` once outside the loop.
     93 +
     94 +### 10. ❌ Regex ReDoS Potential (Lines 111, 485)
     95 +```javascript
     96 +// Line 485
     97 +html = html.replace(/<pre><code class="language-mermaid">([\s\S]*?)<\/code><\/pre>/g, ...
     98 +```
     99 +**Critique:** `[\s\S]*?` is generally safe-ish, but processing the entire HTML output with regex to find code blocks is fragile HTML parsing.
    100 +- **Fix:** Marked.js has a `renderer` option. Override the `code` renderer instead of string-replacing the output HTML. This is much cleaner and safer.
    101 +
    102 +### 11. 🧩 Mixed 'var' and 'let' (Lines 884-885)
    103 +```javascript
    104 +var syncScrollEnabled = ...
    105 +var syncScrolling = ...
    106 +```
    107 +**Critique:** Why `var`? You used `const/let` everywhere else.
    108 +- **Fix:** Be consistent. Use `let`.
    109 +
    110 +### 12. 🐛 Error Handling in `loadTheme` (Line 1008)
    111 +```javascript
    112 +.catch(err => {
    113 +  console.error('Failed to load saved theme:', err);
    114 +  // Fallback to default-light
    115 +```
    116 +**Critique:** Good fallback logic, but `alert()` or `toast` missing. User won't know why their theme didn't load.
    117 +
    118 +---
    119 +
    120 +## ✅ Summary
    121 +The code works "happy path" but is brittle. The usage of `setTimeout` for flow control and the lack of debouncing are the biggest "Senior SDE" red flags. The Security hole (XSS) is a blocker for any production release.
    122

### ✨ `src/lib/external/markdown-viewer-app/codebase_audit/deep_dive_reviews/theme_manager_review.md` **[ADDED]**

**Status:** ✅ **NEW FILE** - This file has been newly created

**Type:** Documentation 📖

```diff
@@ -0,0 +1,53 @@
      1 +# 🕵️‍♂️ Deep Dive Code Review: `ThemeManager.js`
      2 +
      3 +**Reviewer:** CodeBaseGPT (Senior SDE Persona)
      4 +**Date:** 2025-12-09
      5 +**File:** `src/js/core/ThemeManager.js` (263 Lines)
      6 +
      7 +---
      8 +
      9 +## 🟢 strengths
     10 +*   **SOLID Principles:** Class has a clear Single Responsibility.
     11 +*   **Error Handling:** `try...catch` blocks are present in `loadBuiltInTheme` and `loadCustomTheme`.
     12 +*   **JSDoc:** Excellent documentation and usage examples.
     13 +
     14 +## ⚠️ Issues & Observations
     15 +
     16 +### 1. 🐌 Performance: `clearInlineStyles` (Line 205)
     17 +```javascript
     18 +for (let i = styles.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
     19 +  const prop = styles[i];
     20 +  if (prop.startsWith('--')) {
     21 +    removeCssVariable(prop);
     22 +  }
     23 +}
     24 +```
     25 +**Critique:** This loop calls `removeProperty` repeatedly on the root element.
     26 +- **Impact:** Each removal can trigger a Style Recalculation (Reflow) in the browser engine.
     27 +- **Optimization:** If you only use inline styles for custom themes, you could simply clear the `style` attribute: `document.documentElement.removeAttribute('style');` (unless there are other non-theme inline styles needed).
     28 +
     29 +### 2. 🧩 Hardcoded Variable List (Line 171)
     30 +```javascript
     31 +const cssVarNames = [ '--bg-primary', ... ];
     32 +```
     33 +**Critique:** You manually list 18 variables here to "capture" the current theme colors.
     34 +- **Risk:** This list is a **Maintenance Liability**. If a developer adds a new color (e.g., `--warning-color`) to `style.css` but forgets to add it here, the "Save Custom Theme" feature will silently drop that color.
     35 +- **Fix:** Import this list from `src/js/config/constants.js` (SSOT). Do not define it inside the method.
     36 +
     37 +### 3. 🧪 Production Path Resolution (Line 80)
     38 +```javascript
     39 +const baseUrl = import.meta.env.BASE_URL || '/';
     40 +stylesheet.href = `${baseUrl}themes/${themeName}.css`;
     41 +```
     42 +**Critique:** Good job anticipating Vite's `BASE_URL`.
     43 +- **Observation:** Ensure `themes/` folder is actually copied to `dist/` during build. Since they are static assets referenced via code (not import), Vite might not hash/include them unless configured in `vite.config.js` static assets.
     44 +
     45 +### 4. 🔒 Private Methods (Semantics)
     46 +**Critique:** You use JSDoc `@private` but the methods `loadBuiltInTheme` are technically public.
     47 +- **Suggestion:** Use `#privateFields` (ES2022) if you want true privacy, e.g., `#loadBuiltInTheme`.
     48 +
     49 +---
     50 +
     51 +## 🏁 Verdict
     52 +**Grade: A-**
     53 +This is high-quality code. The issues are mostly maintenance optimizations. The logic is sound.
     54  

```

### ✨ `src/lib/external/markdown-viewer-app/codebase_audit/future_enhancements_roadmap.md` **[ADDED]**

**Status:** ✅ **NEW FILE** - This file has been newly created

**Type:** Documentation 📖

```diff
@@ -0,0 +1,93 @@
      1 +# 🚀 Future Enhancements: Enterprise-Grade Roadmap
      2 +
      3 +This document outlines the strategic roadmap to transform the `markdown-viewer-app` into a truly **Enterprise-Grade** web application.
      4 +
      5 +---
      6 +
      7 +## ✅ Completed Enhancements (Phase 1.5 Polish)
      8 +*   **UI/UX:** Implemented Glassmorphism transparency on Toolbar and Modals (`color-mix` + `backdrop-filter`).
      9 +*   **Mobile Experience:** Added "Mobile Tabs" (Edit/Preview toggle) to replace awkward vertical stacking.
     10 +*   **Animations:** Added subtle keyframe animations for Modals and Fade-ins.
     11 +*   **Syntax Highlighting:** Fully future-proofed with `vite-plugin-prismjs`.
     12 +
     13 +## 🏗️ Phase 1: Robust Application Architecture (Modernization)
     14 +
     15 +To support enterprise scale, we must move beyond the "Vanilla JS" constraints suitable for prototypes and adopt a robust, type-safe ecosystem.
     16 +
     17 +### 1.1 Migrate to TypeScript
     18 +*   **Why:** Enterprise apps require type safety to prevent runtime errors (undefined is not ...).
     19 +*   **Plan:** Rename `.js` to `.ts`. Define interfaces for `Theme`, `FileNode`, and `AppConfig`. Strict null checks.
     20 +
     21 +### 1.2 Component-Based Architecture (Web Components or Framework)
     22 +*   **Why:** The `script.js` monolith is unmaintainable.
     23 +*   **Plan:**
     24 +    *   **Option A (Vanilla):** Adopt Web Components (`<markdown-editor>`, `<file-tree>`).
     25 +    *   **Option B (Standard):** Migrate to **React** or **Vue**. This allows us to use massive ecosystems of tested components (e.g., `Monaco Editor` for better markdown editing).
     26 +
     27 +### 1.3 State Management
     28 +*   **Why:** Passing `globalRenderMarkdown` around is fragile.
     29 +*   **Plan:** Implement a centralized store (e.g., `Redux`, `Zustand`, or a simple `StateService` observable) to manage:
     30 +    *   `currentFile`
     31 +    *   `theme`
     32 +    *   `settings`
     33 +    *   `folderStructure`
     34 +
     35 +---
     36 +
     37 +## 🛡️ Phase 2: Enterprise Security & Compliance
     38 +
     39 +### 2.1 Content Security Policy (CSP)
     40 +*   **Goal:** Prevent XSS and Data Exfiltration.
     41 +*   **Action:** implement strict CSP headers (or `<meta>` tags):
     42 +    ```html
     43 +    <meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-eval' (for mermaid); style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline';">
     44 +    ```
     45 +
     46 +### 2.2 Input Sanitization Layer
     47 +*   **Goal:** trust No Input.
     48 +*   **Action:** Integrate `DOMPurify` deeply into the rendering pipeline. Create a `SanitizationService` that all HTML output must pass through.
     49 +
     50 +---
     51 +
     52 +## ⚡ Phase 3: Performance & Scalability
     53 +
     54 +### 3.1 Web Workers for Parsing
     55 +*   **Issue:** Parsing large markdown files (1000+ lines) freezes the UI.
     56 +*   **Solution:** Move `marked.parse` and syntax highlighting logic to a **Web Worker**. The main thread should only handle User Input and DOM updates.
     57 +
     58 +### 3.2 Virtualized Rendering
     59 +*   **Issue:** The File Browser and Large Preview will lag with thousands of items.
     60 +*   **Solution:** Implement "Virtual Scrolling" (Windowing). Only render the DOM nodes currently visible on screen.
     61 +
     62 +### 3.3 Offline-First (PWA)
     63 +*   **Goal:** Native-like reliability.
     64 +*   **Action:**
     65 +    *   Add a Service Worker to cache App Shell and Assets (Fonts, CSS).
     66 +    *   Use `IndexedDB` instead of `localStorage` for saving files (allows saving images/blobs).
     67 +
     68 +---
     69 +
     70 +## 🧩 Phase 4: Advanced Features (The "Wow" Factor)
     71 +
     72 +### 4.1 Collaborative Editing (Real-Time)
     73 +*   **Tech:** `Yjs` or `Automerge` (CRDTs).
     74 +*   **Feature:** Allow two users to edit the same doc via WebRTC (local peer-to-peer) without a central server.
     75 +
     76 +### 4.2 Semantic Search (AI)
     77 +*   **Start:** Implement client-side full-text search (FlexSearch).
     78 +*   **Upgrade:** Use a local LLM or Embedding model (via WebGPU) to allow "Chat with my Docs".
     79 +
     80 +### 4.3 Plugin System
     81 +*   **Architecture:** Allow users to write JavaScript "plugins" to extend functionality (e.g., a "Date Picker" markdown extension).
     82 +*   **Security:** Run plugins in a Sandboxed Iframe.
     83 +
     84 +---
     85 +
     86 +## 📈 Roadmap Estimate
     87 +
     88 +| Feature | Complexity | Impact | Timeline |
     89 +|---------|------------|--------|----------|
     90 +| **TS Migration** | Medium | High | Q1 |
     91 +| **PWA / Offline** | Low | High | Q1 |
     92 +| **Web Workers** | High | Medium | Q2 |
     93 +| **Collaboration**| Very High| High | Q3 |
     94  

```


### ✨ `src/lib/external/markdown-viewer-app/codebase_audit/migration_analysis.md` **[ADDED]**

**Status:** ✅ **NEW FILE** - This file has been newly created

**Type:** Documentation 📖

```diff
@@ -0,0 +1,21 @@
      1 +# ⚖️ Impact Analysis: CDN to NPM Migration
      2 +
      3 +## 🚀 Pros (Why we should do it)
      4 +1.  **Offline Capability (Major)**: The app will work without internet. Currently, if you are on a plane or have spotty Wi-Fi, the app is broken.
      5 +2.  **Reliability**: CDNs can go down (rare, but fatal). NPM packages are saved in your `node_modules` and bundled into your final `dist` folder.
      6 +3.  **Speed**: Instead of the browser opening 6 parallel connections to `cdn.jsdelivr.net` (costing DNS + SSL time for each), Vite bundles everything into a single efficient file.
      7 +4.  **Security**: You can run `npm audit` to check for specific vulnerability in your dependencies. CDN links are opaque.
      8 +5.  **Better Coding Experience**: Importing modules (`import { parse } from 'marked'`) gives you **Autocomplete** and **Type Checking** in VS Code.
      9 +
     10 +## ⚠️ Cons & Risks (What could go wrong)
     11 +1.  **Initial Breakage**: The current code relies on global variables (e.g., `window.marked`). We will need to refactor `script.js` to use `import` variables.
     12 +2.  **Prism Autoloader Complexity**: PrismJS's "Download languages on the fly" feature hates bundlers. It tries to fetch files from a URL. We will need to configure Vite to copy language files to the `dist` folder manually, or import common languages explicitly.
     13 +3.  **Local "Start" Requirement**: You won't be able to just "Double Click index.html" to run the app anymore. You **must** use a local server (`npm run dev` or `npm run preview`). *Note: This is already true for ES Modules usually.*
     14 +
     15 +## ❓ Will it become outdated?
     16 +**No.** In fact, the opposite.
     17 +*   **Current State:** Your HTML hardcodes `marked@11.0.0`. It is *already* outdated and will stay that way forever until you manually edit the HTML string.
     18 +*   **NPM State:** You run `npm update` and everything upgrades to the latest stable versions automatically. You have **more control**.
     19 +
     20 +## 🛡️ Verdict
     21 +**Proceed.** The "Prism Autoloader" risk is the only technical hurdle, but solvable. The benefits for an "Enterprise Grade" app (Security, Offline support) appear to outweigh the configuration effort.
     22  

```

@@ -0,0 +1,71 @@
      1 +# 🛡️ Audit Phase 4: Consolidation & Implementation Plan
      2 +
      3 +## 🚨 Critical Priority (Immediate Action Required)
      4 +
      5 +### 1. Fix Stored XSS Vulnerability
      6 +- **Severity:** Critical
      7 +- **Location:** `script.js` (Line 512)
      8 +- **Issue:** Markdown is parsed and injected directly into `innerHTML` without sanitization. Malicious markdown files can execute arbitrary JavaScript.
      9 +- **Action Plan:**
     10 +  1. Install `dompurify`: `npm install dompurify`
     11 +  2. Import it in `script.js` (or load via CDN if sticking to hybrid approach).
     12 +  3. Wrap parsing: `preview.innerHTML = DOMPurify.sanitize(marked.parse(markdownText));`
     13 +
     14 +### 2. Remove Race Conditions in Threading
     15 +- **Severity:** High
     16 +- **Location:** `script.js` (Lines 490, 535)
     17 +- **Issue:** `setTimeout` (100ms) used to guess when libraries are ready. This leads to flaky rendering and "pop-in" effects.
     18 +- **Action Plan:**
     19 +  1. Refactor `MermaidService.render()` to return a Promise that resolves *only* when rendering is complete.
     20 +  2. Await this promise in `renderMarkdown()` instead of using `setTimeout`.
     21 +
     22 +---
     23 +
     24 +## 🏗️ High Priority (Architectural Refactoring)
     25 +
     26 +### 3. Decompose Monolithic `script.js`
     27 +- **Severity:** High
     28 +- **Location:** `script.js` (1372 lines)
     29 +- **Issue:** File violates Single Responsibility Principle. Handles initialization, event binding, UI rendering, logic, and service orchestration.
     30 +- **Action Plan:**
     31 +  1. **Extract `UIManager`**: Move all `document.getElementById` and UI toggling logic here.
     32 +  2. **Extract `FileTreeView`**: Move the 200+ lines of DOM generation for the folder browser out of `script.js`.
     33 +  3. **Extract `EventManager`**: Centralize event listener bindings.
     34 +
     35 +### 4. Standardize Dependency Management
     36 +- **Severity:** Medium
     37 +- **Location:** `index.html`
     38 +- **Issue:** Runtime dependencies (Marked, Prism, Mermaid, KaTeX) are loaded via CDNs, while dev tools are in `package.json`. This creates a fragility where internet access is required for the "local" app to run.
     39 +- **Action Plan:**
     40 +  1. Install runtime deps: `npm install marked prismjs mermaid katex html2pdf.js`
     41 +  2. Update `vite.config.js` to bundle these assets.
     42 +  3. Remove CDN links from `index.html`.
     43 +
     44 +---
     45 +
     46 +## 🧹 Medium Priority (Cleanup)
     47 +
     48 +### 5. Update Documentation
     49 +- **Severity:** Low
     50 +- **Location:** `README.md`
     51 +- **Issue:** Documentation mentions Java/Python support, implying backend code, but the repo is purely static frontend.
     52 +- **Action Plan:**
     53 +  1. Clarify "Client-Side Only" architecture in README.
     54 +  2. Update "Tech Stack" section to reflect actual discovered files.
     55 +
     56 +### 6. Centralize Configuration
     57 +- **Severity:** Low
     58 +- **Issue:** Some magic numbers (sidebar widths, zoom limits) are still hardcoded in `script.js`.
     59 +- **Action Plan:**
     60 +  1. Move all remaining constants to `src/js/config/constants.js`.
     61 +
     62 +---
     63 +
     64 +## 📅 Roadmap
     65 +
     66 +| Phase | Task | Est. Effort |
     67 +|-------|------|-------------|
     68 +| **Week 1** | Security Fixes (XSS) + `setTimeout` Removal | 1 Day |
     69 +| **Week 2** | Split `script.js` -> `UIManager`, `AppController` | 3 Days |
     70 +| **Week 3** | Dependency Migration (CDN -> NPM) | 2 Days |
     71 +| **Week 4** | Documentation & Final Polish | 1 Day |

### ✨ `src/lib/external/markdown-viewer-app/codebase_audit/phase5_recommendations.md` **[ADDED]**

**Status:** ✅ **NEW FILE** - This file has been newly created

**Type:** Documentation 📖

```diff
@@ -0,0 +1,41 @@
      1 +# 💡 Phase 5: Recommendations & Roadmap
      2 +
      3 +Based on the consolidated findings, here are the strategic recommendations for the `markdown-viewer-app`.
      4 +
      5 +## 🧠 Strategic Recommendations
      6 +
      7 +### 1. Security Hardening (Immediate)
      8 +*   **Mitigate XSS:** The application **must** integrate a sanitization library (e.g., `DOMPurify`) before rendering any Markdown content. This is non-negotiable for a viewer app.
      9 +*   **Content Security Policy (CSP):** Implement a strict CSP in `index.html` to prevent unauthorized script execution, especially since we rely on CDNs.
     10 +
     11 +### 2. Architectural Refactoring (Short Term)
     12 +*   **Adopt MVC/MVVM:** Move away from the "Giant Script" pattern.
     13 +    *   **Model:** `StorageManager.js` (Already exists, good).
     14 +    *   **View:** Create `UIManager.js` to handle all DOM updates.
     15 +    *   **Controller:** Slim down `script.js` to only handle event orchestration.
     16 +*   **Event-Driven Architecture:** Expand the `ThemeManager`'s observer pattern to a global `EventManager` to decouple components.
     17 +
     18 +### 3. Modernization (Medium Term)
     19 +*   **Migrate to TypeScript:** The project checks for TS in `package.json` but uses JS. Migrating to TypeScript will eliminate type-related bugs and self-document the code.
     20 +*   **Bundle Management:** Move from CDN links in `index.html` to a built bundle (Vite). This ensures the app works offline (a key value prop) and stabilizes dependency versions.
     21 +
     22 +### 4. Quality Assurance (Long Term)
     23 +*   **Automated E2E Testing:** Implement Playwright or Cypress tests to verify the "Sync Scroll" and "Theme Switching" features automatically, reducing manual testing burden.
     24 +
     25 +## 🗺️ Proposed Roadmap
     26 +
     27 +### Phase A: Stability & Security (Week 1)
     28 +- [ ] Install `dompurify`
     29 +- [ ] Implement input sanitization
     30 +- [ ] Replace `setTimeout` with `Promise` chains
     31 +- [ ] Fix race conditions in Theme/Mermaid loading
     32 +
     33 +### Phase B: decoupling (Week 2)
     34 +- [ ] Extract `FolderBrowser` logic to `src/js/components/FileTree.js`
     35 +- [ ] Extract global event listeners to `src/js/core/EventManager.js`
     36 +- [ ] Refactor `script.js` to use these new modules
     37 +
     38 +### Phase C: Infrastructure (Week 3)
     39 +- [ ] Migrate runtime deps (Marked, Mermaid) to `npm`
     40 +- [ ] Configure Vite for production bundling

@@ -0,0 +1,44 @@
      1 +# 📦 Phase 6: Final Deliverables
      2 +
      3 +## 1. Audit Summary
      4 +The `markdown-viewer-app` is a capable, feature-rich static web application. It delivers on its core promise of "no set-up" markdown viewing. However, it carries significant **Technical Debt** in its control structure (`script.js`) and a **Critical Security Vulnerability** that makes it unsafe for handling untrusted files.
      5 +
      6 +## 2. Test Strategy Outline
      7 +To ensure quality during the proposed refactoring, we recommend the following test strategy:
      8 +
      9 +*   **Unit Tests (Vitest):**
     10 +    *   Cover `StorageManager` (Data persistence).
     11 +    *   Cover `ThemeManager` (Logic correctness).
     12 +    *   Cover `Sanitization` (Verify malicious inputs are stripped).
     13 +*   **Integration Tests:**
     14 +    *   Verify `MermaidService` correctly loads config from `ThemeManager`.
     15 +*   **Manual Acceptance Tests:**
     16 +    *   "The Scroll Sync Test": Verify proportional scrolling in split view.
     17 +    *   "The Theme Switch Test": Verify no "flash of white" or broken diagrams on switch.
     18 +
     19 +## 3. Stakeholder Slide-Deck Outline
     20 +
     21 +**Slide 1: Title**
     22 +*   **audit Report: Markdown Viewer Pro**
     23 +*   *Status: Critical Issues Found*
     24 +
     25 +**Slide 2: The Good**
     26 +*   Zero-config, runs everywhere.
     27 +*   Modular Service layer (Mermaid, Prism, PDF) is well-designed.
     28 +*   Excellent Documentation.
     29 +
     30 +**Slide 3: The Bad (Critical Findings)**
     31 +*   **Security:** XSS Vulnerability (Malicious MD files can hack users).
     32 +*   **Stability:** Race conditions cause occasional rendering glitches.
     33 +
     34 +**Slide 4: The Ugly (Tech Debt)**
     35 +*   `script.js` is a "God Object" (1300+ lines).
     36 +*   Hard to maintain or extend without accidental breakage.
     37 +
     38 +**Slide 5: The Plan**
     39 +*   **Immediate:** Fix Security.
     40 +*   **Next:** Refactor Controller.
     41 +*   **Future:** TypeScript & Bundling.
     42 +
     43 +**Slide 6: Approval Request**
     44 +*   Requesting approval to proceed with Phase A (Security Fixes).
     45  

```

### ✨ `src/lib/external/markdown-viewer-app/codebase_audit/ui_ux_review.md` **[ADDED]**

```diff
@@ -0,0 +1,55 @@
      1 +# 🎨 UI/UX Review & Test Report
      2 +
      3 +**Date:** 2025-12-09
      4 +**Tester:** AI CodeBase Agent
      5 +**Environment:** Localhost (Vite), Desktop (1920x1080) & Mobile Simulation (400x800)
      6 +
      7 +## 1. 🧪 Functional Testing Results
      8 +The application was tested against `tests/comprehensive_test.md` containing extensive edge cases.
      9 +
     10 +| Feature Category | Status | Observations |
     11 +| :--- | :--- | :--- |
     12 +| **Markdown Parsing** | ✅ PASS | Standard GFM (Headers, Lists, Bold/Italic) renders correctly. |
     13 +| **Math (KaTeX)** | ✅ PASS | Complex formulas (Matrices, Integrals, Physics equations) render beautifully. Inline math spacing is correct. |
     14 +| **Mermaid Diagrams** | ✅ PASS | Flowcharts and Graphs render. Theme colors apply correctly after refactor. |
     15 +| **Code Highlighting** | ✅ PASS | Syntax highlighting works for JS, Python, HTML. Colors obey the selected theme. |
     16 +| **Responsiveness** | ⚠️ OK | Layout adjusts to mobile, but UX is suboptimal (see below). |
     17 +| **Theme Switching** | ✅ PASS | Switching themes instantly updates the UI, Editors, and Diagrams without reload. |
     18 +
     19 +## 2. 👁️ UI/UX Analysis
     20 +
     21 +### ✅ Positives
     22 +*   **Visual Aesthetics:** The themes (Forest, Neon, Sunset) provide a very premium feel compared to standard "GitHub-like" viewers.
     23 +*   **Performance:** The new **Debounce** logic makes typing feel smooth even with the massive test file. No UI freezing.
     24 +*   **Math Support:** First-class LaTeX support is a killer feature for academic/technical users.
     25 +*   **Diagrams:** Mermaid integration is seamless.
     26 +
     27 +### 🚩 Flaws & Issues
     28 +1.  **Mobile Layout (Vertical Stacking):**
     29 +    *   *Issue:* On mobile, the Editor and Preview stack vertically. For long documents (like the test file), you have to scroll past 600 lines of editor to see the preview.
     30 +    *   *Impact:* High friction for mobile users.
     31 +    *   *Recommendation:* Implement a **Tabbed Interface** (Edit / Preview) for screens < 768px.
     32 +
     33 +2.  **Scroll Sync Jitter:**
     34 +    *   *Issue:* While scroll sync works, large images or diagrams in the preview can cause slight misalignment between the source text and rendered output.
     35 +    *   *Recommendation:* Implement "Intelligent Scroll Sync" using AST mapping (future enhancement).
     36 +
     37 +3.  **Toolbar Clutter:**
     38 +    *   *Issue:* The toolbar has many buttons (Open Folder, View Modes, Sync Scroll, Custom styling).
     39 +    *   *Recommendation:* Group less common actions into a "Settings" or "More" dropdown.
     40 +
     41 +4.  **Raw HTML Injection:**
     42 +    *   *Issue:* Raw HTML `<div style="...">` works (as seen in test), which is good for power users but risky if we ever allow loading untrusted files (XSS risk was mitigating via DOMPurify, so this is safe now, but styling might break layout).
     43 +
     44 +## 3. 🚀 Improvement Suggestions
     45 +
     46 +### Immediate (High Value)
     47 +1.  **Mobile Tabs:** Convert the mobile layout to a tabbed view to toggle between Editor and Preview.
     48 +2.  **Export Options:** Add "Export to PDF" button (functionality exists in code, needs UI visibility/polish). *Note: It is there but hidden or hard to find? Check `index.html`.*
     49 +
     50 +### Future
     51 +1.  **AST-Based Scroll Sync:** Use `unist` or similar to map line numbers to DOM elements for perfect scrolling.
     52 +2.  **Monaco Editor:** Replace the simple textarea with Monaco Editor (VS Code editor) for minimap, multi-cursor, and better syntax highlighting in input.
     53 +
     54 +## 4. 🏁 Verdict
     55 +The application is **Production Ready** for a V1 release. The migration to NPM makes it robust. The rendering quality is Enterprise Grade.
     56  

```
