### ✨ `src/lib/external/markdown-viewer-app/docs/competitive_programming_constraints.md` **[ADDED]**

**Status:** ✅ **NEW FILE** - This file has been newly created

**Type:** Documentation 📖

```diff
@@ -0,0 +1,621 @@
      1 +# 🎯 Coding Interview & Competitive Programming Constraints Guide
      2 +
      3 +### 📝 2025-12-19
      4 +**Category**: `interview prep` | **Level**: `Essential` | **Time**: `15 min read`
      5 +
      6 +> **Master the numbers** that every competitive programmer and interviewee should know by heart!
      7 +
      8 +---
      9 +
     10 +## 📋 Table of Contents
     11 +
     12 +1. [Standard Assumptions](#-standard-assumptions)
     13 +2. [Integer Limits & Data Types](#-integer-limits--data-types)
     14 +3. [Array & Container Constraints](#-array--container-constraints)
     15 +4. [String Constraints](#-string-constraints)
     16 +5. [Time Complexity Limits](#-time-complexity-limits)
     17 +6. [Space Complexity Limits](#-space-complexity-limits)
     18 +7. [Common Primes & Mathematical Constants](#-common-primes--mathematical-constants)
     19 +8. [Edge Cases Checklist](#-edge-cases-checklist)
     20 +9. [Platform-Specific Constraints](#-platform-specific-constraints)
     21 +10. [Quick Reference Cheatsheet](#-quick-reference-cheatsheet)
     22 +
     23 +---
     24 +
     25 +## 🎯 Standard Assumptions
     26 +
     27 +### The Golden Rules
     28 +
     29 +| Assumption | Typical Value | Reasoning |
     30 +|------------|---------------|-----------|
     31 +| **Time Limit** | 1-2 seconds | ~10⁸ simple operations/second |
     32 +| **Memory Limit** | 256 MB | Standard competitive programming |
     33 +| **Max Input Size (n)** | 10⁵ to 10⁶ | Fits in memory, allows O(n log n) |
     34 +| **Max Integer Value** | 10⁹ | Fits in `int` |
     35 +| **Large Integer Value** | 10¹⁸ | Requires `long long` |
     36 +
     37 +### What to Ask in Interviews
     38 +
     39 +1. **Input size constraints?** (n ≤ ?)
     40 +2. **Value range?** (values ≤ ?)
     41 +3. **Can values be negative?**
     42 +4. **Are there duplicates?**
     43 +5. **Is input sorted?**
     44 +6. **Can input be empty?**
     45 +
     46 +---
     47 +
     48 +## 🔢 Integer Limits & Data Types
     49 +
     50 +### Standard Integer Ranges
     51 +
     52 +| Type | Bytes | Range | Max (~) | Use When |
     53 +|------|-------|-------|---------|----------|
     54 +| `int` | 4 | -2³¹ to 2³¹-1 | ±2.1×10⁹ | Default choice |
     55 +| `unsigned int` | 4 | 0 to 2³²-1 | 4.3×10⁹ | Non-negative only |
     56 +| `long long` | 8 | -2⁶³ to 2⁶³-1 | ±9.2×10¹⁸ | Large values |
     57 +| `unsigned long long` | 8 | 0 to 2⁶⁴-1 | 1.8×10¹⁹ | Very large non-negative |
     58 +
     59 +### Critical Constants (MEMORIZE!)
     60 +
     61 +```cpp
     62 +#include <climits>
     63 +
     64 +INT_MAX    =  2,147,483,647      // ≈ 2.1 × 10⁹
     65 +INT_MIN    = -2,147,483,648      // ≈ -2.1 × 10⁹
     66 +LLONG_MAX  =  9,223,372,036,854,775,807  // ≈ 9.2 × 10¹⁸
     67 +LLONG_MIN  = -9,223,372,036,854,775,808  // ≈ -9.2 × 10¹⁸
     68 +
     69 +// Quick mental math
     70 +INT_MAX   ≈ 2 × 10⁹    (2 billion)
     71 +LLONG_MAX ≈ 9 × 10¹⁸   (9 quintillion)
     72 +```
     73 +
     74 +### When to Use Which Type
     75 +
     76 +| Problem Constraint | Type to Use | Example |
     77 +|-------------------|-------------|---------|
     78 +| n ≤ 10⁵, values ≤ 10⁹ | `int` | Most problems |
     79 +| Values > 2×10⁹ | `long long` | Large sums, products |
     80 +| Sum of n elements, n ≤ 10⁵ | `long long` | 10⁵ × 10⁹ = 10¹⁴ |
     81 +| Product of elements | `long long` or modulo | Overflow danger! |
     82 +| n × n where n ≤ 10⁵ | `long long` | 10¹⁰ > INT_MAX |
     83 +
     84 +### ⚠️ Overflow Danger Zones
     85 +
     86 +```cpp
     87 +// ❌ OVERFLOW! (10⁵ × 10⁵ = 10¹⁰ > INT_MAX)
     88 +int n = 100000;
     89 +int result = n * n;  // WRONG!
     90 +
     91 +// ✅ SAFE
     92 +long long result = (long long)n * n;
     93 +long long result = 1LL * n * n;
     94 +
     95 +// ❌ OVERFLOW! (sum of 10⁵ elements each up to 10⁹)
     96 +int sum = 0;
     97 +for (int x : arr) sum += x;  // WRONG if arr is large!
     98 +
     99 +// ✅ SAFE
    100 +long long sum = 0;
    101 +for (int x : arr) sum += x;
    102 +```
    103 +
    104 +### Modular Arithmetic
    105 +
    106 +When problem says "answer modulo 10⁹+7":
    107 +
    108 +```cpp
    109 +const int MOD = 1e9 + 7;  // 1,000,000,007 (prime)
    110 +
    111 +// Addition
    112 +(a + b) % MOD
    113 +
    114 +// Subtraction (add MOD to avoid negative)
    115 +((a - b) % MOD + MOD) % MOD
    116 +
    117 +// Multiplication
    118 +(1LL * a * b) % MOD  // Cast to long long first!
    119 +
    120 +// Common modulo values
    121 +10⁹ + 7  = 1,000,000,007  // Most common (prime)
    122 +10⁹ + 9  = 1,000,000,009  // Also prime
    123 +998244353                  // FFT-friendly prime (2²³ × 7 × 17 + 1)
    124 +```
    125 +
    126 +---
    127 +
    128 +## 📊 Array & Container Constraints
    129 +
    130 +### Maximum Array Sizes
    131 +
    132 +| Memory | Max Elements (`int`) | Max Elements (`long long`) |
    133 +|--------|---------------------|---------------------------|
    134 +| 256 MB | ~64 million | ~32 million |
    135 +| 512 MB | ~128 million | ~64 million |
    136 +| 1 GB | ~256 million | ~128 million |
    137 +
    138 +**Formula:** Max elements = Memory / sizeof(type)
    139 +- 256 MB = 256 × 10⁶ bytes
    140 +- int array: 256 × 10⁶ / 4 = 64 × 10⁶
    141 +
    142 +### Typical Constraints by Problem Type
    143 +
    144 +| Problem Type | Typical n | Expected Complexity |
    145 +|--------------|-----------|-------------------|
    146 +| Easy | ≤ 10³ | O(n²) acceptable |
    147 +| Medium | ≤ 10⁵ | O(n log n) expected |
    148 +| Hard | ≤ 10⁶ | O(n) or O(n log n) |
    149 +| Very Hard | ≤ 10⁷ | O(n) only |
    150 +
    151 +### 2D Array Limits
    152 +
    153 +```cpp
    154 +// Max 2D array with 256MB memory
    155 +// n × m × sizeof(int) ≤ 256 × 10⁶
    156 +
    157 +// Safe limits:
    158 +int arr[1000][1000];     // 4 MB - ✅ Safe
    159 +int arr[5000][5000];     // 100 MB - ✅ Usually safe
    160 +int arr[10000][10000];   // 400 MB - ❌ Too large!
    161 +
    162 +// For larger grids, use vector (dynamic allocation)
    163 +vector<vector<int>> grid(n, vector<int>(m));
    164 +```
    165 +
    166 +### Container Memory Usage
    167 +
    168 +| Container | Memory per Element | Notes |
    169 +|-----------|-------------------|-------|
    170 +| `vector<int>` | 4 bytes | Most efficient |
    171 +| `deque<int>` | 4 bytes + overhead | Block allocation |
    172 +| `list<int>` | 4 + 16 bytes | Node pointers |
    173 +| `set<int>` | 4 + 32 bytes | Red-black tree |
    174 +| `unordered_set<int>` | 4 + ~8 bytes | Hash table |
    175 +| `map<int,int>` | 8 + 32 bytes | Red-black tree |
    176 +| `unordered_map<int,int>` | 8 + ~16 bytes | Hash table |
    177 +
    178 +---
    179 +
    180 +## 📝 String Constraints
    181 +
    182 +### String Length Limits
    183 +
    184 +| Constraint | Typical Value | Common Problems |
    185 +|------------|---------------|-----------------|
    186 +| Short strings | ≤ 100 | Brute force OK |
    187 +| Medium strings | ≤ 10⁵ | O(n) required |
    188 +| Long strings | ≤ 10⁶ | O(n) only |
    189 +| Multiple strings | Total length ≤ 10⁶ | Sum constraint |
    190 +
    191 +### Character Set Assumptions
    192 +
    193 +```cpp
    194 +// Lowercase letters only: 'a' to 'z' (26 chars)
    195 +int freq[26] = {0};
    196 +freq[ch - 'a']++;
    197 +
    198 +// All letters: 'A'-'Z', 'a'-'z' (52 chars)
    199 +// Usually case-insensitive or convert to one case
    200 +
    201 +// Digits: '0' to '9' (10 chars)
    202 +int digit = ch - '0';
    203 +
    204 +// ASCII printable: 32 to 126 (95 chars)
    205 +int freq[128] = {0};  // Safe for all ASCII
    206 +
    207 +// Unicode: Use std::string with UTF-8
    208 +// Careful: string[i] may not be a full character!
    209 +```
    210 +
    211 +### String Comparison Complexity
    212 +
    213 +```cpp
    214 +// Comparing two strings of length n and m
    215 +s1 == s2;           // O(min(n, m))
    216 +s1.compare(s2);     // O(min(n, m))
    217 +s1 < s2;            // O(min(n, m))
    218 +
    219 +// For multiple comparisons, use hashing
    220 +hash<string> hasher;
    221 +size_t h = hasher(s);
    222 +```
    223 +
    224 +---
    225 +
    226 +## ⏱️ Time Complexity Limits
    227 +
    228 +### Operations per Second
    229 +
    230 +| Operation Type | Operations/Second |
    231 +|---------------|-------------------|
    232 +| Simple arithmetic | ~10⁹ |
    233 +| Array access | ~10⁸ - 10⁹ |
    234 +| Vector operations | ~10⁸ |
    235 +| Set/Map operations | ~10⁷ |
    236 +| String operations | ~10⁷ |
    237 +| I/O (cin/cout) | ~10⁶ (without fast I/O) |
    238 +| I/O (fast I/O) | ~10⁷ |
    239 +
    240 +### Maximum n for Time Limits
    241 +
    242 +| Time Limit | O(n) | O(n log n) | O(n²) | O(n³) | O(2ⁿ) |
    243 +|------------|------|------------|-------|-------|-------|
    244 +| 1 second | 10⁸ | 10⁶-10⁷ | 10⁴ | 500 | 25 |
    245 +| 2 seconds | 2×10⁸ | 2×10⁷ | 1.4×10⁴ | 600 | 26 |
    246 +| 5 seconds | 5×10⁸ | 5×10⁷ | 2×10⁴ | 800 | 28 |
    247 +
    248 +### Quick Complexity Check
    249 +
    250 +```cpp
    251 +// Given n, what's the max acceptable complexity?
    252 +n ≤ 10     → O(n!) or O(2ⁿ) OK
    253 +n ≤ 20     → O(2ⁿ) OK, O(n!) too slow
    254 +n ≤ 100    → O(n³) OK
    255 +n ≤ 1000   → O(n²) OK
    256 +n ≤ 10⁵    → O(n log n) or better
    257 +n ≤ 10⁶    → O(n log n) risky, O(n) preferred
    258 +n ≤ 10⁸    → O(n) only
    259 +```
    260 +
    261 +### Reverse: Given Complexity, Max n
    262 +
    263 +| Complexity | Max n (1 sec) |
    264 +|------------|---------------|
    265 +| O(n!) | n ≤ 10 |
    266 +| O(2ⁿ) | n ≤ 20-25 |
    267 +| O(n³) | n ≤ 500 |
    268 +| O(n² log n) | n ≤ 1000 |
    269 +| O(n²) | n ≤ 5000-10000 |
    270 +| O(n√n) | n ≤ 10⁵ |
    271 +| O(n log n) | n ≤ 10⁶-10⁷ |
    272 +| O(n) | n ≤ 10⁸ |
    273 +| O(log n) | n ≤ 10¹⁸ |
    274 +| O(1) | n = anything |
    275 +
    276 +---
    277 +
    278 +## 💾 Space Complexity Limits
    279 +
    280 +### Memory Calculation
    281 +
    282 +```cpp
    283 +// Typical memory limits
    284 +256 MB = 256 × 10⁶ bytes = 64 × 10⁶ ints
    285 +512 MB = 512 × 10⁶ bytes = 128 × 10⁶ ints
    286 +
    287 +// Stack vs Heap
    288 +// Stack: Limited (~1-8 MB) - local variables, recursion
    289 +// Heap: Limited by problem constraint - new, vector
    290 +
    291 +// Recursion depth limit (stack)
    292 +// ~10⁴ - 10⁵ calls typically safe
    293 +// Deep recursion may cause stack overflow!
    294 +
    295 +// Tail recursion or iteration preferred for deep recursion
    296 +```
    297 +
    298 +### Data Structure Space
    299 +
    300 +| Structure | Space | Example |
    301 +|-----------|-------|---------|
    302 +| Array of n ints | 4n bytes | n = 10⁶ → 4 MB |
    303 +| n × n int matrix | 4n² bytes | n = 5000 → 100 MB |
    304 +| Adjacency list | O(V + E) | |
    305 +| Adjacency matrix | O(V²) | |
    306 +| Binary tree (n nodes) | ~32n bytes | Node + 2 pointers |
    307 +| Graph (V vertices, E edges) | V + E | Adjacency list |
    308 +
    309 +---
    310 +
    311 +## 🔢 Common Primes & Mathematical Constants
    312 +
    313 +### Primes to Know
    314 +
    315 +```cpp
    316 +// For modular arithmetic
    317 +10⁹ + 7 = 1,000,000,007  // Most common modulo (prime)
    318 +10⁹ + 9 = 1,000,000,009  // Alternative (prime)
    319 +998244353                 // NTT prime (2²³ × 7 × 17 + 1)
    320 +
    321 +// Small primes for hashing
    322 +31, 37, 53, 97, 131, 1009, 10007
    323 +
    324 +// For string hashing (rolling hash)
    325 +base = 31 or 37 (for lowercase letters)
    326 +base = 53 (for mixed case)
    327 +mod = 10⁹ + 7 or 10⁹ + 9
    328 +
    329 +// Largest prime ≤ n
    330 +// Under 100: 97
    331 +// Under 1000: 997
    332 +// Under 10000: 9973
    333 +// Under 10⁵: 99991
    334 +// Under 10⁶: 999983
    335 +// Under 10⁹: 999999937
    336 +```
    337 +
    338 +### Mathematical Constants
    339 +
    340 +```cpp
    341 +// For geometry and floating point
    342 +const double PI = acos(-1);        // 3.14159265358979...
    343 +const double PI = 3.14159265358979323846;
    344 +const double E = exp(1);           // 2.71828...
    345 +
    346 +// For comparison (floating point tolerance)
    347 +const double EPS = 1e-9;
    348 +if (abs(a - b) < EPS) // a == b
    349 +
    350 +// For "infinity" in algorithms
    351 +const int INF = 1e9;           // For int (won't overflow on add)
    352 +const int INF = INT_MAX / 2;   // Safe for addition
    353 +const long long INF = 1e18;    // For long long
    354 +const long long INF = LLONG_MAX / 2;
    355 +```
    356 +
    357 +### Useful Mathematical Facts
    358 +
    359 +```cpp
    360 +// Factorials
    361 +10! = 3,628,800             // Fits in int
    362 +12! = 479,001,600           // Last to fit in int
    363 +13! = 6,227,020,800         // Needs long long
    364 +20! ≈ 2.4 × 10¹⁸            // Last to fit in long long
    365 +21! overflows long long!
    366 +
    367 +// Powers of 2
    368 +2¹⁰ = 1,024 ≈ 10³
    369 +2²⁰ = 1,048,576 ≈ 10⁶
    370 +2³⁰ = 1,073,741,824 ≈ 10⁹
    371 +2³² = 4,294,967,296 ≈ 4 × 10⁹ (unsigned int max + 1)
    372 +2⁶⁴ ≈ 1.8 × 10¹⁹
    373 +
    374 +// Fibonacci
    375 +F(45) = 1,134,903,170       // Last to fit in int
    376 +F(92) = 7,540,113,804,746,346,429  // Last to fit in long long
    377 +
    378 +// Catalan numbers (combinatorics)
    379 +C(17) = 129,644,790         // Fits in int
    380 +C(35) = 3,116,285,494,907,301,262  // Fits in long long

    384 +
    385 +## ✅ Edge Cases Checklist
    386 +
    387 +### Array/Vector Edge Cases
    388 +
    389 +```cpp
    390 +// Always test:
    391 +□ Empty array (n = 0)
    392 +□ Single element (n = 1)
    393 +□ Two elements (n = 2)
    394 +□ All same elements
    395 +□ Already sorted (ascending)
    396 +□ Reverse sorted (descending)
    397 +□ Maximum size (n = max constraint)
    398 +□ Negative numbers
    399 +□ Zero values
    400 +□ INT_MAX / INT_MIN values
    401 +□ Duplicates at boundaries
    402 +```
    403 +
    404 +### String Edge Cases
    405 +
    406 +```cpp
    407 +// Always test:
    408 +□ Empty string (s = "")
    409 +□ Single character (s = "a")
    410 +□ All same character (s = "aaa")
    411 +□ Palindrome
    412 +□ All unique characters
    413 +□ Maximum length
    414 +□ Spaces/special characters (if allowed)
    415 +□ Case sensitivity (if relevant)
    416 +```
    417 +
    418 +### Graph Edge Cases
    419 +
    420 +```cpp
    421 +// Always test:
    422 +□ Empty graph (no edges)
    423 +□ Single node
    424 +□ Disconnected graph
    425 +□ Complete graph
    426 +□ Tree (n-1 edges)
    427 +□ Cycle
    428 +□ Self-loop (if allowed)
    429 +□ Multiple edges between same nodes
    430 +□ Negative edge weights (if allowed)
    431 +□ All edges same weight
    432 +```
    433 +
    434 +### Tree Edge Cases
    435 +
    436 +```cpp
    437 +// Always test:
    438 +□ Empty tree (null root)
    439 +□ Single node
    440 +□ Skewed tree (all left or all right)
    441 +□ Perfect/complete binary tree
    442 +□ Maximum depth
    443 +□ All same values
    444 +□ Negative values (if allowed)
    445 +```
    446 +
    447 +### Number Edge Cases
    448 +
    449 +```cpp
    450 +// Always test:
    451 +□ Zero (0)
    452 +□ Negative zero (-0 for floating point)
    453 +□ INT_MAX (2,147,483,647)
    454 +□ INT_MIN (-2,147,483,648)
    455 +□ Powers of 2
    456 +□ One less than power of 2
    457 +□ Prime numbers
    458 +□ Perfect squares
    459 +□ Negative numbers
    460 +□ Very small positive (1)
    461 +□ Very large (max constraint)
    462 +```
    463 +
    464 +### Binary Search Edge Cases
    465 +
    466 +```cpp
    467 +// Always test:
    468 +□ Target at index 0
    469 +□ Target at last index
    470 +□ Target not in array
    471 +□ Target smaller than all elements
    472 +□ Target larger than all elements
    473 +□ All elements are target
    474 +□ Single element equals target
    475 +□ Single element doesn't equal target
    476 +□ Two elements
    477 +```
    478 +
    479 +---
    480 +
    481 +## 🖥️ Platform-Specific Constraints
    482 +
    483 +### LeetCode
    484 +
    485 +```cpp
    486 +// Typical constraints
    487 +n ≤ 10⁵ (most problems)
    488 +n ≤ 10³ (allows O(n²))
    489 +n ≤ 10⁴ (O(n²) risky)
    490 +Values: -10⁹ to 10⁹ (fits in int)
    491 +
    492 +// Time limit: Usually generous
    493 +// Memory: 256 MB typical
    494 +
    495 +// Fast I/O not needed (uses function calls)
    496 +```
    497 +
    498 +### Codeforces
    499 +
    500 +```cpp
    501 +// Typical constraints
    502 +n ≤ 2 × 10⁵ (common)
    503 +n ≤ 10⁶ (harder problems)
    504 +Time: 1-2 seconds
    505 +Memory: 256 MB (standard)
    506 +
    507 +// Fast I/O REQUIRED for large input
    508 +ios::sync_with_stdio(false);
    509 +cin.tie(nullptr);
    510 +```
    511 +
    512 +### HackerRank
    513 +
    514 +```cpp
    515 +// Varies by problem
    516 +// Often has multiple test cases
    517 +// Time limits can be strict
    518 +// Fast I/O recommended
    519 +
    520 +// Multiple test cases pattern
    521 +int t;
    522 +cin >> t;
    523 +while (t--) {
    524 +    // solve
    525 +}
    526 +```
    527 +
    528 +### Google/FAANG Interviews
    529 +
    530 +```cpp
    531 +// Focus on:
    532 +- Optimal time complexity
    533 +- Clean, readable code
    534 +- Handle all edge cases
    535 +- Discuss trade-offs
    536 +
    537 +// Typical expectations:
    538 +n ≤ 10⁵ to 10⁶
    539 +Time: O(n) or O(n log n)
    540 +Space: O(1) to O(n)
    541 +```
    542 +
    543 +---
    544 +
    545 +## 📋 Quick Reference Cheatsheet
    546 +
    547 +### Numbers to Memorize
    548 +
    549 +| Value | Meaning | Use Case |
    550 +|-------|---------|----------|
    551 +| 10⁹ | ~INT_MAX / 2 | Safe int limit |
    552 +| 2 × 10⁹ | ~INT_MAX | Max positive int |
    553 +| 10¹⁸ | ~LLONG_MAX / 9 | Safe long long |
    554 +| 10⁹ + 7 | Common modulo | Modular arithmetic |
    555 +| 10⁵ | Typical n limit | O(n log n) problems |
    556 +| 10⁴ | O(n²) threshold | When O(n²) is OK |
    557 +| 20-25 | 2ⁿ threshold | Bitmask/subset problems |
    558 +| 10 | n! threshold | Permutation problems |
    559 +
    560 +### Quick Type Selection
    561 +
    562 +```cpp
    563 +// Default
    564 +int x;                  // Values ≤ 10⁹
    565 +
    566 +// Large values
    567 +long long x;           // Values > 2×10⁹
    568 +
    569 +// Large sums
    570 +long long sum = 0;     // Sum of many ints
    571 +
    572 +// Products
    573 +long long prod = 1LL * a * b;  // Multiply ints
    574 +
    575 +// Modular
    576 +const int MOD = 1e9 + 7;
    577 +((1LL * a * b) % MOD)
    578 +```
    579 +
    580 +### Fast I/O Template
    581 +
    582 +```cpp
    583 +#include <bits/stdc++.h>
    584 +using namespace std;
    585 +
    586 +int main() {
    587 +    ios::sync_with_stdio(false);
    588 +    cin.tie(nullptr);
    589 +
    590 +    // Your code here
    591 +
    592 +    return 0;
    593 +}
    594 +```
    595 +
    596 +### Infinity Values
    597 +
    598 +```cpp
    599 +// For shortest path, DP
    600 +const int INF = 1e9;           // int infinity
    601 +const long long INF = 1e18;    // long long infinity
    602 +
    603 +// For comparisons (safe for addition)
    604 +const int INF = INT_MAX / 2;
    605 +const long long INF = LLONG_MAX / 2;
    606 +```
    607 +
    608 +---
    609 +
    610 +## 🎯 Interview Tips
    611 +
    612 +1. **Always ask for constraints first** - Determines algorithm choice
    613 +2. **State assumptions explicitly** - "I'm assuming n ≤ 10⁵"
    614 +3. **Check for overflow** - Especially with multiplication and sums
    615 +4. **Use appropriate data types** - `long long` when in doubt
    616 +5. **Test edge cases mentally** - Before coding, walk through edge cases
    617 +6. **Know your constants** - INT_MAX, 10⁹+7, complexity thresholds
    618 +
    619 +---
    620 +
    621 +*Last Updated: December 19, 2025*

@@ -0,0 +1,401 @@
      1 +# Product Context: Markdown Viewer Pro
      2 +
      3 +## Problem Statement
      4 +
      5 +Technical writers, developers, documentation specialists, and content creators face friction in their markdown workflows:
      6 +
      7 +1. **Preview Fragmentation**: Switching between editor and preview requires multiple tools or windows
      8 +2. **Styling Inconsistency**: Generic markdown renderers lack professional theming and customization
      9 +3. **Setup Overhead**: Existing solutions require installation, configuration, or backend infrastructure
     10 +4. **Export Complexity**: Sharing rendered markdown requires complex build processes or platform lock-in
     11 +5. **Visual Preference Limitations**: Most tools offer limited or no theme customization options
     12 +
     13 +## Value Proposition
     14 +
     15 +**Markdown Viewer Pro** eliminates workflow friction by providing an instant, zero-setup markdown environment that combines professional rendering, extensive theming, and seamless export—all in a single HTML file.
     16 +
     17 +### Core Value Drivers
     18 +
     19 +1. **Instant Gratification**: Open file → start working. Zero configuration, zero installation.
     20 +2. **Visual Excellence**: 10 professionally designed themes ensure content looks presentation-ready
     21 +3. **True Portability**: Export to self-contained HTML files that work anywhere
     22 +4. **Workflow Integration**: Fits seamlessly into existing development and documentation processes
     23 +5. **Customization Freedom**: Visual theme editor empowers users to create personalized experiences
     24 +
     25 +## Target Users & Personas
     26 +
     27 +### Primary Persona: Technical Writer
     28 +
     29 +**Background**: Creates documentation, tutorials, and technical guides
     30 +
     31 +**Pain Points**:
     32 +
     33 +- Needs to preview formatting while writing
     34 +- Requires professional-looking output
     35 +- Works across multiple projects with different style guides
     36 +- Must share documentation with non-technical stakeholders
     37 +
     38 +**Use Cases**:
     39 +
     40 +- Writing API documentation
     41 +- Creating README files
     42 +- Drafting technical blog posts
     43 +- Preparing training materials
     44 +
     45 +**Value Received**: Real-time preview with professional themes + easy export for sharing
     46 +
     47 +---
     48 +
     49 +### Secondary Persona: Software Developer
     50 +
     51 +**Background**: Writes code documentation, README files, and project notes
     52 +
     53 +**Pain Points**:
     54 +
     55 +- Needs quick markdown preview during development
     56 +- Wants syntax highlighting for code examples
     57 +- Requires consistent rendering across platforms
     58 +- Values speed and simplicity over features
     59 +
     60 +**Use Cases**:
     61 +
     62 +- Writing README.md files
     63 +- Documenting API endpoints
     64 +- Creating architectural decision records (ADRs)
     65 +- Drafting release notes
     66 +
     67 +**Value Received**: Fast, reliable rendering with excellent code syntax support
     68 +
     69 +---
     70 +
     71 +### Tertiary Persona: Content Creator
     72 +
     73 +**Background**: Bloggers, educators, and writers using markdown for content creation
     74 +
     75 +**Pain Points**:
     76 +
     77 +- Needs distraction-free writing environment
     78 +- Wants attractive visual presentation
     79 +- Requires flexibility to match personal brand
     80 +- Must export to various formats
     81 +
     82 +**Use Cases**:
     83 +
     84 +- Drafting blog posts
     85 +- Creating course materials
     86 +- Writing newsletters
     87 +- Preparing presentations
     88 +
     89 +**Value Received**: Beautiful themes + customization + clean export
     90 +
     91 +---
     92 +
     93 +### Tertiary Persona: Student/Researcher
     94 +
     95 +**Background**: Takes notes, writes papers, and creates study materials
     96 +
     97 +**Pain Points**:
     98 +
     99 +- Needs organized note-taking system
    100 +- Wants mathematical notation and diagrams
    101 +- Requires offline access
    102 +- Values simplicity and reliability
    103 +
    104 +**Use Cases**:
    105 +
    106 +- Taking lecture notes
    107 +- Creating study guides
    108 +- Organizing research notes
    109 +- Preparing presentations
    110 +
    111 +**Value Received**: Mermaid diagram support + reliable auto-save + offline capability
    112 +
    113 +## User Experience Goals
    114 +
    115 +### Cognitive Load Minimization
    116 +
    117 +- **Zero Learning Curve**: Intuitive split-pane design requires no explanation
    118 +- **Immediate Feedback**: Changes appear instantly (<100ms)
    119 +- **Consistent Patterns**: All controls behave predictably
    120 +- **Visual Clarity**: Clear information hierarchy and typography
    121 +
    122 +### Workflow Efficiency
    123 +
    124 +- **Single-File Deployment**: No setup or installation friction
    125 +- **Persistent State**: Auto-save prevents data loss
    126 +- **Keyboard Accessibility**: Common actions accessible via keyboard
    127 +- **Fast Theme Switching**: Instant theme changes without page reload
    128 +
    129 +### Creative Freedom
    130 +
    131 +- **10 Professional Themes**: Curated color palettes for different contexts
    132 +- **Visual Customizer**: Non-technical users can create custom themes
    133 +- **Live Preview**: See customization changes in real-time
    134 +- **Save & Share**: Custom themes persist and can be reused
    135 +
    136 +### Output Quality
    137 +
    138 +- **Professional Rendering**: Typography and spacing match published standards
    139 +- **Syntax Highlighting**: Code blocks are properly formatted and colored
    140 +- **Diagram Support**: Mermaid integration for technical diagrams
    141 +- **Clean Exports**: HTML output is self-contained and portable
    142 +
    143 +## User Journey Map
    144 +
    145 +### Discovery Phase
    146 +
    147 +1. User searches for "markdown viewer" or "markdown editor"
    148 +2. Finds Markdown Viewer Pro via search or recommendation
    149 +3. Downloads single HTML file or opens hosted version
    150 +
    151 +**Friction Points**: None (zero setup required)
    152 +
    153 +---
    154 +
    155 +### Onboarding Phase
    156 +
    157 +1. Opens `index.html` in browser
    158 +2. Sees split-pane interface with sample content
    159 +3. Immediately understands editor (left) and preview (right) model
    160 +4. Explores theme dropdown and sees instant visual changes
    161 +
    162 +**Key Moment**: First markdown render appears instantly
    163 +
    164 +**Success Metric**: User understands interface within 30 seconds
    165 +
    166 +---
    167 +
    168 +### Core Usage Phase
    169 +
    170 +1. Clears sample content and starts writing
    171 +2. Types markdown and sees immediate preview updates
    172 +3. Switches themes to find preferred visual style
    173 +4. Content auto-saves to localStorage
    174 +5. Exports finished document to HTML
    175 +
    176 +**Key Moments**:
    177 +
    178 +- First successful export
    179 +- Discovery of theme customizer
    180 +- Realization that content persists across sessions
    181 +
    182 +**Success Metrics**:
    183 +
    184 +- User returns for subsequent sessions
    185 +- User explores theme options
    186 +- User successfully exports documents
    187 +
    188 +---
    189 +
    190 +### Power User Phase
    191 +
    192 +1. Creates custom theme matching personal/brand preferences
    193 +2. Uses for multiple document types (docs, notes, blog posts)
    194 +3. Integrates into regular workflow
    195 +4. Shares tool with colleagues/friends
    196 +
    197 +**Key Moments**:
    198 +
    199 +- Creation of first custom theme
    200 +- First workflow integration
    201 +- First recommendation to others
    202 +
    203 +**Success Metrics**:
    204 +
    205 +- Multiple custom themes created
    206 +- Daily usage patterns
    207 +- Organic sharing and recommendations
    208 +
    209 +## Pain Points Being Solved
    210 +
    211 +### Before Markdown Viewer Pro
    212 +
    213 +| Problem | User Impact | Business Cost |
    214 +|---------|------------|---------------|
    215 +| Need separate editor and preview tools | Context switching friction | Lost productivity |
    216 +| Markdown renders differently across platforms | Inconsistent output | Rework and frustration |
    217 +| Complex setup processes | Time waste, barrier to entry | Adoption friction |
    218 +| Generic, unattractive rendering | Unprofessional output | Brand damage |
    219 +| No theme customization | Can't match style guides | Manual styling overhead |
    220 +| Complicated export processes | Sharing friction | Communication delays |
    221 +
    222 +### After Markdown Viewer Pro
    223 +
    224 +| Solution | User Benefit | Business Value |
    225 +|----------|--------------|----------------|
    226 +| Unified editor + preview | Instant feedback loop | Faster document creation |
    227 +| Consistent rendering engine | Predictable output | Quality assurance |
    228 +| Zero-setup deployment | Immediate productivity | No onboarding cost |
    229 +| 10 professional themes | Presentation-ready output | Professional appearance |
    230 +| Visual theme customizer | Brand alignment without code | Consistent branding |
    231 +| One-click HTML export | Easy sharing | Efficient collaboration |
    232 +
    233 +## Success Metrics & KPIs
    234 +
    235 +### User Engagement
    236 +
    237 +- **Session Duration**: Average time spent per session
    238 +- **Return Rate**: Percentage of users who return within 7 days
    239 +- **Feature Adoption**: % of users who try theme switching, customization, export
    240 +
    241 +### User Satisfaction
    242 +
    243 +- **Task Completion Rate**: % of users who successfully export documents
    244 +- **Theme Exploration**: Average number of themes tried per session
    245 +- **Custom Theme Creation**: Number of custom themes created
    246 +
    247 +### Technical Performance
    248 +
    249 +- **Render Latency**: Time from keystroke to preview update (<100ms target)
    250 +- **Initial Load Time**: Time to interactive (<2s target)
    251 +- **Error Rate**: Frequency of rendering errors (target: <0.1%)
    252 +
    253 +### Business Outcomes
    254 +
    255 +- **Organic Growth**: Word-of-mouth recommendations and shares
    256 +- **Workflow Integration**: Users incorporate into daily routine
    257 +- **Professional Output**: Documents meet publication standards
    258 +
    259 +## Ethical Considerations
    260 +
    261 +### Privacy
    262 +
    263 +- **No Tracking**: Zero analytics or telemetry
    264 +- **Local Storage Only**: All data stays on user's device
    265 +- **No External Transmission**: Content never sent to servers
    266 +- **Transparent Data Handling**: Users know exactly where data is stored
    267 +
    268 +### Accessibility
    269 +
    270 +- **Color Contrast**: WCAG 2.1 AA compliance in all themes
    271 +- **Keyboard Navigation**: All features accessible without mouse
    272 +- **Screen Reader Support**: Semantic HTML for assistive technology
    273 +- **Responsive Design**: Works on tablets and larger devices
    274 +
    275 +### Inclusivity
    276 +
    277 +- **No Account Required**: No barriers to entry
    278 +- **Offline Capability**: Works without internet (after first load)
    279 +- **Free Forever**: No paywalls or feature restrictions
    280 +- **Open Standards**: Uses standard markdown syntax
    281 +
    282 +## Competitive Landscape
    283 +
    284 +### Direct Competitors
    285 +
    286 +**1. GitHub Markdown Preview**
    287 +
    288 +- **Strengths**: Integrated into workflow, familiar to developers
    289 +- **Weaknesses**: Platform lock-in, limited themes, no export
    290 +- **Our Advantage**: Standalone, 10 themes, HTML export
    291 +
    292 +**2. StackEdit**
    293 +
    294 +- **Strengths**: Feature-rich, cloud sync, multiple export formats
    295 +- **Weaknesses**: Requires account, complex UI, online-only
    296 +- **Our Advantage**: Zero setup, offline, simpler interface
    297 +
    298 +**3. Typora**
    299 +
    300 +- **Strengths**: WYSIWYG editing, native app, polished UI
    301 +- **Weaknesses**: Paid software, installation required, limited themes
    302 +- **Our Advantage**: Free, zero installation, extensive theming
    303 +
    304 +**4. Dillinger**
    305 +
    306 +- **Strengths**: Online, easy sharing, multiple export options
    307 +- **Weaknesses**: Requires internet, privacy concerns, generic styling
    308 +- **Our Advantage**: Offline, privacy-first, professional themes
    309 +
    310 +### Indirect Competitors
    311 +
    312 +- **VS Code with Preview Extension**: Developer-focused, requires setup
    313 +- **Notion**: All-in-one tool, complex, proprietary format
    314 +- **Obsidian**: Note-taking focus, requires vault setup
    315 +
    316 +### Differentiation Strategy
    317 +
    318 +**Key Differentiators**:
    319 +
    320 +1. **Single-File Deployment**: Unmatched simplicity
    321 +2. **Theme Excellence**: 10 professionally designed themes
    322 +3. **Visual Customizer**: Non-technical theme creation
    323 +4. **Zero Configuration**: Instant productivity
    324 +5. **Privacy-First**: No accounts, no tracking, local-only
    325 +
    326 +**Market Position**: The simplest, most beautiful markdown viewer for professionals who value speed, privacy, and visual quality.
    327 +
    328 +## User Feedback Integration
    329 +
    330 +### Potential User Requests
    331 +
    332 +**High Priority**:
    333 +
    334 +- Additional themes (solved: 10 themes available)
    335 +- Dark mode support (solved: every theme has dark variant)
    336 +- Export options (solved: HTML export implemented)
    337 +
    338 +**Medium Priority**:
    339 +
    340 +- PDF export (future consideration)
    341 +- Collaborative editing (out of scope)
    342 +- File import/drag-drop (enhancement opportunity)

      1 +# Project Brief: Markdown Viewer Pro
      2 +
      3 +## Core Mission
      4 +
      5 +Create a production-grade, standalone markdown viewer application that provides real-time preview, extensive theming capabilities, and professional rendering of markdown content with syntax highlighting and diagram support.
      6 +
      7 +## Strategic Objectives
      8 +
      9 +1. **Zero-Dependency Deployment**: Deliver a self-contained, browser-based application requiring no installation or backend infrastructure
     10 +2. **Superior Theming System**: Provide 10 professionally designed themes with intuitive customization capabilities
     11 +3. **Professional Markdown Rendering**: Support comprehensive markdown features including syntax highlighting for 20+ languages and Mermaid diagrams
     12 +4. **User Experience Excellence**: Ensure instant feedback, persistent state, and seamless workflow with export functionality
     13 +
     14 +## Explicit Acceptance Criteria
     15 +
     16 +### Functional Requirements
     17 +
     18 +- ✅ Real-time markdown rendering with <100ms latency
     19 +- ✅ Support all standard markdown syntax (headers, lists, links, images, tables, blockquotes, code)
     20 +- ✅ Syntax highlighting for 20+ programming languages
     21 +- ✅ Mermaid diagram rendering (flowcharts, sequence, class, state, ER, Gantt, pie)
     22 +- ✅ 10 distinct themes (5 families × light/dark variants)
     23 +- ✅ Visual color customizer with live preview
     24 +- ✅ Export to standalone HTML with embedded styling
     25 +- ✅ Auto-save functionality using localStorage
     26 +- ✅ Custom theme persistence
     27 +
     28 +### Non-Functional Requirements
     29 +
     30 +#### Performance
     31 +
     32 +- Initial load time: <2 seconds on standard connection
     33 +- Rendering latency: <100ms for typical markdown documents
     34 +- Smooth scrolling at 60fps
     35 +- Memory footprint: <50MB for typical usage
     36 +
     37 +#### Usability
     38 +
     39 +- Zero learning curve - intuitive split-pane interface
     40 +- Keyboard-accessible controls
     41 +- Responsive design for tablets (768px+)
     42 +- Clear visual hierarchy and information architecture
     43 +
     44 +#### Maintainability
     45 +
     46 +- Separation of concerns: HTML structure, CSS styling, JS behavior
     47 +- Modular theme system with CSS custom properties
     48 +- Single-file architecture for easy deployment
     49 +- Comprehensive inline documentation
     50 +
     51 +#### Browser Compatibility
     52 +
     53 +- Chrome/Edge 90+ (primary target)
     54 +- Firefox 88+
     55 +- Safari 14+
     56 +- Opera 76+
     57 +
     58 +#### Security
     59 +
     60 +- No external data transmission
     61 +- Client-side only execution
     62 +- Safe handling of user-generated content
     63 +- XSS prevention in markdown rendering
     64 +
     65 +## Project Scope
     66 +
     67 +### In Scope
     68 +
     69 +- Real-time markdown editing and preview
     70 +- Comprehensive markdown feature support
     71 +- Professional syntax highlighting
     72 +- Mermaid diagram integration
     73 +- Theme system with 10 built-in themes
     74 +- Custom theme creation and persistence
     75 +- HTML export with embedded styling
     76 +- localStorage persistence for content and preferences
     77 +- Responsive design for desktop and tablet
     78 +
     79 +### Out of Scope
     80 +
     81 +- Backend server or database
     82 +- User authentication or multi-user support
     83 +- Collaborative editing features
     84 +- Version control integration
     85 +- Mobile-first design (tablet minimum)
     86 +- File system access (uses copy/paste workflow)
     87 +- Markdown table-of-contents generation
     88 +- Spell checking or grammar tools
     89 +- PDF export (HTML only)
     90 +- Image upload or hosting
     91 +
     92 +## Success Criteria
     93 +
     94 +### Business Value
     95 +
     96 +1. **Instant Productivity**: Users can start working immediately without setup
     97 +2. **Professional Output**: Generated content is presentation-ready
     98 +3. **Workflow Integration**: Easily fits into documentation, note-taking, and content creation workflows
     99 +4. **Zero Cost Deployment**: Can be hosted on any static file server
    100 +
    101 +### User Value
    102 +
    103 +1. **Speed**: Instant feedback loop between writing and preview
    104 +2. **Customization**: Visual preferences accommodated through theming
    105 +3. **Portability**: Exported files are self-contained and shareable
    106 +4. **Reliability**: No data loss through auto-save functionality
    107 +
    108 +### Technical Excellence
    109 +
    110 +1. **Code Quality**: Maintainable, well-documented, production-grade code
    111 +2. **Performance**: Consistent 60fps rendering and <100ms updates
    112 +3. **Accessibility**: WCAG 2.1 AA color contrast ratios in all themes
    113 +4. **Zero Technical Debt**: Clean architecture with no known issues
    114 +
    115 +## Quality Gates
    116 +
    117 +Every release must pass:
    118 +
    119 +1. **Functional Testing**: All markdown features render correctly
    120 +2. **Cross-Browser Testing**: Works in all supported browsers
    121 +3. **Performance Benchmarks**: Meets latency and memory targets
    122 +4. **Theme Consistency**: All 10 themes display correctly
    123 +5. **Export Validation**: Generated HTML opens correctly in all browsers
    124 +6. **Accessibility Check**: Color contrast ratios meet WCAG standards
    125 +
    126 +## Project Boundaries
    127 +
    128 +### Technical Constraints
    129 +
    130 +- Pure client-side JavaScript (ES6+)
    131 +- No build process required
    132 +- CDN dependencies for libraries (Marked.js, Prism.js, Mermaid.js)
    133 +- localStorage for persistence (no cookies or external storage)
    134 +
    135 +### Design Constraints
    136 +
    137 +- Split-pane layout (editor left, preview right)
    138 +- Toolbar at top
    139 +- Modal-based color customizer
    140 +- Maximum viewport width utilization
    141 +
    142 +### Performance Constraints
    143 +
    144 +- Maximum bundle size: N/A (CDN-loaded libraries)
    145 +- Maximum localStorage usage: 5MB typical
    146 +- Supports documents up to 10,000 lines
    147 +
    148 +## Definition of Done
    149 +
    150 +A feature or task is complete when:
    151 +
    152 +1. Code is written following SOLID principles
    153 +2. Functionality works in all target browsers
    154 +3. Code is documented with clear comments
    155 +4. Performance meets defined benchmarks
    156 +5. No console errors or warnings
    157 +6. localStorage persistence works correctly
    158 +7. Theme system compatibility verified
    159 +8. Responsive behavior tested
    160 +
    161 +The project is complete when:
    162 +
    163 +1. All acceptance criteria met
    164 +2. All 10 themes implemented and tested
    165 +3. Export functionality validated
    166 +4. README and QUICK-REFERENCE documentation complete
    167 +5. Zero known bugs or technical debt
    168 +6. Performance benchmarks achieved
    169 +7. Cross-browser compatibility confirmed
    170 +
    171 +## Risk Assessment
    172 +
    173 +### Low Risk
    174 +
    175 +- Technology stack maturity (established libraries)
    176 +- Scope clarity and stability
    177 +- No external dependencies or APIs
    178 +
    179 +### Medium Risk
    180 +

### ✨ `src/lib/external/markdown-viewer-app/memory-bank/systemPatterns.md` **[ADDED]**

**Status:** ✅ **NEW FILE** - This file has been newly created

**Type:** Documentation 📖

```diff
@@ -0,0 +1,717 @@
      1 +# System Patterns: Markdown Viewer Pro
      2 +
      3 +## Architecture Overview
      4 +
      5 +Markdown Viewer Pro follows a **client-side monolithic architecture** with strict separation of concerns. The entire application runs in the browser without any backend dependencies.
      6 +
      7 +### Core Architectural Principles
      8 +
      9 +1. **Zero Backend**: Pure client-side execution using browser APIs
     10 +2. **Separation of Concerns**: HTML (structure), CSS (presentation), JavaScript (behavior)
     11 +3. **Progressive Enhancement**: Core functionality works without JavaScript, enhanced experience with it
     12 +4. **Modular Theming**: CSS custom properties enable runtime theme switching
     13 +5. **Stateless Design**: No server-side state, all persistence via browser localStorage
     14 +
     15 +## System Architecture Diagram
     16 +
     17 +```
     18 +┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
     19 +│                     Browser Window                       │
     20 +│                                                           │
     21 +│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
     22 +│  │              Toolbar Component                      │ │
     23 +│  │  [Theme Selector] [Customize] [Export]             │ │
     24 +│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
     25 +│                                                           │
     26 +│  ┌────────────────────┐  ┌─────────────────────────────┐│
     27 +│  │  Editor Panel      │  │    Preview Panel            ││
     28 +│  │                    │  │                             ││
     29 +│  │  ┌──────────────┐ │  │  ┌───────────────────────┐ ││
     30 +│  │  │              │ │  │  │   Rendered HTML       │ ││
     31 +│  │  │   Textarea   │ │  │  │   + Syntax Highlight  │ ││
     32 +│  │  │   (Markdown) │ │  │  │   + Mermaid Diagrams  │ ││
     33 +│  │  │              │ │  │  │                       │ ││
     34 +│  │  └──────────────┘ │  │  └───────────────────────┘ ││
     35 +│  └────────────────────┘  └─────────────────────────────┘│
     36 +│                                                           │
     37 +│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
     38 +│  │          Theme Customizer Modal (Hidden)           │ │
     39 +│  │  [Color Pickers] [Reset] [Save Custom Theme]      │ │
     40 +│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
     41 +└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
     42 +         │                    │                    │
     43 +         ▼                    ▼                    ▼
     44 +   ┌──────────┐       ┌──────────┐        ┌──────────┐
     45 +   │ Marked.js│       │ Prism.js │        │ Mermaid  │
     46 +   │ (Parser) │       │ (Syntax) │        │(Diagrams)│
     47 +   └──────────┘       └──────────┘        └──────────┘
     48 +         │                    │                    │
     49 +         └────────────────────┴────────────────────┘
     50 +                              │
     51 +                              ▼
     52 +                      ┌───────────────┐
     53 +                      │  localStorage │
     54 +                      │  - content    │
     55 +                      │  - theme      │
     56 +                      │  - custom     │
     57 +                      └───────────────┘
     58 +```
     59 +
     60 +## Component Architecture
     61 +
     62 +### 1. Presentation Layer (HTML/CSS)
     63 +
     64 +**Responsibilities**:
     65 +
     66 +- Define semantic document structure
     67 +- Provide accessible HTML elements
     68 +- Implement responsive layout grid
     69 +- Establish visual styling framework
     70 +
     71 +**Key Components**:
     72 +
     73 +- `index.html`: Single-page application structure
     74 +- `style.css`: Layout, typography, component styling
     75 +- `themes/*.css`: Color palette definitions via CSS custom properties
     76 +
     77 +**Design Patterns**:
     78 +
     79 +- **CSS Custom Properties Pattern**: All colors defined as CSS variables
     80 +- **BEM-like Naming**: Component-based class naming (.toolbar, .editor-container)
     81 +- **Mobile-First Responsive**: Breakpoints for tablet/desktop layouts
     82 +
     83 +### 2. Business Logic Layer (JavaScript)
     84 +
     85 +**Responsibilities**:
     86 +
     87 +- Markdown parsing and rendering
     88 +- Theme management and switching
     89 +- User interaction handling
     90 +- State persistence
     91 +- Export functionality
     92 +
     93 +**Key Modules** (all in `script.js`):
     94 +
     95 +- `initializeApp()`: Bootstrap and dependency checking
     96 +- `setupEditor()`: Editor initialization and event binding
     97 +- `renderMarkdown()`: Markdown-to-HTML conversion pipeline
     98 +- `changeTheme()`: Theme loading and application
     99 +- `exportHTML()`: HTML document generation
    100 +- Event handlers for user interactions
    101 +
    102 +**Design Patterns**:
    103 +
    104 +- **Module Pattern**: Functions encapsulate specific responsibilities
    105 +- **Event-Driven Architecture**: User actions trigger event handlers
    106 +- **Pipeline Pattern**: Markdown → HTML → Syntax Highlighting → Mermaid
    107 +- **Observer Pattern**: Input event triggers preview update
    108 +
    109 +### 3. Data Layer (localStorage)
    110 +
    111 +**Responsibilities**:
    112 +
    113 +- Persist user content across sessions
    114 +- Store theme preferences
    115 +- Save custom theme configurations
    116 +
    117 +**Data Schema**:
    118 +
    119 +```javascript
    120 +localStorage = {
    121 +  "markdownContent": "string",      // Current editor content
    122 +  "selectedTheme": "string",        // Active theme identifier
    123 +  "customTheme": "JSON string"      // Custom color palette object
    124 +}
    125 +```
    126 +
    127 +## Data Flow Architecture
    128 +
    129 +### Primary Data Flows
    130 +
    131 +#### 1. Markdown Rendering Flow
    132 +
    133 +```
    134 +User Types
    135 +    ↓
    136 +Textarea Input Event
    137 +    ↓
    138 +renderMarkdown()
    139 +    ↓
    140 +marked.parse(text)
    141 +    ↓
    142 +Mermaid Block Detection & Replacement
    143 +    ↓
    144 +Set innerHTML
    145 +    ↓
    146 +Prism.highlightElement()
    147 +    ↓
    148 +Mermaid.render() (async)
    149 +    ↓
    150 +Visual Update
    151 +    ↓
    152 +localStorage.setItem()
    153 +```
    154 +
    155 +#### 2. Theme Switching Flow
    156 +
    157 +```
    158 +User Selects Theme
    159 +    ↓
    160 +Change Event Handler
    161 +    ↓
    162 +changeTheme(themeName)
    163 +    ↓
    164 +    ├─→ Custom Theme?
    165 +    │      ↓
    166 +    │   Load from localStorage
    167 +    │      ↓
    168 +    │   Apply inline CSS variables
    169 +    │
    170 +    └─→ Built-in Theme?
    171 +           ↓
    172 +        Update <link> href
    173 +           ↓
    174 +        Browser loads CSS file
    175 +           ↓
    176 +        Visual Update
    177 +    ↓
    178 +localStorage.setItem()
    179 +```
    180 +
    181 +#### 3. Export Flow
    182 +
    183 +```
    184 +User Clicks Export
    185 +    ↓
    186 +exportHTML()
    187 +    ↓
    188 +    ├─→ Fetch Current Theme CSS
    189 +    │      ↓
    190 +    │   Theme file or custom colors
    191 +    │
    192 +    └─→ Generate HTML Template
    193 +           ↓
    194 +        Embed CSS + Content
    195 +           ↓
    196 +        Create Blob
    197 +           ↓
    198 +        Trigger Download
    199 +```
    200 +
    201 +## Domain Boundaries
    202 +
    203 +### Core Domain: Markdown Processing
    204 +
    205 +**Responsibilities**:
    206 +
    207 +- Parse markdown syntax
    208 +- Generate HTML output
    209 +- Apply syntax highlighting
    210 +- Render diagrams
    211 +
    212 +**Dependencies**: Marked.js, Prism.js, Mermaid.js
    213 +
    214 +### Supporting Domain: Theme Management
    215 +
    216 +**Responsibilities**:
    217 +
    218 +- Load theme CSS files
    219 +- Apply custom color values
    220 +- Persist theme preferences
    221 +- Provide theme customization UI
    222 +
    223 +**Dependencies**: CSS custom properties, localStorage
    224 +
    225 +### Supporting Domain: User Interface
    226 +
    227 +**Responsibilities**:
    228 +
    229 +- Handle user input
    230 +- Display content
    231 +- Manage modal dialogs
    232 +- Provide controls
    233 +
    234 +**Dependencies**: DOM APIs, Event system
    235 +
    236 +### Supporting Domain: Persistence
    237 +
    238 +**Responsibilities**:
    239 +
    240 +- Save content to localStorage
    241 +- Restore content on load
    242 +- Manage storage quota
    243 +- Handle storage errors
    244 +
    245 +**Dependencies**: localStorage API
    246 +
    247 +## State Management Strategy
    248 +
    249 +### Application State
    250 +
    251 +**State Location**: Browser memory (DOM + JavaScript variables)
    252 +
    253 +**State Components**:
    254 +
    255 +1. **Editor State**: Textarea value (ephemeral, backed by localStorage)
    256 +2. **Preview State**: Rendered HTML (derived from editor state)
    257 +3. **Theme State**: Active theme identifier (persisted)
    258 +4. **Custom Theme State**: Color values JSON (persisted)
    259 +5. **Modal State**: Open/closed (ephemeral)
    260 +
    261 +**State Flow**:
    262 +
    263 +```
    264 +User Input → State Update → DOM Update → localStorage Sync
    265 +```
    266 +
    267 +**State Persistence Strategy**:
    268 +
    269 +- **Eager Write**: Save to localStorage on every input event
    270 +- **Lazy Read**: Load from localStorage only on page load
    271 +- **No Versioning**: Overwrite strategy (last write wins)
    272 +
    273 +## Inter-Component Communication
    274 +
    275 +### Communication Patterns
    276 +
    277 +1. **DOM Events**: User interactions propagate through event system
    278 +2. **Function Calls**: Direct function invocation for synchronous operations
    279 +3. **Callbacks**: Asynchronous operations use callbacks (Mermaid rendering)
    280 +4. **Global State**: Shared access to localStorage
    281 +
    282 +### Event Flow Diagram
    283 +
    284 +```
    285 +┌──────────────┐
    286 +│ User Action  │
    287 +└──────┬───────┘
    288 +       │
    289 +       ▼
    290 +┌──────────────┐
    291 +│ Event Listener│
    292 +└──────┬────────┘
    293 +       │
    294 +       ▼
    295 +┌──────────────┐
    296 +│ Handler Fn   │
    297 +└──────┬────────┘
    298 +       │
    299 +       ├─→ Update DOM
    300 +       ├─→ Call Helper Fn
    301 +       └─→ Save to Storage
    302 +```
    303 +
    304 +## Dependency Management Philosophy
    305 +
    306 +### External Dependencies
    307 +
    308 +**Philosophy**: Minimize dependencies, prefer battle-tested libraries, use CDN delivery
    309 +
    310 +**Core Dependencies**:
    311 +
    312 +1. **Marked.js** (v11.0.0): Markdown parsing
    313 +   - Rationale: Industry standard, reliable, actively maintained
    314 +   - Alternative considered: markdown-it (more complex)
    315 +
    316 +2. **Prism.js** (v1.29.0): Syntax highlighting
    317 +   - Rationale: Lightweight, extensive language support
    318 +   - Alternative considered: Highlight.js (heavier)
    319 +
    320 +3. **Mermaid.js** (v10.6.1): Diagram rendering
    321 +   - Rationale: Rich diagram types, good documentation
    322 +   - Alternative considered: PlantUML (requires backend)
    323 +
    324 +**Dependency Loading Strategy**:
    325 +
    326 +- CDN-first approach (jsDelivr/Cloudflare)
    327 +- `defer` attribute for non-blocking load
    328 +- Dependency availability check before initialization
    329 +- Graceful degradation if CDN fails
    330 +
    331 +### Zero Build Dependencies
    332 +
    333 +**Philosophy**: No build step, no npm packages, no compilation
    334 +
    335 +**Benefits**:
    336 +
    337 +- Instant deployment (single file)
    338 +- Zero setup time
    339 +- No version conflicts
    340 +- Maximum portability
    341 +
    342 +## Concurrency & Asynchronous Patterns
    343 +
    344 +### Asynchronous Operations
    345 +
    346 +1. **Mermaid Diagram Rendering**: Async with promise-based API
    347 +2. **Theme CSS Loading**: Async via browser's CSS engine
    348 +3. **Export Theme Fetching**: Async fetch API call
    349 +
    350 +### Concurrency Handling
    351 +
    352 +**Pattern**: Callback-based for Mermaid, promise-based for fetch
    353 +
    354 +```javascript
    355 +// Mermaid rendering - async callback
    356 +mermaid.render(id, code).then(result => {
    357 +    element.innerHTML = result.svg;
    358 +}).catch(err => {
    359 +    element.innerHTML = errorMessage;
    360 +});
    361 +
    362 +// Theme fetching - promise chain
    363 +fetch(`themes/${themeName}.css`)
    364 +    .then(response => response.text())
    365 +    .then(css => generateHTML(css))
    366 +    .catch(err => fallbackGeneration());
    367 +```
    368 +
    369 +**Race Condition Prevention**:
    370 +
    371 +- Mermaid renders have unique IDs
    372 +- Theme changes clear previous inline styles
    373 +- No concurrent writes to localStorage
    374 +
    375 +## Error Propagation & Recovery
    376 +
    377 +### Error Handling Strategy
    378 +
    379 +**Philosophy**: Fail gracefully, provide user feedback, maintain functionality
    380 +
    381 +### Error Categories & Handling
    382 +
    383 +#### 1. Dependency Load Failure
    384 +
    385 +```javascript
    386 +if (typeof marked === 'undefined') {
    387 +    console.error('Required libraries not loaded. Retrying...');
    388 +    setTimeout(initializeApp, 100);  // Retry
    389 +    return;
    390 +}
    391 +```
    392 +
    393 +**Recovery**: Retry mechanism with timeout
    394 +
    395 +#### 2. Markdown Parsing Error
    396 +
    397 +```javascript
    398 +try {
    399 +    html = marked.parse(markdownText);
    400 +} catch (error) {
    401 +    console.error('Render error:', error);
    402 +    preview.innerHTML = '<p style="color: red;">Error rendering markdown</p>';
    403 +}
    404 +```
    405 +
    406 +**Recovery**: Display error message, maintain UI
    407 +
    408 +#### 3. Mermaid Rendering Error
    409 +
    410 +```javascript
    411 +mermaid.render(id, code).catch(err => {
    412 +    element.innerHTML = '<p style="color: red;">Mermaid diagram error</p>';
    413 +});
    414 +```
    415 +
    416 +**Recovery**: Show error message, continue with other content
    417 +
    418 +#### 4. localStorage Quota Exceeded
    419 +
    420 +```javascript
    421 +try {
    422 +    localStorage.setItem('markdownContent', text);
    423 +} catch (e) {
    424 +    if (e.name === 'QuotaExceededError') {
    425 +        console.warn('Storage quota exceeded');
    426 +        // Notify user (future enhancement)
    427 +    }
    428 +}
    429 +```
    430 +
    431 +**Recovery**: Silent failure with console warning
    432 +
    433 +#### 5. Export Failure
    434 +
    435 +```javascript
    436 +fetch(`themes/${theme}.css`).catch(err => {
    437 +    console.error('Error loading theme:', err);
    438 +    generateHTML();  // Continue without theme CSS
    439 +});
    440 +```
    441 +
    442 +**Recovery**: Generate export without theme styling
    443 +
    444 +### Error Logging
    445 +
    446 +**Strategy**: Console logging only (no external error tracking)
    447 +
    448 +**Log Levels**:
    449 +
    450 +- `console.error()`: Critical failures
    451 +- `console.warn()`: Non-critical issues
    452 +- `console.log()`: Debugging information (minimal in production)
    453 +
    454 +## Scalability Considerations
    455 +
    456 +### Performance Optimization
    457 +
    458 +#### 1. Rendering Performance
    459 +
    460 +**Challenge**: Large documents (>5000 lines) may cause lag
    461 +
    462 +**Strategy**:
    463 +
    464 +- Debouncing not implemented (instant feedback prioritized)
    465 +- Browser's event loop handles rendering queue
    466 +- Virtual scrolling not needed (browser handles well)
    467 +
    468 +**Load Characteristics**: O(n) where n = document length
    469 +
    470 +#### 2. Theme Switching Performance
    471 +
    472 +**Strategy**: Instant switching via CSS file replacement
    473 +
    474 +**Load Characteristics**: O(1) - just a file reference change
    475 +
    476 +#### 3. localStorage Performance
    477 +
    478 +**Strategy**: Synchronous writes are acceptable for this use case
    479 +
    480 +**Constraint**: 5MB typical localStorage limit
    481 +
    482 +### Horizontal Scalability
    483 +
    484 +**N/A**: Single-user, client-side application. No horizontal scaling needed.
    485 +
    486 +### Vertical Scalability
    487 +
    488 +**Limitations**:
    489 +
    490 +- Browser memory limits (typically 1-2GB per tab)
    491 +- localStorage quota (5-10MB depending on browser)
    492 +- Maximum document size: ~10,000 lines practical limit
    493 +
    494 +## Design Patterns Applied
    495 +
    496 +### 1. Observer Pattern
    497 +
    498 +**Usage**: Editor input triggers preview updates
    499 +
    500 +```javascript
    501 +editor.addEventListener('input', renderMarkdown);
    502 +```
    503 +
    504 +### 2. Strategy Pattern
    505 +
    506 +**Usage**: Theme loading strategy (built-in vs custom)
    507 +
    508 +```javascript
    509 +if (themeName === 'custom') {
    510 +    applyCustomTheme();
    511 +} else {
    512 +    loadThemeFile(themeName);
    513 +}
    514 +```
    515 +
    516 +### 3. Template Method Pattern
    517 +
    518 +**Usage**: Export HTML generation
    519 +
    520 +```javascript
    521 +function generateHTML() {
    522 +    const template = `<!DOCTYPE html>...`;
    523 +    // Fill in theme and content
    524 +    return template;
    525 +}
    526 +```
    527 +
    528 +### 4. Singleton Pattern
    529 +
    530 +**Usage**: Single application instance per page
    531 +
    532 +```javascript
    533 +window.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function() {
    534 +    initializeApp();  // Called once
    535 +});
    536 +```
    537 +
    538 +### 5. Facade Pattern
    539 +
    540 +**Usage**: Simplified API over complex libraries
    541 +
    542 +```javascript
    543 +function renderMarkdown() {
    544 +    // Facade over Marked, Prism, Mermaid
    545 +    const html = marked.parse(text);
    546 +    applyPrism(html);
    547 +    renderMermaid(html);
    548 +}
    549 +```
    550 +
    551 +## Architectural Decisions (ADRs)
    552 +
    553 +### ADR-001: Client-Side Only Architecture
    554 +
    555 +**Decision**: Implement as pure client-side application with no backend
    556 +
    557 +**Rationale**:
    558 +
    559 +- Eliminates deployment complexity
    560 +- Ensures user privacy (no data transmission)
    561 +- Enables offline functionality
    562 +- Simplifies architecture
    563 +
    564 +**Trade-offs**:
    565 +
    566 +- ✅ Gains: Simplicity, privacy, portability
    567 +- ❌ Loses: Collaboration features, cloud sync
    568 +
    569 +---
    570 +
    571 +### ADR-002: CSS Custom Properties for Theming
    572 +
    573 +**Decision**: Use CSS custom properties instead of class-based theming
    574 +
    575 +**Rationale**:
    576 +
    577 +- Runtime theme switching without reloading
    578 +- Easy custom theme creation
    579 +- Clean separation between structure and color
    580 +
    581 +**Trade-offs**:
    582 +
    583 +- ✅ Gains: Flexibility, performance, simplicity
    584 +- ❌ Loses: IE11 support (acceptable)
    585 +
    586 +---
    587 +
    588 +### ADR-003: CDN Dependencies
    589 +
    590 +**Decision**: Load libraries from CDN instead of bundling
    591 +
    592 +**Rationale**:
    593 +
    594 +- Keeps file size minimal
    595 +- Leverages browser caching across sites
    596 +- No build step required
    597 +- Easy version updates
    598 +
    599 +**Trade-offs**:
    600 +
    601 +- ✅ Gains: Simplicity, smaller files
    602 +- ❌ Loses: Guaranteed offline first-load
    603 +
    604 +---
    605 +
    606 +### ADR-004: localStorage for Persistence
    607 +
    608 +**Decision**: Use localStorage instead of IndexedDB or files
    609 +
    610 +**Rationale**:
    611 +
    612 +- Simple synchronous API
    613 +- Sufficient storage (5MB+)
    614 +- Universal browser support
    615 +- Perfect for text content
    616 +
    617 +**Trade-offs**:
    618 +
    619 +- ✅ Gains: Simplicity, reliability
    620 +- ❌ Loses: Large file support, structured querying
    621 +
    622 +---
    623 +
    624 +### ADR-005: Single File Architecture
    625 +
    626 +**Decision**: Keep HTML, CSS, JS separate but reference-minimal
    627 +
    628 +**Rationale**:
    629 +
    630 +- Clear separation of concerns
    631 +- Easy to understand and modify
    632 +- Standard web development practices
    633 +- Good for version control
    634 +
    635 +**Trade-offs**:
    636 +
    637 +- ✅ Gains: Maintainability, clarity
    638 +- ❌ Loses: Single-file portability (acceptable)
    639 +
    640 +## Code Quality Standards
    641 +
    642 +### Naming Conventions
    643 +
    644 +- **Variables**: camelCase (`themeSelector`, `markdownText`)
    645 +- **Functions**: camelCase with verb prefix (`renderMarkdown`, `changeTheme`)
    646 +- **CSS Classes**: kebab-case with component prefix (`.toolbar`, `.editor-container`)
    647 +- **CSS Variables**: kebab-case with double dash (`--bg-primary`, `--link-color`)
    648 +
    649 +### Function Design
    650 +
    651 +- **Single Responsibility**: Each function does one thing well
    652 +- **Maximum Length**: ~50 lines per function (guideline, not rule)
    653 +- **Maximum Complexity**: <10 cyclomatic complexity
    654 +- **Pure Functions**: Prefer pure functions where possible
    655 +- **Side Effects**: Document side effects in comments
    656 +
    657 +### Error Handling
    658 +
    659 +- **Try-Catch**: Wrap risky operations
    660 +- **User Feedback**: Display errors in UI where appropriate
    661 +- **Console Logging**: Always log errors for debugging
    662 +- **Graceful Degradation**: Continue operating despite errors
    663 +
    664 +### Documentation
    665 +
    666 +- **Inline Comments**: Explain "why" not "what"
    667 +- **Function Headers**: Describe purpose, params, returns
    668 +- **Complex Logic**: Extra comments for non-obvious code
    669 +- **ADRs**: Document architectural decisions
    670 +
    671 +## Testing Strategy
    672 +
    673 +### Current State
    674 +
    675 +**Manual Testing**: All testing done manually in browser
    676 +
    677 +**Test Coverage**:
    678 +
    679 +- ✅ Functional testing across browsers
    680 +- ✅ Theme switching validation
    681 +- ✅ Export functionality verification
    682 +- ✅ Markdown rendering accuracy
    683 +
    684 +### Future Testing Strategy
    685 +
    686 +**Unit Testing** (if implemented):
    687 +
    688 +- Markdown parsing accuracy
    689 +- Theme loading logic
    690 +- localStorage operations
    691 +- Export generation
    692 +
    693 +**Integration Testing**:
    694 +
    695 +- End-to-end user workflows
    696 +- Cross-browser compatibility
    697 +- Performance benchmarks
    698 +
    699 +**Acceptance Testing**:
    700 +
    701 +- User story validation
    702 +- Accessibility compliance
    703 +- Visual regression testing
    704 +
    705 +## Conclusion
    706 +
    707 +Markdown Viewer Pro's architecture prioritizes simplicity, maintainability, and user experience. The client-side monolithic design with strict separation of concerns enables rapid development while maintaining code quality. The modular theme system and clean data flow patterns ensure the application remains easy to understand, modify, and extend.
    708 +
    709 +Key architectural strengths:
    710 +
    711 +1. Zero backend complexity
    712 +2. Clear separation of concerns
    713 +3. Minimal dependencies
    714 +4. Graceful error handling
    715 +5. Performance-optimized rendering
    716 +
    717 +This architecture supports the product vision of providing an instant, beautiful, privacy-respecting markdown editing experience.
    718
